The identity stack is one decision with exactly two columns. There is no third.** The corpus decides it three times with incompatible answers; here it is reconciled:\n\n| | Column A — EVM | Column B — Cosmos/Ed25519 |\n|---|---|---|\n| Signature | secp256k1 ECDSA (EIP-155, EIP-2 low-s, ERC-2098) | Ed25519, **ZIP-215 semantics pinned as normative consensus text** |\n| Address | 20-byte hex | Bech32m (BIP-350), own HRP, 32-byte hash of a typed key envelope |\n| SLIP-44 | Reuse **60** — do not register a new one | Reuse **118** (Keplr recommends it for Ledger) |\n| Wallet on day 1 | MetaMask, free | Keplr-class, free; **no MetaMask** |\n| Hardware wallet | Free (existing Ethereum app) | 6–12 months + a Kudelski/Quarkslab audit + a Ledger Live commercial agreement |\n| Exchange deposit derivation | Watch-only xpub works (BIP-32) | **Broken.** SLIP-0010 ed25519 is hardened-only: *\"If curve is ed25519 or curve25519: return failure\"* on non-hardened derivation. Exchanges cannot derive fresh deposit addresses from an xpub |\n| Decimals | **18, `uint256`, no exceptions** | 6, u64 storage, u128 for every intermediate multiply |\n\nOn ZIP-215 specifically: the corpus asserts in bold \"verified 2026-08\" that `ed25519-dalek` documents no ZIP-215 path. **This is false** — dalek **3.0.0** (published 2026-07-06) states on `VerifyingKey::from_bytes`: *\"Verifies the point is valid under ZIP-215 rules.\"* Separate the two things: ZIP-215 **point decoding** (dalek 3.0.0 does this) from the ZIP-215 **cofactored verification equation** `[8][S]B = [8]R + [8][k]A` (the fork-relevant rule). Verify which your pinned crate implements, and correct the blueprint's mistake list — it says \"use `verify_strict()`\", which the crypto brief correctly identifies as *not* ZIP-215 and therefore a fork risk.\n\n**2. EVM-or-never is a genesis decision, and it drags decimals with it.** If EVM is possible in v1 *or ever*, take 18 decimals and 256-bit amounts at genesis. An 18-decimal EVM over a 6-decimal bank denom needs a conversion layer at every boundary, with truncation and rounding asymmetries — a repeatedly-exploited bug class on Cosmos EVM chains. Otherwise write \"no EVM, ever\" into the frozen-genesis list next to the address format.\n\n**3. On Cosmos, the minimum gas price is node-local, not consensus.** One operator running `minimum-gas-prices = 0` makes the chain free to spam, and none of the mempool eviction analysis binds. Decide at genesis: ship a consensus-enforced fee floor (feemarket/globalfee-class module) or write down that the floor is advisory. Then write the e2e test where one validator runs at zero and the network is flooded.\n\n**4. Cold start: how does the first user get gas?** No user can transact without your gas token, and your gas token exists only on your chain. Pick one mechanism *before* genesis — protocol-level fee grants for the first N transactions per address, or a gated mainnet claim funded from the community pool — and write the claim → canonical DEX pool → first CEX sequence with owners and dates. This is a month 5–6 wall that stops all usage regardless of how good the chain is.\n\n---\n\n## The decision tree\n\n```\nQ0. Deliverable: a 6-block reorg that leaves your UTXO set byte-identical to a genesis replay.\n2. **Weeks 7–12, Path 2.** Ship the ERC-20 + Permit, run the Trail of Bits integration checklist against yourself, initialize and seed the Uniswap v4 pool in one bundle (anyone can initialize your `PoolKey` at any price, so never leave the gap open), publish a canonical-contracts page.\n\n**Full-time (~480–520 hours).** Path 3 or a Path 4 *devnet* — not a mainnet:\n\n- OP Stack on Sepolia end to end (`make init` / `make setup` / `make up` around `op-deployer`, ~2–3 Sepolia ETH), or\n- `ignite scaffold chain --no-module` → re-pin go.mod → one module → 4-node local net → rehearse a real v1→v2 upgrade **before** genesis.\n\n**What does not fit in 3 months, at any intensity:** an L1 mainnet. The external lead times alone exceed the window — chainId PR (first PR wins the ID permanently), validator recruitment at 6–8 weeks, a 5-day gentx window, a 4-week public testnet, Safe's *monthly* batched registry releases, Chainlink and LayerZero at \"months\", and Circle's bridged-USDC standard which **\"must be incorporated prior to deploying… as it cannot be retroactively applied.\"**\n\n---\n\n## If you have 2 years\n\nAt 500 h/year that is 1,000 hours — still short of Path 7's floor. **Two years of full-time work for 2–3 people (≈4,000–12,000 h) is the first configuration where Path 7 is honest.** Assuming that:\n\n| When | Do it now because the lead time, not the work, is the constraint |\n|---|---|\n| **M0–M1** | Determinism seam (`Clock`/`Rng`/`Net`/`Storage` traits + `handle(Event) -> Vec<Action>`), canonical hand-written codec with a million-iteration property test, frozen domain-separation tag list. All three are unrecoverable-if-skipped. |\n| **M2** | **File the `ethereum-lists/chains` PR.** It needs only a `name` and a globally-unique `shortName`. First PR wins permanently; replacement PRs are closed. There is no reason this waits for T-24. |\n| **M2** | Get the POEM/FEMA opinion **before incorporating anything offshore** — an offshore entity run from India can be assessed as an Indian tax resident (~40% + surcharge on worldwide income), and the incorporation is itself an overseas investment requiring AD-bank routing. Both must clear before, not after. |\n| **M3** | Publish the Immunefi-style severity table. It is your threat model in a form researchers can act on, and it costs nothing. Credible band for a new chain: **$50k–$250k critical** (Cosmos and The Graph both cap at $50k; under $25k reads as \"we would rather not know\"). |\n| **M4–M6** | Reference-vs-production differential executor (a deliberately dumb `apply(prev_root, block) -> (new_root, receipts)` written from the spec text, run against every block). Deterministic simulator with `DST_SEED` printed as line 1. Both are the highest-leverage items available to a small team. |\n| **M6** | Decide the identity stack, EVM-or-never, decimals, fee floor and cold-start mechanism — all five together, in one document, frozen. |\n| **M8** | Calibrate the gas limit: measure p99 `apply_block` on your *minimum-spec* node at 100% adversarial blocks, set the limit so p99 execution ≤ 25% of the block interval, and alert on the ratio. CometBFT's `MaxGas = -1` default is a live DoS surface. |\n| **M9** | Ship the sentry topology as the *documented default* validator deployment (validator with `pex=false`, private peers, reachable only via sentries across ≥3 ASNs and ≥2 providers). Deriving the proposer schedule and DDoSing the next three proposers halts a 20-validator chain with a rented botnet and no stake. |\n| **M10–M12** | Start the **decentralisation ledger**: one CSV per month recording validator count and operator identity, voting-power concentration, foundation stake share, who can upgrade, who can halt, who runs RPC — with a retirement milestone per control. This is the cheapest artifact for both an exchange listing pack and a securities-classification opinion, and it cannot be reconstructed after the fact. |\n| **T-24 weeks** | Validator recruitment (15–30 professional operators; their calendars, not your code, are the long pole). Write the kill criteria now and read them at T+26. |\n| **T-12** | Set `snapshot-interval` explicitly. The default is `0` = disabled, the chain keeps producing blocks, dashboards stay green, and every prospective validator quietly gives up during genesis replay. And note `enterprise/poa` is a **Source Available Evaluation License**, not Apache-2.0.\n\n### Deliverables\n\n| # | Artifact | Detail |\n|---|---|---|\n| 3.1 | rust-libp2p 0.56.0, QUIC-first | ALPN `\"libp2p\"`, TLS 1.3, self-signed cert with OID `1.3.6.1.4.1.53594.1.1`. TCP fallback: `Noise_XX_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256` only. **Never offer mplex.** Yamux `/yamux/1.0.0` — raise the 256 KiB default window, or one stream caps near 3 MB/s at 80 ms RTT |\n| 3.2 | Override the five hostile defaults | `max_transmit_size = 65536` (your 2 MB block is silently unsendable), `mesh_n_low = 5` (spec says 4), `duplicate_cache_time`, `heartbeat_interval`, and the default message-id of `base58(peer_id) ‖ seqno` — the duplicate-storm bug |\n| 3.3 | Ethereum's gossipsub params | D=8, D_low=6, D_high=12, D_lazy=6, heartbeat 0.7 s, mcache_len 6, `seen_ttl` above your block time. v1.1: `D_out = 2` with `D_out < D_low` and `D_out ≤ D/2` — a real anti-eclipse mechanism. Wire your signature verifier to the **P₄ invalid-message score component**: cheapest DoS defence you will ever install |\n| 3.4 | **Fork digest in every topic string and in the handshake** | `/mychain/<fork_digest>/<name>/<encoding>`. Plus a **dual-subscribe window of N blocks before activation**, unsubscribe after. Without this, upgraded and non-upgraded nodes share one mesh at the activation height, propagate mutually invalid blocks, score each other down via P₄, and partition non-deterministically |\n| 3.5 | Address book, ported from Bitcoin | 1024 new / 256 tried buckets, size 64, `SET_TRIED_COLLISION_SIZE = 10`, HORIZON 30d, RETRIES 3, MAX_FAILURES 10, MIN_FAIL 7d. Bucket by `GetGroup(src)` = **/16 or ASN, not IP**. Note Bitcoin Core no longer has a numeric ban score — misbehaviour is binary discouragement; do not build accumulating ban points |\n| 3.6 | **Sentry topology as the default validator deployment** | Validator with `pex = false`, `private_peer_ids` set, **no public P2P address**, reachable only via sentries across ≥3 ASNs and ≥2 providers. Publish a reference compose/terraform. On a 20-validator chain, deriving the proposer schedule and DDoSing each upcoming proposer is a chain halt achievable with a rented botnet and zero stake |\n| 3.7 | Slashing, tuned for reality | `SignedBlocksWindow` **10,000** not 100 (100 blocks ≈ 60 s jails you during a rolling upgrade). `SlashFractionDowntime` **0.0001** not 0.01. `SlashFractionDoubleSign` **0.20–0.30** not 0.05. Copy Ethereum's asymmetry: Electra cut `MIN_SLASHING_PENALTY_QUOTIENT` from **32 (Bellatrix) → 4096** so an honest operator accident costs ~0.02%, while the correlated term still burns ~everything for a coordinated 1/3 |\n| 3.8 | Hard invariant | `checkpoint_interval < evidence_max_age < unbonding_time`. Enforced by nothing in the software. `max_evidence_age < unbonding_time` is a live exit-scam window |\n| 3.9 | Set the two defaults that are booby-trapped | `ConsensusParams.Block.MaxGas = -1` is **unbounded** — set it from your Phase 2 calibration. `snapshot-interval = 0` **disables state sync entirely** — the chain keeps producing blocks, dashboards stay green, and every prospective validator quietly gives up during genesis replay |\n| 3.10 | Fenced signer | fsync'd `(height, round, step)` high-water mark held **outside** the node's lifecycle, exclusive-locked, documented as \"must never be restored from backup.\" tmkms's own warning: \"there is presently no double signing defense in the case that multiple KMS instances are running simultaneously\" |\n| 3.11 | Deterministic simulator | ~600 lines: `BinaryHeap<(virtual_time_ns, seq, Event)>`, seeded ChaCha8, link matrix, invariant checker after every event. Print `DST_SEED=<n>` first; append failures to `tests/seeds/regressions.txt`; CI replays them |\n| 3.12 | Versioned snapshot format | Gate restore on the version. A pre-upgrade snapshot that no longer restores post-upgrade silently breaks all new-node onboarding at every fork |\n\n### Definition of done — run these\n\n```bash\ndocker compose -f e2e/4val.yml up -d\n./e2e/run.sh --stages setup,start,load,perturb,wait,test\n./e2e/run.sh --perturb kill-1     # chain continues\n./e2e/run.sh --perturb kill-2     # chain HALTS — and you can state why 3-of-4 quorum fails\n./e2e/run.sh --perturb double-signing\nchaind query slashing signing-infos | jq '.info[] | select(.tombstoned==true)'\n./e2e/run.sh --scenario ddos-next-3-proposers      # sentries hold; no halt\n./e2e/run.sh --scenario mixed-version-across-activation   # node type `upgrade`, not a binary swap\nLD_PRELOAD=libfaketime.so.1 FAKETIME=\"+7s\" ./e2e/run.sh --scenario skew-across-fork-height\niptables -A INPUT -s <peer> -j DROP                # asymmetric partition, not just docker disconnect\ncargo test -p sim -- --seeds 10000                 # nightly; 3 seeds per PR\n./scripts/coldjoin.sh --from-published-docs        # weekly in CI, alert on failure\n./scripts/snapshot_version_gate.sh                 # pre-upgrade snapshot rejected, never silently accepted\n```\n\n**Demo.** Four nodes across three ASNs. Partition them, heal them, kill a proposer, double-sign one and watch the tombstone appear on the explorer, then state-sync a fifth node from a published snapshot in under ten minutes. Then show the simulator finding a liveness bug from a printed seed and replaying it in under a second.\n\n**Deliberately do NOT yet.** No bridge (Ronin $624M, Poly $611M, BNB $586M, Wormhole $326M, Bybit **$1,436,173,027** — and Wormhole runs 19 Guardians with 29 third-party audits; that is the resourcing level of the *hacked* systems). No IBC. No public testnet. No token. No DAG mempool, no sharding, no Block-STM. **Leave vote extensions disabled at genesis** (`VoteExtensionsEnableHeight: 0`) and enable at a scheduled height — `VerifyVoteExtension` MUST be deterministic and a bug there halts the chain.\n\n**Read first.** `p2p-networking` (all) → `consensus-pos-bft` (all) → `from-scratch-blueprint` M7–M10 → `testing-ops-upgrades` (all) → `security-attacks` §2.\n\n**Time discipline starts here.** One mandated time source (chrony), a documented max drift, and an alert on it. Write the block-timestamp validity predicate into the chain spec as normative text. Timestamp-activated forks plus validator clock skew means validators cross the activation boundary at different wall-clock moments — that is what scenario `skew-across-fork-height` exists to catch.\n\n---\n\n## Phase 4 — Public testnet\n\n**Goal.** Other people run your software, and the ecosystem surface — 30–40% of all remaining effort — actually exists.\n\n**Duration.** 280–420 h.\n\n### Deliverables\n\n| Track | Artifact | Detail |\n|---|---|---|\n| RPC | Method-aware proxy | Never expose the node. Batch ≤ **50** (geth's default 1000 is reckless; CometBFT's is 10), body ≤ 1 MiB, `eth_getLogs` ≤ 10,000 blocks and ≤ 10,000 results rejected with `-32005` **naming the limit**, WS ≤ 5 subs/conn and ≤ 900 conns. Block `engine_*`, `admin_*`, `personal_*`, `miner_*`. Engine API on its own port, JWT HS256, `iat` within ±60 s — run chrony or the head stalls with no useful log line |\n| Explorer | Blockscout in production | Size the DB from **Blockscout's own numbers**, not your node's disk: Ethereum 21,000 GiB, **Sepolia — a testnet — 5,200 GiB**. `db_storage` on AWS \"can only be adjusted 1 time in a 24 hour period\" |\n| Indexer | Ponder live the week testnet opens | `eth_getLogs` cannot answer \"all transactions for address X\", \"top 100 holders\", or \"TVL over time\" |\n| Wallet UX | Fee guidance doc + replace/cancel + stuck-nonce runbook | Ship **before** the first congestion event, not after. `eth_estimateGas` failure modes (binary search, the 63/64 rule, state-dependent reverts) documented |\n| Predeploy | Multicall3 at `0xcA11bde05977b3631167028862bE2a173976CA11` | It is **not** CREATE2 — a presigned tx from `0x05f32b3c…` costing exactly **872,776 gas**. If your gas schedule differs at all, the presigned tx fails and you must predeploy it in genesis. viem and wagmi batch every multi-read through it |\n| Faucet | Geoblocking on the **first deployed page** | Plus: test tokens have no monetary value, are not offered for sale, may be reset. That wording is what keeps them outside India's s.2(47A) \"representation of having inherent value\" |\n| Fee floor | Decide: consensus rule or operator config | On a Cosmos-shaped stack the minimum gas price is **node-local**, so one operator running at zero makes the chain free to spam and none of your mempool-eviction analysis binds. Ship a feemarket/globalfee-class module or write down that the floor is advisory |\n| Community | Canonical-contracts + verified-links page, impersonation playbook, status page, three incident templates (halt / exploit / scheduled fork), named comms owner | Written while nothing is on fire. The scam wave arrives in week 1 of any public testnet: fake token contracts, fake claim sites, fake support DMs, fake validator recruitment |\n| Policy | **Published transaction-inclusion policy** | You will operate the canonical public RPC and most of the validator set. Does that RPC screen OFAC-listed addresses? Does your default builder censor? \"No\" is defensible with consequences; \"yes\" is a centralisation property you must disclose. Set RPC log retention and minimisation at the same time |\n| Economics | Validator P&L in fiat, before recruitment | $200–400/mo × N validators × 12 = **$50–100k/year of hard fiat** against a token with no float and no reliable price. Write a 12-month subsidy budget. Tie a criterion to it: \"if we cannot fund N validators for 18 months, launch with N/2 and say so.\" Exit is not gradual degradation on a BFT chain — it is a halt the moment >1/3 leave |\n| Record | Decentralisation ledger, monthly CSV, from block 1 | Validator count and operator identity, Nakamoto coefficient / HHI, foundation stake share, who can upgrade, who can halt, who runs RPC — each with a defined retirement milestone. One CSV a month; the cheapest artifact for both a listing pack and a classification opinion |\n| Aggregators | Circulating-supply attestation endpoint | CoinGecko and CMC require it. It is an engineering deliverable derived from your protocol-level vesting accounts, not a BD task |\n\n### Alerts — the six, plus two the corpus omits\n\n`time() - last_block_timestamp > 3× block time` · `p2p_peers < 3` for 5m · `consensus_rounds > 0` for 2m · validator missing from last 50 blocks · disk < 20% · RPC p99 > 2s for 10m · **`apply_block_duration_seconds / block_interval > 0.25`** · **snapshot age and `trust_hash` staleness**. Plus a second Grafana dashboard for economics and decentralisation: page on any single operator crossing **1/3** (unilateral halt capability) or top-3 crossing **2/3** (unilateral finality), realised vs modelled inflation, and the kill-criteria metrics wired in so the T+26 review reads a number.\n\n### Definition of done — run these\n\n```bash\ncurl -s https://rpc.testnet.example -d '{\"method\":\"eth_chainId\",\"id\":1,\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\"}' \\\n  | jq -r .result                        # matches your merged ethereum-lists PR\ntime ./scripts/newcomer_flow.sh          # addEthereumChain → faucet → send → explorer, target < 5 min\n./scripts/coldjoin.sh --fresh-vm         # weekly in CI\n./e2e/run.sh --scenario zero-min-gas-price-operator --flood\n                                         # asserts your fee-floor invariant actually binds\ncurl -s https://api.example/v1/supply/circulating | jq -e 'type == \"number\"'\nchaind query gov proposals               # a real param change passed on testnet\ncosmovisor / ./scripts/upgrade_rehearsal.sh --height <H>   # full binary upgrade, real validator set\n```\n\nThe testnet runs **four weeks** with the real validator set and deliberately induces: downtime jailing, one double-sign, a param change, and a full upgrade. Recruit operators **6–8 weeks ahead** — their calendars, not your code, are the long pole.\n\n**Demo.** Hand someone the docs URL and nothing else. They run a validator, join via state sync, and produce a block within 30 minutes.\n\n**Deliberately do NOT yet.** No mainnet date announced. **No listing announcement of any kind** — one \"listing soon\" tweet from one team member retroactively voids MiCA Art. 4(2) via Art. 4(3), on an offer you believed exempt. No token sale, ever. No bridge. No mainnet genesis file.\n\n**Read first.** `launch-operations` (all) → `node-apis-tooling` §4–6 → `legal-compliance` Phase 1 → `testing-ops-upgrades` §monitoring → `tokenomics` §3, §6.\n\n---\n\n## Phase 5 — The security gate\n\n**Goal.** A gate, not a phase. Nothing proceeds until every row is green. Shortening this is the decision that ends chains.\n\n**Duration.** 200–320 h of your time, plus external money and 8–16 weeks of auditor calendar.\n\n### Deliverables\n\n| # | Artifact | Detail |\n|---|---|---|\n| 5.1 | **Reference-vs-production differential executor** | The single highest-value item available to a solo builder. A deliberately dumb `apply(prev_root, block_bytes) -> (new_root, receipts)` written *from the spec text* with a BTreeMap and no caching, run against every fixture, fuzz input and simulated block, asserting identical roots **and error codes**. ~2 weeks. This is what goevmlab's trophy list (Nethermind BLS gas #2208, Geth BLS gas #21253, Besu EIP-2929 #1468) actually catches; a single implementation is its own spec and cannot find these |\n| 5.2 | Fuzzing | `cargo fuzz`, 4 CPU-h per target nightly, on the decoder and `apply_tx`. **Recursion depth cap and `MAX_LEN` checked before allocation** — Cosmos ASA-2024-0012 (deeply-nested packet → stack overflow → network halt, CWE-674) and ASA-2024-0013 (nested `UnpackAny` → exponential CPU/memory, bypassing `max_tx_bytes`, CWE-400) are both High and both recent |\n| 5.3 | Model checking | `quint verify spec.qnt --invariant=no_conflicting_finality` (JDK ≥17). 2–4 weeks |\n| 5.4 | **Tokenomics parameter simulation** | The one subsystem you can never refactor, and the only one with no testing story anywhere in the corpus. A few hundred lines exercising: staking ratio under price shocks, an unbonding wave against the 21-day queue and `max_entries = 7`, and governance outcomes at your stated quorum/veto with realistic participation. Run it **before** the parameters go into genesis |\n| 5.5 | Two audits, two firms | Not one firm at twice the size — auditors have correlated blind spots. Budget a remediation re-audit pass. **Audit pricing is unverified in this corpus; get three written quotes, do not plan from a blog number** |\n| 5.6 | Bug bounty published **before** the audit | Immunefi blockchain/DLT scale v2.3. Credible band for a new chain is **$50k–$250k max** (Cosmos and The Graph both cap at $50k; ENS and SSV at $250k). Under $25k reads as \"we would rather not know.\" Publishing the severity table *is* publishing your threat model in a form researchers can act on |\n| 5.7 | Reproducible builds | Guix-style `./contrib/guix/guix-build` → `guix-attest` → `guix-verify` against a second independent builder. SLSA Build **L2** minimum: dedicated infrastructure, provenance tied to it by signature |\n| 5.8 | Validator deployment doc | Name the Kubernetes anti-patterns explicitly: **never a Deployment, never `replicas > 1`, never a rolling strategy, never an HPA.** Single-replica StatefulSet plus the fenced signer. The 2019 double-sign mechanism was restoring `priv_validator_state.json` from backup; the 2026 mechanism is a rolling update briefly overlapping two pods with one key. Add \"signer unreachable\", \"signer added latency\", and \"two pods, one key\" to the fault taxonomy |\n| 5.9 | Consensus key rotation | Decide at genesis whether it exists. Document the procedure and its cost. Rehearse \"validator key compromised but not yet used to double-sign, rotate under time pressure\" alongside halt-and-restart |\n| 5.10 | Legal, in writing, before genesis | (a) CA opinion on receipt-vs-transfer taxation of block rewards; (b) counsel opinion on PMLA s.2(1)(sa) scope; (c) **POEM/FEMA clearance before any offshore incorporation, not after** — the offshore entity can be assessed as an Indian tax resident and the incorporation is itself an overseas investment requiring AD-bank routing; (d) **claim-side sanctions screening decided before the Merkle root is published** — it cannot be retrofitted onto a published root |\n| 5.11 | Emergency response, rehearsed | (a) automatic halt on internal invariant violation — supply ≠ Σ balances → **stop, do not continue**; (b) a circuit breaker disabling *specific message types* (`x/circuit`'s `MsgTripCircuitBreaker{authority, msg_type_urls}` is the model); (c) a halt-and-restart runbook with out-of-band comms. **Explicitly do not ship arbitrary state-edit authority** |\n| 5.12 | Kill criteria, written and wired | Active addresses, non-validator transaction count, TVL, validator count. Read at T+26 as numbers, not a vibe |\n\n### Definition of done — run these\n\n```bash\ncargo fuzz run decode -- -runs=100000000            # zero crashes; corpus committed\ncargo fuzz run apply_tx -- -runs=100000000\n./scripts/differential.sh --blocks 100000           # roots AND error codes identical, every block\nquint verify spec.qnt --invariant=no_conflicting_finality\ncargo run --bin paramsim -- --scenario price-shock,unbonding-wave,gov-capture\n./contrib/guix/guix-verify --sigs ../second-builder-sigs   # byte-identical\n./scripts/halt_drill.sh --record-wallclock          # panic → resumed production, timed vs published RTO\ngh api repos/$ORG/$REPO/security-advisories         # 0 unresolved Critical/High\n```\n\n**Demo.** Publish the two audit reports, the differential harness, the fuzz corpus, the parameter simulation output, and the halt-drill timing as one package. That package is exactly what an exchange listing committee and a token-classification opinion both read.\n\n**Rule one for a real halt, learned the expensive way.** Do not run any reset command. Copy `data/` and the consensus WAL from ≥3 nodes — **including one that disagreed** — to cold storage first. Default to forward-only recovery (patch, resume from halt height, no state change). Recovery time is dominated by coordination, not by the patch: decide in advance who declares an incident, where the war room is, and what quorum authorises a restart. Note Base's June 2026 halt landed on the day of a scheduled hardfork — precisely when your fork-activation path is least exercised and you are most fatigued.\n\n**Read first.** `security-attacks` (all) → `testing-ops-upgrades` §upgrades and §incidents → `legal-compliance` (all) → `tokenomics` §5–7.\n\n---\n\n## Phase 6 — Genesis, cold start, mainnet\n\n**Goal.** A live network with users who are not you, and a first rehearsed upgrade behind you within 90 days.\n\n**Duration.** 160–260 h, then **$465–$1,600/month forever** plus on-call.\n\n### Deliverables\n\n| # | Artifact | Detail |\n|---|---|---|\n| 6.1 | Genesis ceremony | 5-day gentx window; `genesis_time` ≥ 48 h out; publish `genesis.json` **with its SHA-256** and require every operator to echo their own `sha256sum` in the operator channel. **Never publish a second hash.** Accepting one late gentx and re-running `collect-gentxs` puts two hashes in circulation and forks you at height 1. Once the hash is out, the window is closed — launch without that validator |\n| 6.2 | Genesis size, measured | **Prefer claim-on-demand against a Merkle root committed in genesis over a large alloc.** A 10k–100k-account alloc makes producing exactly one hash harder, not easier, and nobody sanely sha256's a 100 MB file by hand. Boot a genesis with the real intended account count in CI and record `InitChain` wall-clock and file size **before** the ceremony window opens |\n| 6.3 | **Cold start — pick one before genesis** | No user can transact without your gas token, and your gas token exists only on your chain. This is the month 5–6 wall that stops all usage regardless of how good the chain is. Either protocol-level fee grants / sponsorship for the first N transactions per address, or a gated mainnet claim funded from the community pool. Then write the sequence **claim → canonical DEX pool → first CEX** with owners and dates, checked against \"never take consideration\" |\n| 6.4 | Exchange & custodian integration guide | Finality rule and required confirmations, required RPC methods, address derivation and whether watch-only xpub works, reorg policy, dust threshold, sample deposit-detection pseudocode. **Dry-run against one real custodian's checklist before mainnet.** (If you took trunk P, this is where the 100-block reorg cap becomes their deposit double-credit problem, and they will say no) |\n| 6.5 | Liquidity, if any | Never announce a token before its canonical pool exists. Uniswap v4 `PoolKey{currency0, currency1, fee, tickSpacing, hooks}` requires `uint160(currency0) < uint160(currency1)`; `sqrtPriceX96` for 1:1 is `79228162514264337593543950336`. **Anyone can initialize a pool for your key at any price** — initialize and seed in one `multicall` bundle. Launch with `hooks: IHooks(address(0))` |\n| 6.6 | Interop, if IBC | The parameter coupling is one inequality, not three settings: **the counterparty light client's trusting period must sit inside your unbonding period**, which couples directly to `unbonding_time` / `max_evidence_age` / `checkpoint_interval`. Relayer gas is a recurring operating cost with a named owner. And write the runbook with the longest tail: **a halt lasting longer than the trusting period expires your light client on every counterparty chain, and recovery is a governance action on *their* chain, not yours** |\n| 6.7 | Treasury | Safe 3-of-5 on Ethereum mainnet, hardware wallets from three vendors, geographically split, one non-employee signer. Do not secure your operating capital with the least-audited chain in existence — your own |\n| 6.8 | First rehearsed upgrade within 90 days | Fork-boundary semantics beyond the STF: **revalidate the whole mempool at activation and drop with a distinguishable error, never silently**; pending fee caps invalidated by a gas-schedule change; and a separate go/no-go for the explorer, indexer, public RPC, snapshot servers and wallet fee estimation. Cancel the plan if voting power on the target binary is < 2/3 with six hours to go — cancelling is cheap |\n\n### Definition of done — run these\n\n```bash\nsha256sum genesis.json                     # echoed identically by ≥2/3 of the gentx set, publicly\nchaind status | jq -r .SyncInfo.latest_block_height    # block 1 within 60s of genesis_time\ntime ./scripts/stranger_join.sh            # published docs only, state sync, target ≤ 15 min\nchaind query bank balances <first-real-user>           # paid for by a mechanism that predates genesis\ncurl -s https://api.example/v1/supply/circulating\n./scripts/decentralisation_ledger.sh --month $(date +%Y-%m) >> ledger.csv\n./scripts/upgrade_rehearsal.sh --mainnet --height <H>  # T+90\n```\n\n**Demo.** Thirty days running with nothing but on-call, one monthly decentralisation-ledger CSV, one completed upgrade, and a T+26 review that reads the kill-criteria dashboard.\n\n**Still deliberately do NOT.** No bridge. No governance-controlled mint. No arbitrary state-edit authority. No token sale — fund development with equity or a SAFE into a company. No BUSL on the node (the moat expires in four years and meanwhile no exchange, RPC provider or institutional validator wants a licence question in their infra review; Apache-2.0 for its express patent grant).\n\n**Read first.** `launch-operations` §genesis and §cost → `legal-compliance` Phase 2–3 → `tokenomics` §3 → `node-apis-tooling` §registries.\n\n---\n\n## The parallel clock — long-lead items pinned to earliest start, not to when they're needed\n\nFour independent clocks exist in the corpus and none references the others. This is the merge. Every item is placed at the **earliest date it can start**, with the blocking prerequisite named.\n\n| Item | Real lead time | Start at | Only needs | Cost of starting late |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| **chainId PR** (`ethereum-lists/chains`) | days to merge, **permanent** | **Phase 2** | a name + a globally unique `shortName` | First PR wins the ID; replacement PRs are closed |\n| **POEM / FEMA opinion** | weeks–months | **Phase 0** | your residence and intent | Must clear *before* you incorporate anything offshore. After is unfixable |\n| Validator recruitment | **6–8 weeks** | Phase 4 minus 8 wk | a testnet that actually joins | Their calendars are the long pole, not your code |\n| PMLA s.2(1)(sa) scope opinion | weeks | Phase 4 | your distribution design | Determines whether FIU-IND registration is even in scope. Do not register pre-emptively |\n| Two audits + remediation | **8–16 weeks** | Phase 4 end | frozen scope | Auditors book out; the remediation pass is a second slot |\n| Claim-side screening decision | — | **before the Merkle root** | counsel | Cannot be retrofitted onto a published root |\n| **Circle bridged USDC standard** | before deploy, **irreversible** | Phase 5 | a bridge decision | \"Must be incorporated prior to deploying… cannot be retroactively applied.\" And Circle is under no obligation to upgrade bridged → native |\n| Safe deployment | **monthly** batched npm release | Phase 5 | chainId + singleton factory | One missed batch is a month |\n| Chainlink (push) | **months** + commercial + node-operator subsidy | Phase 4 | a budget | It is BD, not an integration. Pyth (pull) is days–weeks and is the pragmatic first oracle |\n| LayerZero V2 | **months** | Phase 5 | EndpointV2 / SendUln302 / ReceiveUln302 / Executor + explicit DVN config | EIDs are 30xxx mainnet / 40xxx testnet, unrelated to chainId |\n| Ledger device app *(column B only)* | **6–12 months** + third-party audit + a separate Ledger Live agreement | Phase 3 | Rust (C is maintenance-only) | This line item alone can justify identity column A |\n\n---\n\n## The decisions frozen at genesis\n\nEach of these is a hard fork or a full user migration to change. Write them into `DECISIONS.md` in Phase 0 and treat edits as amendments.\n\n1. Trunk (R / C / P / L). 2. Identity column (A / B) — signature scheme, address format, coin type, and every downstream integration. 3. **Decimals and integer width** — 18/uint256 if EVM is possible in v1 *or ever*; otherwise 6/u64 **plus \"no EVM, ever\" written down**. 4. The complete domain-separation tag list. 5. Canonical encoding (Borsh in Rust; RLP if EVM-equivalent). 6. Hash function inside the state commitment tree (EIP-7864's own note: \"the hash function used in the current draft is not final\" — pick Poseidon2 if you may ever SNARK your STF, BLAKE3 if not). 7. Chain ID, inside the sighash from block zero. 8. Account struct shape (`code_hash` / `storage_root` present or absent). 9. Whether the fee floor is a consensus rule or operator config. 10. Whether consensus key rotation exists. 11. Emission curve shape (only the parameters should be governable). 12. `unbonding_time` / `max_evidence_age` / `checkpoint_interval` ordering. 13. Fork-activation mechanism — **timestamp-based only**. 14. Whether a bridge or an EVM is possible later at all.\n\n---\n\n## Where a framework becomes the right call — ranked\n\n| Trigger | Do this |\n|---|---|\n| You cannot name a transaction users can't do on Base today | Stop at Phase 0. Ship an ERC-20. An afternoon, $0/mo |\n| You want Solidity + Ethereum liquidity but not a monetary policy | Stop at Phase 2. OP Stack (MIT) self-hosted (~1.5 FTE forever, ~14 ETH in proposal bonds), or a managed rollup at ~$3k/mo **+ 5% sequencer profit** |\n| **You reach Phase 3 and are about to write vote gossip, evidence gossip, block sync and a light client** | **Adopt CometBFT v0.38.26 or Malachite. This is the single largest correct off-ramp in the roadmap: 400–700 hours** |\n| You are also about to write staking, slashing, governance, vesting and an upgrade path | Take trunk C: Cosmos SDK **v0.54.4** + CometBFT v0.39.4. Accept the identity column flip, or take `cosmos/evm` (pins SDK v0.54.3) to keep column A |\n| You reach Phase 5 and cannot fund two audits | You are not ready for mainnet. Stay on testnet, or ship on someone else's security |\n| You reach Phase 6 and cannot fund N validators for 18 months in fiat | Launch with N/2 and say so publicly, or do not launch |\n\nWriting your own consensus is a legitimate *study* exercise, and it belongs in a scratch repo alongside Phase 3. It does not belong in the binary that holds other people's money.\n\n---\n\n## Corpus corrections applied in this roadmap\n\nThe research corpus is unusually well-sourced, and it is wrong in specific, checkable places. Every version carries an as-of date and a decay class (**F** = re-verify before you type it, **S** = stable for years). The trunk (freeze this before commit 1)\n\nThe corpus contains four mutually exclusive top-level recommendations. This document picks one and kills the other three. It is one decision, and it cascades into six budget lines.\n\n| Consequence | **Column A (chosen)** | Column B |\n|---|---|---|\n| Curve / sighash | secp256k1, EIP-155 + EIP-2 low-s | Ed25519, ZIP-215 |\n| Address | `last20(keccak256(pubkey_uncompressed[1..]))`, EIP-55 checksum hex | Bech32m, own HRP, 32-byte hash |\n| HD path | BIP-32 + BIP-44, `m/44'/60'/0'/0/i` — **watch-only xpub works** | SLIP-0010, hardened-only — **xpub deposit derivation impossible** |\n| Wallet on day 1 | MetaMask/Rabby via `wallet_addEthereumChain`, $0 | Keplr-class, needs a chain-registry PR + suggest-chain flow |\n| Hardware wallet | Ledger's existing Ethereum app, $0 | New Ledger device app: **Rust mandatory, third-party audit by Kudelski/Quarkslab, 6–12 months, real money** |\n| Exchange deposits | Standard xpub sweep; every custodian has code for it | Custom derivation; some custodians will decline |\n| Explorer/indexer | Blockscout fork, Ponder, graph-node all work unmodified | Fork all three |\n| Tooling | Foundry, Hardhat, viem/ethers unmodified | Four SDKs you write |\n\nColumn A also fixes your transaction wire format: **EIP-2718 typed envelope, type `0x02` (dynamic fee), RLP-encoded, exactly as Ethereum**. That is the price of MetaMask signing natively. Do not invent a codec on the signed path.\n\n### 0.2 Frozen-at-genesis list (unchangeable without a coordinated hard fork or a new chain)\n\n`CHAIN_ID` · address derivation · signature scheme and the accept-set predicate · tx type set and RLP field order · sighash preimage · header field list and RLP order · merkle leaf/node domain tags · state-key derivation (`keccak(addr)`) · state commitment hash function · decimals · `GAS_PER_BYTE` deposit constant · genesis hash · SLIP-44 coin type · snapshot format version 1.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Repository layout — Rust (reference implementation)\n\nDependency arrows point one way. **`consensus` must never depend on `executor`, `state`, or `storage`.** If it needs to, the ABCI seam is broken.\n\n```\ntypes → codec → crypto → storage → trie → state → executor → mempool\n                     ↘ consensus (types + crypto ONLY)\n                     ↘ p2p → sync → rpc → node → bin/myl1\n```\n\n```\nmyl1/\n├── Cargo.toml                 # [workspace] resolver=\"2\", edition=\"2024\", rust-version=\"1.95\"\n├── rust-toolchain.toml        # channel = \"1.95.0\"  (exact; not \"stable\")\n├── clippy.toml                # determinism gate, see §6\n├── deny.toml                  # cargo-deny: advisories, licenses, bans, duplicate-crate check\n├── crates/\n│   ├── types/                 # Header, Block, SignedTx, Receipt, Account, ForkSpec, StfError\n│   ├── codec/                 # RLP, typed envelope, domain tags, canonical-form property tests\n│   ├── crypto/                # Signer trait, recover, keccak, merkle (RFC-6962 shape), keystore\n│   ├── storage/               # redb tables, ONE write txn per block, changesets, reorg journal\n│   ├── trie/                  # StateCommitment trait; v1 sorted binary Merkle; v2 vendored JMT\n│   ├── state/                 # StateStore: snapshot / stage / commit / prove; WorkingSet journal\n│   ├── executor/              # BlockExecutor; native handlers; `evm` feature -> revm\n│   ├── executor-ref/          # deliberately naive STF (BTreeMap, no cache) — differential oracle\n│   ├── mempool/               # TxPool\n│   ├── consensus/             # sans-I/O: step(Input) -> Vec<Effect>. Repository layout — TypeScript\n\nBe honest about the role. A second *full* node in TS costs 8–12 additional person-weeks; its payoff is that it is a genuine differential oracle (a single implementation is its own spec and cannot find the CVE-2020-26241 bug class). If you cannot afford that, build `packages/{types,codec,crypto,light,sdk}` + `apps/indexer` only and skip `executor/consensus/p2p`.\n\n```\nmyl1-ts/\n├── package.json               # pnpm workspace, \"type\":\"module\", packageManager pinned w/ hash\n├── tsconfig.base.json         # strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes,\n│                              # useUnknownInCatchVariables, project references\n├── packages/\n│   ├── types/                 # all amounts bigint; branded types for Address/B256\n│   ├── codec/                 # RLP + typed envelope; MUST byte-match the Rust codec\n│   ├── crypto/                # @noble/curves wrappers, keccak, merkle, keystore v3\n│   ├── storage/               # classic-level, same key prefixes as Rust (§4)\n│   ├── trie/  state/  executor/  executor-ref/  mempool/  consensus/  p2p/  sync/  rpc/\n│   ├── light/                 # header chain + Merkle proof verifier; browser-safe, no node: imports\n│   ├── sdk/                   # tx build/sign/send, fee oracle client, nonce manager, replace/cancel\n│   └── conformance/           # ONE suite, run against BOTH implementations in CI\n├── apps/\n│   ├── node/                  # full node (optional, see above)\n│   ├── cli/                   # commander\n│   ├── indexer/               # Ponder-shaped; owns the address/tx/holder tables RPC cannot answer\n│   └── faucet/                # geoblock + rate limit from the first deployed page\n└── test/{vectors,e2e}\n```\n\n**TS-specific ceilings.** 1,000 secp256k1 verifications at ~60 µs is a 60 ms event-loop stall — past your propose timeout budget (§7). Core interfaces (actual code)\n\n### 3.1 Types (Rust)\n\n```rust\n// crates/types/src/block.rs\npub type Address = alloy_primitives::Address;   // 20 bytes\npub type B256    = alloy_primitives::B256;\npub type U256    = alloy_primitives::U256;\n\n/// RLP field order is FROZEN. Appending is a hard fork; reordering is a new chain.\n#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, RlpEncodable, RlpDecodable)]\npub struct Header {\n    pub parent_hash:   B256,\n    pub height:        u64,\n    pub timestamp_ms:  u64,     // NEVER u32 seconds — Bitcoin's field overflows in 2106\n    pub state_root:    B256,    // POST-state of THIS block (see §3.6 hazard)\n    pub transactions_root: B256,\n keccak256(0x02 || rlp(payload_without_signature))\n    pub fn sighash(&self) -> B256 { .. }\n    /// hash = keccak256(0x02 || rlp(payload_with_signature))\n    pub fn hash(&self) -> B256 { .. }\n}\n\npub struct Receipt {\n    pub tx_type: u8, pub success: bool,\n    pub cumulative_gas_used: u64, pub logs: Vec<Log>,\n}\n\npub struct BlockCtx {\n    pub height: u64, pub timestamp_ms: u64, pub proposer: Address,\n    pub base_fee_per_gas: u128, pub gas_limit: u64,\n    pub randomness: B256, pub fork: ForkId,\n}\n\npub enum Activation { ByTimestampMs(u64) }   // never by height — height drifts with block time\npub struct ForkSpec {\n    pub id: ForkId, pub name: &'static str, pub activation: Activation,\n    pub tx_types: &'static [u8], pub gas_schedule: &'static GasSchedule,\n    pub max_block_bytes: usize, pub gas_limit_max: u64,\n}\npub const FORKS: &[ForkSpec] = &[ /* genesis, fork1, ... ascending */ ];\n```\n\n### 3.2 StateDB / StateStore\n\nThe load-bearing split is **`stage` (pure, returns a root, writes nothing) vs `commit` (writes, only after consensus decides)**. Fusing them means a rejected proposal poisons the database unrecoverably.\n\n```rust\n// crates/state/src/lib.rs\npub trait StateDB {\n    type Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + 'static;\n    fn basic(&self, addr: Address)                -> Result<Option<Account>, Self::Error>;\n    fn code_by_hash(&self, h: B256)               -> Result<Option<Bytes>,  Self::Error>;\n    fn storage(&self, addr: Address, key: U256)   -> Result<U256,           Self::Error>;\n    fn block_hash(&self, height: u64)             -> Result<B256,           Self::Error>;\n}\n\n/// Opaque, fully computed, not yet durable. Cheap to drop.\npub struct Staged { pub root: B256, pub(crate) batch: WriteBatch, pub(crate) height: u64 }\n\npub trait StateStore: Send + Sync + 'static {\n    type View<'a>: StateDB where Self: 'a;\n\n    fn view_at(&self, root: B256) -> Result<Self::View<'_>, StoreError>;\n    fn head(&self) -> (u64, B256);                       // (height, block_hash)\n    fn finalized(&self) -> (u64, B256);\n\n    /// PURE. Same input -> byte-identical root, zero disk writes. Callable on a proposal\n    /// you are about to reject. Deterministic across x86-64 and aarch64.\n    fn stage(&self, base: B256, changes: StateChanges) -> Result<Staged, StoreError>;\n\n    /// ONE atomic write txn: header + body + receipts + state + changesets + indices\n    /// + canonical[height] + head pointer. The head pointer is written LAST, inside the\n    /// same txn. Never split the head pointer from the data it points at.\n    fn commit(&self, staged: Staged, blk: &Block, outcome: &BlockOutcome) -> Result<(), StoreError>;\n\n    fn prove(&self, root: B256, key: StateKey) -> Result<MerkleProof, StoreError>;\n    fn unwind_to(&self, height: u64) -> Result<Vec<SignedTx>, StoreError>; // returns txs to re-pool\n    fn snapshot_manifest(&self, height: u64) -> Result<SnapshotManifest, StoreError>;\n}\n\n/// Commitment is swappable so the hash function is not welded into consensus code.\npub trait StateCommitment {\n    fn empty_root() -> B256;\n    fn apply(&self, base: B256, sorted_writes: &[(StateKey, Option<Bytes>)]) -> (B256, Vec<TrieNode>);\n    fn prove(&self, root: B256, key: StateKey) -> MerkleProof;\n    fn verify(root: B256, key: StateKey, val: Option<&[u8]>, p: &MerkleProof) -> bool;\n}\n```\n\n⚑ Ship the ~200-line sorted-map binary Merkle first. `jmt 0.12.0` was published **2025-10-28**, not 2026-08-16 — one release in ~22 months. Vendor it and read it; do not treat it as a live upstream.\n\n### 3.3 BlockExecutor\n\n```rust\n// crates/executor/src/lib.rs\npub struct BlockOutcome {\n    pub state_root: B256,        // from stage()\n    pub receipts: Vec<Receipt>,\n    pub receipts_root: B256,\n    pub gas_used: u64,\n    pub access_list: BlockAccessList,   // read+write sets per tx, emitted from commit 1\n    pub staged: Staged,\n    pub validator_updates: Vec<ValidatorUpdate>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]\npub enum StfError {                 // every variant is a wire-stable numbered code\n    NonceMismatch { expected: u64, got: u64 },\n    InsufficientFunds { need: U256, have: U256 },\n    IntrinsicGasTooLow { need: u64, got: u64 },\n    TxGasLimitAboveCap { cap: u64 },\n    BlockGasLimitExceeded,\n    BadSignature, WrongChainId, TxTypeNotEnabledInFork(u8),\n    StateRootMismatch { expected: B256, got: B256 },\n    InvariantViolated(&'static str),\n}\n\npub trait BlockExecutor: Send + Sync {\n    /// MUST be a pure function of (base, block, ctx). No clock, no rng, no net, no fs.\n    fn execute(&self, base: B256, blk: &Block, ctx: &BlockCtx)\n        -> Result<BlockOutcome, StfError>;\n\n    /// Same rules, but stops at gas_limit/byte_limit and returns what fits.\n    fn build(&self, base: B256, ctx: &BlockCtx, pool: &dyn TxPool)\n        -> Result<(Vec<SignedTx>, BlockOutcome), StfError>;\n}\n```\n\n### 3.4 TxPool\n\n```rust\npub enum TxSource { Rpc, Gossip, Reinject }        // Reinject skips the min-fee floor\npub enum AddOutcome { Added, Replaced(B256), AlreadyKnown }\n\npub trait TxPool: Send + Sync {\n    fn add(&self, tx: SignedTx, src: TxSource) -> Result<AddOutcome, PoolError>;\n    fn get(&self, h: B256) -> Option<SignedTx>;\n    fn pending_nonce(&self, a: Address) -> u64;\n\n    /// Iterated as a topological sort: global priority order, EXCEPT a sender's txs\n    /// always come out in nonce order.\n    fn best(&self, base_fee: u128, gas_limit: u64, byte_limit: usize) -> Vec<SignedTx>;\n\n    fn on_new_head(&self, ev: &ChainEvent);        // remove included, re-pool unwound, re-price\n    /// ⚑ At a fork activation height, revalidate EVERY pooled tx against the new rules and\n    /// drop failures with a distinguishable error. Silent invalidation is a support incident.\n    fn on_fork_activation(&self, new: ForkId);\n    fn min_gas_price(&self) -> u128;               // DYNAMIC floor, see below\n    fn status(&self) -> PoolStatus;                // pending, queued, bytes, min_fee\n}\n```\n\n| Pool parameter | Value | Rationale |\n|---|---|---|\n| `GLOBAL_SLOTS` / `GLOBAL_QUEUE` | 4096 / 1024 | geth legacypool shape |\n| `ACCOUNT_SLOTS` / `ACCOUNT_QUEUE` | 16 / 64 | per-sender DoS bound |\n| `MAX_BYTES` | 128 MiB | the *byte* cap is what actually binds |\n| `MAX_TX_BYTES` | 128 KiB | |\n| `LIFETIME` | 3 h | |\n| Static floor | 1 gwei | never 1 wei |\n| **Dynamic floor** | on byte-cap overflow, evict lowest effective-fee-rate first and raise `min_gas_price` to `last_evicted_rate + INCREMENTAL_RELAY_FEE` | this, not the static floor, is the anti-spam mechanism |\n| Replacement | ≥10% bump on **both** `max_fee` and `max_priority_fee` **and** `+1 gwei × gas_limit` absolute | percentage-only breaks at the bottom of the range with integer math |\n\n⚑ Do **not** implement ancestor/descendant limits. Bitcoin Core v31.0 (2026-04-20) removed them in favour of cluster limits, and they are meaningless in an account model anyway — per-sender nonce ordering is the equivalent constraint.\n\n⚑ Never ban a peer for a stateful failure (nonce gap, balance). Those are transient. Ban only on stateless-permanent failures (bad signature, wrong chain id, undecodable, over-cap).\n\n### 3.5 ConsensusEngine (sans-I/O)\n\n```rust\n// crates/consensus/src/lib.rs — depends on `types` and `crypto` ONLY.\npub enum ConsensusInput {\n    Start { height: u64, validators: ValidatorSet },\n    Timeout(TimeoutKind, u64, u32),\n    Message { from: PeerId, msg: ConsensusMsg },\n    ProposalValidated { hash: B256, valid: bool },\n    ValueBuilt { height: u64, round: u32, block: Block },\n    WalReplayed(Vec<WalEntry>),\n}\n\npub enum ConsensusEffect {\n    ScheduleTimeout(TimeoutKind, u64, u32, Duration),\n    CancelTimeout(TimeoutKind, u64, u32),\n    Broadcast(ConsensusMsg),\n    /// The engine NEVER holds a key. The runtime routes this to the fenced signer.\n    SignVote(Vote),\n    /// MUST be durably fsync'd BEFORE any Broadcast emitted in the same Vec is sent.\n    WalAppend(WalEntry),\n    BuildValue { height: u64, round: u32, deadline: Instant },\n    ValidateProposal(Block),\n    Decide(Certificate),\n    ReportEquivocation(Evidence),\n}\n\npub trait ConsensusEngine: Send {\n    /// Pure. No I/O, no clock, no allocation of randomness. Byzantine scenarios become\n    /// a Vec<ConsensusInput> in a single-threaded test.\n    fn step(&mut self, input: ConsensusInput) -> Vec<ConsensusEffect>;\n    fn height(&self) -> u64;\n    fn round(&self) -> u32;\n}\n```\n\nQuorum math, stated once so it is not re-derived wrong: with total voting power `P`, quorum `Q > 2P/3`, safety holds while Byzantine power `< P/3`. **Minimum viable set is 4 validators (f=1).** Three is not BFT — quorum is 3 and one crash halts you. Ordering of effects is normative: `WalAppend` before `Broadcast`, always.\n\n### 3.6 The `state_root` / `app_hash` hazard\n\nIn this design, `header[N].state_root` is the **post-state of block N** (Ethereum semantics). If you later swap in an ABCI-shaped engine (CometBFT), `header[N].app_hash` is the post-state of block **N−1**, and `header[0].app_hash = InitChainResponse.app_hash`. ⚑ Crossing that seam without noticing works on one node and diverges at height 1 on two. Write which convention you use into the spec text and assert it in a test.\n\n### 3.7 Network\n\n```rust\npub trait Network: Send + Sync {\n    fn publish(&self, topic: Topic, bytes: Bytes) -> Result<(), NetError>;\n    fn request(&self, peer: PeerId, req: Request) -> BoxFuture<'static, Result<Response, NetError>>;\n    /// Wire this to gossipsub's P4 (invalid messages) score component. That single hookup\n    /// is the cheapest DoS defence you will ever install.\n    fn report(&self, peer: PeerId, j: Judgement);\n    fn peers(&self) -> Vec<PeerInfo>;\n    fn local_status(&self) -> Status;\n    fn subscribe(&self, t: Topic) -> Result<(), NetError>;\n    fn unsubscribe(&self, t: Topic) -> Result<(), NetError>;\n}\npub enum Judgement { Valid, Ignore, Reject(RejectReason) }  // Reject == permanent + scored\n```\n\n### 3.8 Determinism seam (write these four in week one)\n\n```rust\npub trait Clock { fn now_ms(&self) -> u64; fn sleep(&self, d: Duration) -> BoxFuture<'static, ()>; }\npub trait Rng   { fn fill(&mut self, buf: &mut [u8]); }\npub trait Net   { /* send/recv over an injected link */ }\npub trait Wal   { fn append(&mut self, e: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()>; fn sync(&mut self) -> io::Result<()>; }\n```\n`Real*` implementations are constructed **only** in `crates/node`. `Sim*` implementations live in `crates/sim`. Retrofitting this costs 5–20× because `spawn`-and-`await` will already be spread through every module.\n\n### 3.9 TypeScript mirrors\n\n```ts\n// packages/types/src/index.ts\nexport type Address = `0x${string}` & { readonly __brand: 'Address' };\nexport type B256    = `0x${string}` & { readonly __brand: 'B256' };\n\nexport interface Header {\n  parentHash: B256; height: bigint; timestampMs: bigint;\n  stateRoot: B256; transactionsRoot: B256; receiptsRoot: B256; balHash: B256;\n  gasLimit: bigint; gasUsed: bigint; baseFeePerGas: bigint;\n  proposer: Address; extraData: Uint8Array; consensusSeal: Uint8Array;\n}\n\nexport interface StateDB {\n  basic(addr: Address): Promise<Account | undefined>;\n  codeByHash(h: B256): Promise<Uint8Array | undefined>;\n  storage(addr: Address, key: bigint): Promise<bigint>;\n  blockHash(height: bigint): Promise<B256>;\n}\n\nexport interface StateStore {\n  viewAt(root: B256): Promise<StateDB>;\n  stage(base: B256, changes: StateChanges): Promise<Staged>;   // pure, no writes\n  commit(staged: Staged, blk: Block, out: BlockOutcome): Promise<void>;\n  prove(root: B256, key: StateKey): Promise<MerkleProof>;\n  unwindTo(height: bigint): Promise<SignedTx[]>;\n}\n\nexport interface BlockExecutor {\n  execute(base: B256, blk: Block, ctx: BlockCtx): Promise<BlockOutcome>;   // throws StfError\n  build(base: B256, ctx: BlockCtx, pool: TxPool): Promise<[SignedTx[], BlockOutcome]>;\n}\n\nexport interface TxPool {\n  add(tx: SignedTx, src: TxSource): Promise<AddOutcome>;\n  best(baseFee: bigint, gasLimit: bigint, byteLimit: number): SignedTx[];\n  pendingNonce(a: Address): bigint;\n  onNewHead(ev: ChainEvent): Promise<void>;\n  onForkActivation(f: ForkId): Promise<void>;\n  minGasPrice(): bigint;\n}\n\nexport interface ConsensusEngine { step(input: ConsensusInput): ConsensusEffect[]; }\nexport interface Network {\n  publish(topic: string, bytes: Uint8Array): Promise<void>;\n  request(peer: PeerId, req: Request): Promise<Response>;\n  report(peer: PeerId, j: Judgement): void;\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## 4. Storage schema\n\nOne redb/LevelDB keyspace, one-byte table prefix, **every numeric key big-endian** (every ordered KV store sorts bytewise; little-endian keys silently break range scans at block 256).\n\n| Prefix | Table | Key | Value |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `0x01` | `CanonicalHash` | `be_u64(height)` | `B256` block hash |\n| `0x02` | `Header` | `B256` hash | `rlp(Header)` |\n| `0x03` | `HeaderNumber` | `B256` hash | `be_u64(height)` |\n| `0x04` | `BodyIndices` | `be_u64(height)` | `{first_tx_num u64, tx_count u32}` |\n| `0x05` | `Tx` | `be_u64(tx_num)` | typed-envelope bytes |\n| `0x06` | `TxHashToNum` | `B256` tx hash | `be_u64(tx_num)` |\n| `0x07` | `Receipt` | `be_u64(tx_num)` | `rlp(Receipt)` |\n| `0x08` | `Account` | `keccak256(addr)` (32 B) | `rlp([nonce, balance, code_hash, storage_root])` |\n| `0x09` | `Storage` | `keccak256(addr) ‖ keccak256(slot)` | `U256` (dupsort under MDBX) |\n| `0x0A` | `Code` | `B256` code hash | raw bytecode |\n| `0x0B` | `AccountChangeSet` | `be_u64(height) ‖ addr` | pre-image account or tombstone |\n| `0x0C` | `StorageChangeSet` | `be_u64(height) ‖ addr ‖ slot` | pre-image `U256` |\n| `0x0D` | `TrieNode` | node path/hash | encoded node |\n| `0x0E` | `LogIndex` | `addr(20) ‖ topic0(32) ‖ be_u64(height) ‖ be_u32(log_idx)` | `()` |\n| `0x0F` | `AddrIndex` | `addr(20) ‖ be_u64(height) ‖ be_u32(tx_idx)` | `()` — answers \"txs for X\" |\n| `0x10` | `Meta` | ascii key | see below |\n| `0x11` | `ReorgJournal` | `be_u64(seq)` | in-progress unwind marker (crash resume) |\n| `0x12` | `BlockAccessList` | `be_u64(height)` | `rlp(BAL)` |\n| `0x13` | `SnapshotChunk` | `be_u32(version) ‖ be_u64(height) ‖ be_u32(chunk)` | chunk bytes |\n| `0x14` | `InvalidBlock` | `B256` | reason code + first-seen ms |\n\n`Meta` subkeys: `head`, `finalized`, `safe`, `genesis_hash`, `chain_id`, `schema_version`, `snapshot_format_version`, `active_fork`, `pruning_mode`, `burned_cumulative`, `last_compaction`.\n\nSeparate files, never in the consensus DB: `addrbook.json`, `node_key.json` (0600), `priv_validator_key.json` (0600), `priv_validator_state.json` (owned by the signer process, **must never be restored from backup**).\n\n**Rules.** (1) One atomic write transaction per block, containing header + body + receipts + state + both changesets + all indices + `canonical[height]` + `head`, with `head` written last inside that same transaction. (2) Reorgs (pre-M8 only): walk both parent chains to the common ancestor, unwind highest-first by replaying changesets in reverse, delete `canonical[h]` / `TxHashToNum` / `Receipt`, return txs to the pool, apply forward — all in one txn with a `ReorgJournal` marker for crash resume. (3) ⚑ Never write to `InvalidBlock` on the basis of a check whose input an attacker can vary while keeping the block hash constant. That is CVE-2012-2459 exactly: the bug was not that duplicated-tx blocks were accepted, it was that the *hash* got cached as invalid, blocking the legitimate block with the same hash. Domain-separate merkle leaves/nodes and **promote** the odd node instead of duplicating it.\n\n**Sizing reality.** Geth quotes a full Ethereum archive at ~12 TB. Blockscout's own measurement (2024-12-23) is 21,000 GiB for Ethereum mainnet and **5,200 GiB for Sepolia — a testnet**. Never size the explorer DB from the node's disk usage.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Algorithms\n\n### 5.1 Block validation\n\n```\nvalidate_block(store, blk, wire_bytes) -> Result<BlockOutcome, (Verdict, StfError)>\n\n  A. Stateless, no DB touch  (cheap, attributable, permanent on failure)\n   1. decode(wire_bytes); reject if trailing bytes remain\n   2. reject unless encode(decode(wire_bytes)) == wire_bytes            # canonical form\n   3. wire_bytes.len() <= MAX_BLOCK_BYTES (2 MiB)\n   4. header.extra_data.len() <= 32\n   5. header.gas_used <= header.gas_limit\n   6. txs.len() <= MAX_TXS (10_000); each tx encoded len <= 128 KiB\n   7. no duplicate tx hash within the block\n   8. computed = keccak256(rlp(header)); reject if != announced hash\n   9. transactions_root == merkle_root(tx_hashes)\n        leaf   = H(0x00 || tx_bytes)      # domain tags; 0x00/0x01 stop a 64-byte tx\n        node   = H(0x01 || left || right) # being reinterpreted as two internal nodes\n        odd node is PROMOTED, never duplicated\n\n  B. Linkage  (transient on failure — park, do NOT penalise)\n  10. parent = store.header(header.parent_hash)  else -> ORPHAN, park, request ancestors\n  11. header.height == parent.height + 1\n  12. fork = FORKS.active_at(header.timestamp_ms)\n\n  C. Time predicate  (normative spec text — copy verbatim into the chain spec)\n  13. header.timestamp_ms > parent.timestamp_ms                          # strictly monotone\n  14. header.timestamp_ms - parent.timestamp_ms >= MIN_BLOCK_INTERVAL_MS (250)\n  15. header.timestamp_ms <= clock.now_ms() + MAX_FUTURE_DRIFT_MS (2_000)\n        -> if violated: FUTURE, park until eligible; do NOT reject, do NOT penalise\n  16. fork boundary: an activation is evaluated ONLY on header.timestamp_ms, never on\n      local wall clock, so validators with ±2 s skew still agree on which fork applies\n\n  D. Consensus seal\n  17. vset = parent_post_state.validator_set\n  18. header.proposer == expected_proposer(vset, height, round_from_seal)\n  19. verify seal: every signer in vset, no duplicate signer, quorum power > 2/3 total\n  20. if header.height <= store.finalized().0 and hash != canonical[height]\n        -> CONFLICTS_FINALIZED: halt the node, page a human, do not continue\n\n  E. Per-tx stateless  (see STF step 5.1; all must pass or the whole block is invalid)\n  21. for each tx: type in fork.tx_types, chain_id == CHAIN_ID, low-s, y_parity in {0,1},\n      gas_limit <= TX_GAS_CAP (16_777_216 = 2^24), max_fee >= max_priority_fee,\n      value and nonce do not overflow\n\n  F. Execution\n  22. base = parent.state_root ; ctx = BlockCtx from header\n  23. expected_base_fee = calc_base_fee(parent); assert == header.base_fee_per_gas\n  24. outcome = executor.execute(base, blk, ctx)          # calls state.stage(), NOT commit()\n  25. outcome.gas_used     == header.gas_used\n  26. outcome.receipts_root == header.receipts_root\n  27. outcome.state_root   == header.state_root\n  28. outcome.bal.hash()   == header.bal_hash\n\n  G. Verdict\n  29. permanent failure (A, C.13-14, D, E, F) -> INVALID:\n        write InvalidBlock[hash], net.report(peer, Reject), no state written\n  30. transient failure (B, C.15, disk error) -> park; NO penalty, NO InvalidBlock entry\n  31. success -> caller decides: consensus commits via store.commit(outcome.staged, ..)\n```\n\n### 5.2 State transition function\n\n```\nexecute(base_root, blk, ctx) -> Result<BlockOutcome, StfError>\n\n   1. ws = WorkingSet::new(store.view_at(base_root))   # journalled overlay; BTreeMap only\n   2. assert ctx.base_fee_per_gas == calc_base_fee(parent):\n        target = parent.gas_limit / ELASTICITY (2)\n        if parent.gas_used == target:  base = parent.base_fee\n        if parent.gas_used >  target:  base = parent.base_fee\n                 + max(parent.base_fee * (used-target) / target / 8, 1)   # the max(...,1) is load-bearing\n        if parent.gas_used <  target:  base = parent.base_fee\n                 - parent.base_fee * (target-used) / target / 8\n        base = max(base, MIN_BASE_FEE = 1_000_000_000)   # 1 gwei floor; never let it hit 0\n   3. system_pre_block(ws):                              # O(1) or O(k) with hard-coded k.\n        - push parent hash into the 256-entry ring buffer   # MUST NOT error, MUST NOT panic\n        - mix ctx.randomness into the beacon\n        - apply at most K=32 queued validator-set entries\n   4. cumulative_gas = 0; receipts = []; bal = BlockAccessList::new()\n      bal.record_index(0, system_pre_block touched set)\n\n   5. for i, tx in blk.txs.enumerate():\n     5.1  stateless checks (validate_block E, repeated — CheckTx is a weak filter, a\n          Byzantine proposer can put anything in a block)\n     5.2  tokens      = zero_bytes + 4 * nonzero_bytes            # EIP-7623\n          intrinsic   = 21_000 + 16*nonzero + 4*zero\n                      + 2_400*al_addresses + 1_900*al_keys\n                      + (is_create ? 2 * ceil(len(init)/32) : 0)\n          floor       = 21_000 + 10 * tokens\n          required    = max(intrinsic, floor)\n     5.3  if tx.gas_limit < required          -> Err(IntrinsicGasTooLow)\n     5.4  if cumulative_gas + tx.gas_limit > blk.header.gas_limit -> Err(BlockGasLimitExceeded)\n     5.5  sender = ecrecover(tx.sighash(), y_parity, r, s)  -> Err(BadSignature) on failure\n          acct   = ws.account(sender)\n     5.6  if acct.nonce != tx.nonce           -> Err(NonceMismatch)     # never skip, never soft-fail\n     5.7  if acct.code_hash != EMPTY and !fork.allows_delegated_senders -> Err(SenderHasCode)\n     5.8  upfront = tx.gas_limit * tx.max_fee_per_gas + tx.value\n          if acct.balance < upfront           -> Err(InsufficientFunds)\n     5.9  eff_price = base + min(tx.max_priority_fee, tx.max_fee - base)\n     5.10 ws.sub_balance(sender, tx.gas_limit * eff_price); ws.inc_nonce(sender)\n     5.11 cp = ws.checkpoint()                       # journal EVERY warm/cold access-set entry\n                                                     # and every transient-storage write here\n     5.12 res = run(ws, tx, ctx)                     # native handler, or revm behind `evm`\n     5.13 if res.reverted: ws.revert_to(cp)          # gas debit and nonce bump SURVIVE\n     5.14 refund   = min(res.refund_counter, res.gas_used / 5)\n          gas_used = max(res.gas_used - refund, floor)          # the floor is never refundable\n     5.15 ws.add_balance(sender, (tx.gas_limit - gas_used) * eff_price)\n     5.16 ws.add_balance(ctx.proposer, gas_used * (eff_price - base))     # tip only\n     5.17 burned += gas_used * base                  # base fee is credited to NOBODY\n     5.18 cumulative_gas += gas_used\n     5.19 receipts.push(Receipt{ tx.type, res.success, cumulative_gas, res.logs })\n     5.20 bal.record_index(i + 1, ws.take_touched())          # read set, write set, post values\n\n   6. system_post_block(ws):\n        - block reward to ctx.proposer (from the emission curve, not from fees)\n        - apply slashing for any evidence carried in the block, at the INFRACTION-height stake\n        - mature at most K=64 unbonding entries       # never an unbounded loop in a hook\n        - emit validator_updates\n      bal.record_index(len(txs)+1, touched)\n\n   7. assert_invariants(ws):                          # cheap, every block, in release builds\n        a. sum(balances) + burned_cumulative + bonded == TOTAL_ISSUED\n        b. every account with (balance>0 | nonce>0 | code) satisfies\n             balance >= bytes_used(account) * GAS_PER_BYTE_DEPOSIT\n        c. cumulative_gas == sum(receipt gas deltas)\n      violation -> Err(InvariantViolated): HALT the node. Do not continue producing.\n\n   8. staged = state.stage(base_root, ws.into_sorted_changes())   # sorted; pure; no disk write\n   9. return BlockOutcome{ state_root: staged.root, receipts, receipts_root: merkle(receipts),\n                           gas_used: cumulative_gas, access_list: bal, staged, validator_updates }\n      # commit() happens ONLY after consensus decides.\n```\n\n### 5.3 Node startup sequence\n\n```\n 1. parse CLI (clap/commander); resolve --home (default $HOME/.myl1)\n 2. load config.toml + app.toml; env overrides; validate every field, exit 2 on any unknown key\n 3. init tracing subscriber + prometheus registry; bind metrics on 127.0.0.1:6060\n 4. acquire an exclusive advisory lock on <home>/data/LOCK; exit 3 if held\n      -> this is the first line of defence against \"two pods, one key\"\n 5. open the DB; read Meta.schema_version\n      != CURRENT -> run the migration or exit 4 with the exact command to run\n 6. read Meta.genesis_hash\n      absent  -> parse genesis.json (sorted keys, LF, no trailing whitespace),\n                 InitChain: apply alloc, stage(), commit() at height 0,\n                 write Meta.genesis_hash, print its sha256 and exit if --init-only\n      present -> recompute the genesis hash from genesis.json; MISMATCH -> exit 5.\n                 This is the single check that catches an operator running the wrong genesis.\n 7. read Meta.head, Meta.finalized; verify canonical[head] resolves and its header decodes\n 8. if ReorgJournal is non-empty -> finish or roll back the interrupted unwind, then clear it\n 9. replay the consensus WAL from the last committed height; reconstruct engine state\n10. START THE SIGNER FIRST, as a separate fenced process/thread:\n      open priv_validator_state.json, take an exclusive flock, read (height,round,step) HWM,\n      fsync-test the file. If the flock fails -> EXIT. Never \"warn and continue\".\n11. verify the local time source: query the configured NTP/chrony peer; if |offset| > 500 ms,\n      refuse to start as a validator (start as a full node with a loud warning)\n12. compute fork_digest = first4(keccak256(genesis_hash || be_u64(active_fork_ts)\n                                          || be_u16(fork_index)))\n13. build the executor; run a 1-block self-test against a compiled-in fixture and assert the\n      known state root (catches a mis-built binary before it touches the network)\n14. open the P2P listeners: /ip4/0.0.0.0/udp/P/quic-v1 and /ip4/0.0.0.0/tcp/P\n15. subscribe gossip topics for fork_digest; if now_ms is within DUAL_SUBSCRIBE_WINDOW\n      (2 h) of the next activation, ALSO subscribe the next fork_digest's topics\n16. dial bootnodes (>=6, across >=4 ASNs) + persistent_peers; start Kademlia bootstrap;\n      call kad.set_mode(Server) only after AutoNAT confirms an external address\n17. handshake each peer with Status{...}; disconnect on genesis_hash or chain_id mismatch;\n      tolerate a stale fork_digest, disconnect on an incompatible one\n18. choose sync mode:\n      no local state and --statesync.enable -> snapshot sync (verify snapshot_format_version\n        FIRST, then the root against a trusted header) -> then block sync\n      else -> headers-first block sync from the highest common ancestor\n19. once within 2 blocks of the network head, mark synced; only now start consensus\n20. start the tx pool; start the RPC server (bind 127.0.0.1 unless --http.addr is explicit);\n      RPC returns eth_syncing != false until step 19 completes\n21. install signal handlers. On SIGTERM: stop accepting connections -> drain in-flight RPC ->\n      stop consensus at a round boundary -> fsync the WAL and priv_validator_state.json ->\n      flush and close the DB -> exit 0.  systemd: TimeoutStopSec=300 (the 90 s default SIGKILL\n      corrupts the DB mid-compaction)\n22. emit a single structured startup line: version, git sha, chain_id, genesis_hash,\n      fork_digest, head, finalized, peer id, listen addrs\n```\n\n---\n\n## 6. Wire protocol\n\n**Transport.** libp2p. QUIC first (`/ip4/…/udp/P/quic-v1`, ALPN `\"libp2p\"`, TLS 1.3, self-signed cert with OID `1.3.6.1.4.1.53594.1.1`), TCP fallback with Noise `Noise_XX_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256` + **yamux only**. ⚑ Never offer mplex — the spec itself says it \"is deprecated for applications requiring resiliency and liveness\". Raise the yamux window from its 256 KiB default: at 80 ms RTT that caps one stream near 3 MB/s and you will misdiagnose it as \"slow sync\".\n\n**Fork digest is mandatory in the topic string and in the handshake.** ⚑ Without it, upgraded and non-upgraded nodes share one mesh at the activation moment, propagate mutually invalid blocks, score each other down via P4, and partition non-deterministically. Topic format, copied from Ethereum: `/myl1/{fork_digest_hex}/{name}/{encoding}`.\n\n### Gossip topics\n\n| Topic | Payload | Cap | Notes |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `/myl1/{fd}/blocks/ssz_snappy` | `Block` or `CompactBlock` | 10 MiB | switch to compact form above 128 KiB |\n| `/myl1/{fd}/tx/ssz_snappy` | `SignedTx` | 128 KiB | |\n| `/myl1/{fd}/vote/ssz_snappy` | `Vote` | 4 KiB | M8+ |\n| `/myl1/{fd}/evidence/ssz_snappy` | `Evidence` | 1 MiB | M8+ |\n\n### Request/response protocols (one stream per request, length-prefixed uvarint, 10 MiB cap)\n\n| Protocol id | Request | Response |\n|---|---|---|\n| `/myl1/1/status/1` | `Status` | `Status` |\n| `/myl1/1/headers/1` | `{start: u64\\|B256, count: u16 (≤1024), reverse: bool, skip: u16}` | `Vec<Header>` |\n| `/myl1/1/bodies/1` | `Vec<B256>` (≤128) | `Vec<Vec<SignedTx>>` |\n| `/myl1/1/receipts/1` | `Vec<B256>` (≤128) | `Vec<Vec<Receipt>>` |\n| `/myl1/1/blocktxn/1` | `{block_hash, indices: Vec<u32>}` | `Vec<SignedTx>` — BIP-152 fill-in |\n| `/myl1/1/pooled_tx/1` | `Vec<B256>` (≤256) | `Vec<SignedTx>` |\n| `/myl1/1/snapshot_manifest/1` | `{height_hint: u64}` | `{format_version: u32, height, state_root, chunk_count, chunk_hashes}` |\n| `/myl1/1/snapshot_chunk/1` | `{format_version, height, chunk: u32}` | chunk bytes |\n| `/myl1/1/ping/1` | `u64 seq` | `u64 seq` |\n\n### Status (handshake) — modelled on `eth/72`, which dropped total difficulty and added a served range\n\n```\nStatus {\n  protocol_version: u32,\n  network_id: u64,\n  chain_id: u64,\n  genesis_hash: B256,\n  fork_digest: [u8;4],\n  fork_next: u64,            // activation timestamp_ms of the next known fork, or 0\n  head_hash: B256,\n  head_height: u64,\n  finalized_height: u64,\n  earliest_available: u64,   // pruning boundary — a peer must not be asked for what it dropped\n  snapshot_format_version: u32,\n}\n```\nDisconnect on `genesis_hash` or `chain_id` mismatch. On `fork_digest` mismatch: if the remote's set is a prefix of yours, tolerate (they are stale, they will upgrade); if yours is a prefix of theirs, tolerate and warn (you are stale); otherwise disconnect and raise an alert.\n\n### Gossipsub parameters (⚑ the rust-libp2p defaults will silently break you)\n\n| Param | Set to | Default that bites |\n|---|---|---|\n| `max_transmit_size` | **10 MiB** | 65,536 — your 2 MB block is silently unsendable |\n| `mesh_n` / `low` / `high` / `lazy` | 8 / 6 / 12 / 6 | Ethereum's production values |\n| `heartbeat_interval` | 700 ms | 1 s |\n| `duplicate_cache_time` / `seen_ttl` | ≥ 4 × block interval | 60 s |\n| `message_id_fn` | `first20(keccak256(domain ‖ decompressed))` | `base58(peer_id) ‖ seqno` — the duplicate-storm bug |\n| `mesh_n_low` | 6 | 5 (not the spec's 4) |\n| `D_out`, `flood_publish`, `prune_backoff` | 2, true, 60 s | anti-eclipse; `D_out < D_low` and `D_out ≤ D/2` |\n| P4 (invalid message) weight | wired to `Network::report` | unwired by default |\n\n---\n\n## 7. Timing, gas calibration and the fee oracle\n\n⚑ The corpus flags `MaxGas = -1` as a DoS surface but gives no method to pick a number. Here is the method.\n\n### 7.1 Block interval budget (T = 2,000 ms)\n\n| Phase | Budget | Measured metric |\n|---|---|---|\n| Build proposal (pool → block) | 200 ms | `build_block_duration_seconds` |\n| Gossip p95 to 95% of validators | 300 ms | `block_propagation_seconds{q=0.95}` |\n| **Validate + execute p99** | **500 ms (25% of T)** | `apply_block_duration_seconds{q=0.99}` |\n| Prevote + precommit round trip | 400 ms | `consensus_round_duration_seconds` |\n| Commit + fsync | 100 ms | `commit_fsync_seconds` |\n| Slack (must stay > 0) | 500 ms | derived |\n\n### 7.2 Gas-limit calibration procedure\n\n```\n1. Define minimum-spec node: 8c/16t, 32 GB RAM, 4 TB NVMe TLC, 50/25 Mbps.\n2. Build an adversarial block generator: max cold SLOADs, max keccak over max calldata,\n   max account creations, max signature recoveries, worst-case trie depth.\n3. Run 1,000 blocks at 100% fullness against a state at the size you expect at month 12\n   (do NOT calibrate on empty state).\n4. Record p99 apply_block wall clock per unit of gas: `ns_per_gas_p99`.\n5. GAS_LIMIT = floor( 0.25 * BLOCK_INTERVAL_MS * 1e6 / ns_per_gas_p99 ).\n6. Sanity-clamp to [5_000_000, 60_000_000]. Publish the number AND the measurement.\n7. Alert on apply_block_duration_seconds / block_interval > 0.35 for 5 minutes.\n8. RE-RUN THIS ON EVERY GAS-SCHEDULE FORK. A repricing invalidates the calibration.\n```\nAlso ship `TX_GAS_CAP = 16_777_216 (2^24)` enforced at **both** mempool admission and block validity. It is the single cheapest DoS control available and Ethereum took ten years to add it.\n\n### 7.3 Fee oracle (⚑ absent from the corpus, and it wedges every user at the first congestion event)\n\nOn a new chain the base fee sits pinned at its floor and observed tips are zero, so every wallet quotes ~zero — and then the first congestion event wedges every user simultaneously.\n\n```\neth_maxPriorityFeePerGas:\n   tips = effective tips of all txs in the last 20 blocks, excluding proposer-inserted txs\n   suggested = max( TIP_FLOOR = 1 gwei,\n                    percentile(tips, 60),\n                    TIP_FLOOR * congestion_multiplier )\n   congestion_multiplier = clamp( avg(gas_used/gas_limit over last 20 blocks) / 0.5, 1.0, 4.0 )\n\neth_feeHistory: return real percentiles [10,50,90] but clamp every reward value to >= TIP_FLOOR.\neth_gasPrice (legacy): base_fee_next * 1.25 + suggested_tip.\n```\nPublish, before the public testnet: a wallet-facing fee guidance page; a documented **replace** path (≥10% bump on both fee fields *and* +1 gwei × gas absolute) and **cancel** path (self-transfer, 21,000 gas, same nonce); and a stuck-nonce runbook. These become a daily support burden in month 4 if you ship them after the first incident.\n\n---\n\n## 8.
