        "codeSketches": [
          {
            "label": "aserti3-2d, verbatim structure from the BCH upgrade spec (note trunc_div vs arithmetic shift)",
            "language": "rust",
            "code": "// anchor = (h_ref, t_ref = anchor block's PARENT time, target_ref)\n// eval   = (h_eval, t_eval) = the block whose nBits we are computing for\nfn aserti3_2d(h_ref: i64, t_ref: i64, target_ref: U256,\n              h_eval: i64, t_eval: i64, p: &Params) -> u32 {\n    const RADIX: i64 = 65536;\n    let time_delta   = t_eval - t_ref;\n    let height_delta = h_eval - h_ref;\n    // TRUNCATED division (toward zero), multiply by radix BEFORE dividing\n    let mut exponent = ((time_delta - p.ideal_block_time * (height_delta + 1))\n                        * RADIX) / p.halflife;\n    // ARITHMETIC shift (floors toward -inf) - do not reuse trunc_div here\n    let num_shifts = exponent >> 16;\n    exponent -= num_shifts * RADIX;              // now 0 <= exponent < 65536\n    let e = exponent as i128;\n    let factor = (((195766423245049i128 * e\n                  + 971821376i128 * e * e\n                  + 5127i128 * e * e * e\n                  + (1i128 << 47)) >> 48) + 65536) as u64;\n    let mut next = U512::from(target_ref) * U512::from(factor); // ~2^272: MUST be wide\n    if num_shifts < 0 { next >>= (-num_shifts) as u32 } else { next <<= num_shifts as u32 }\n    next >>= 16;\n    if next.is_zero()          { return target_to_bits(U256::one()); }\n    if next > p.max_target.into() { return p.max_bits; }          // 486604799 = 0x1d00ffff\n    target_to_bits(next.low_u256())\n}"
          },
          {
            "label": "Compact nBits codec + chainwork - the sign-bit normalization and the 512-bit-avoiding trick",
            "language": "rust",
            "code": "fn set_compact(nbits: u32) -> (U256, bool /*neg*/, bool /*overflow*/) {\n    let exp = (nbits >> 24) as u32;\n    let mant = nbits & 0x007f_ffff;\n    let neg = (nbits & 0x0080_0000) != 0 && mant != 0;   // 0x00800000 is a SIGN bit\n    let (t, of) = if exp <= 3 {\n        (U256::from(mant >> (8 * (3 - exp))), false)\n    } else {\n        (U256::from(mant), mant != 0 && exp > 34)        // would exceed 256 bits\n    };\n    (if exp > 3 && !of { t << (8 * (exp - 3)) } else { t }, neg, of)\n}\n\nfn get_compact(t: U256) -> u32 {\n    let mut exp = (t.bits() + 7) / 8;                    // size in bytes\n    let mut mant: u32 = if exp <= 3 { (t.low_u64() << (8 * (3 - exp))) as u32 }\n                        else         { (t >> (8 * (exp - 3))).low_u64() as u32 };\n    if mant & 0x0080_0000 != 0 { mant >>= 8; exp += 1; } // else it reads as negative\n    (mant & 0x007f_ffff) | ((exp as u32) << 24)\n}\n\n// floor(2^256/(target+1)) without 512-bit math: 2^256 == ~t + t + 1, so\n// 2^256/(t+1) == ((2^256 - t - 1)/(t+1)) + 1 == (~t/(t+1)) + 1\nfn block_work(nbits: u32) -> U256 {\n    let (t, neg, of) = set_compact(nbits);\n    if neg || of || t.is_zero() { return U256::zero(); }\n    (!t / (t + U256::one())) + U256::one()\n}"
          },
          {
            "label": "Stratum V1 job -> 80-byte header: the three endianness traps in one place",
            "language": "python",
            "code": "import hashlib\nsha256d = lambda b: hashlib.sha256(hashlib.sha256(b).digest()).digest()\n\ndef header_from_job(job, en1_hex, en2_hex, ntime_hex, nonce_hex, version_hex):\n    job_id, prevhash, coinb1, coinb2, branches, ver, nbits, ntime, clean = job\n    # 1. coinbase = coinb1 || extranonce1 || extranonce2 || coinb2\n    coinbase = bytes.fromhex(coinb1 + en1_hex + en2_hex + coinb2)\n    root = sha256d(coinbase)                       # internal (little-endian) txid\n    # 2. fold the branch left-to-right, always root FIRST\n    for b in branches:\n        root = sha256d(root + bytes.fromhex(b))\n    # 3. prevhash arrives 32-BIT-WORD-REVERSED: neither BE nor LE.\n    #    Reverse each 4-byte word, then reverse the whole 32 bytes for the header.\n    ph = bytes.fromhex(prevhash)\n    ph = b''.join(ph[i:i+4][::-1] for i in range(0, 32, 4))[::-1]\n    hdr = (bytes.fromhex(version_hex)[::-1]        # version rolled per BIP320 mask 0x1fffe000\n         + ph\n         + root                                    # merkle root stays internal order\n         + bytes.fromhex(ntime_hex)[::-1]\n         + bytes.fromhex(nbits)[::-1]\n         + bytes.fromhex(nonce_hex)[::-1])\n    assert len(hdr) == 80\n    return hdr, int.from_bytes(sha256d(hdr), 'little')   # compare THIS int to target"
          }
        ],

        "brief": "## Proof-of-Stake and BFT Consensus\n\n### What this dimension actually is\n\nConsensus decides one thing: which sequence of blocks is *the* sequence. Every other safety property of your ledger reduces to it. It is also the one subsystem where a solo builder should adopt rather than write — not because the algorithm is hard (the Tendermint round state machine is ~1,500 lines) but because the WAL crash recovery, vote gossip, evidence gossip, block sync, state sync and light client around it are ~90% of the work.\n\nFour families exist in 2026:\n\n| Family | Finality | Representative | Fork choice? |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Classical BFT | Deterministic, 1 block | PBFT, Tendermint/CometBFT, HotStuff/Jolteon | None needed |\n| DAG BFT | Deterministic, 3 msg rounds | Narwhal→Bullshark→Mysticeti | Ordering over a DAG |\n| Hybrid | Probabilistic head + economic finality | Gasper (LMD-GHOST + Casper FFG) | Yes, plus gadget |\n| Nakamoto PoS | Probabilistic | Ouroboros Praos, BABE+GRANDPA | Yes, plus gadget |\n\n**Recommendation: classical BFT, Tendermint family, CometBFT engine, your state machine behind ABCI 2.0.** The decisive argument is not throughput — it is that with single-slot finality, \"reorg\" does not exist as a concept above consensus. You delete reorg handling from your state machine, indexer, wallet, bridge, and exchange docs. For a tiny team that is worth more than any scalability forfeited.\n\n### The quorum math, verified\n\nWith `n` validators of which `f` are Byzantine: liveness needs `q ≤ n − f`; safety needs any two quorums to intersect in an honest node, so `2q − n ≥ f + 1`. Solving gives `n ≥ 3f+1`, `q = 2f+1`. CometBFT generalizes to voting power. The spec defines **`+2/3` as \"more than 2/3\"** and **`1/3+` as \"1/3 or more\"**, and a **proof-of-lock-change (PoLC)** as *\"a set of +2/3 of prevotes for a particular block or `<nil>` at (H,R)\"*.\n\nNote the spec's safety sentence reads *\"at most -1/3 of the voting power … is byzantine\"* — that hyphen is a **typo in the spec itself**; read it as \"less than 1/3\". Also note the repo spec uses older `LastLockRound`/PoLC prose (unlock iff `LastLockRound < PoLC-Round < R`), while the arXiv paper *The latest gossip on BFT consensus* (Buchman, Kwon, Milosevic) uses `lockedValue/lockedRound/validValue/validRound`. They describe the same protocol; don't mix vocabularies mid-implementation.\n\nMinimum viable set is **4 validators (f=1)**. Three is not BFT — quorum is 3, one crash halts you.\n\n### Engine choice and the CometBFT version trap\n\nThe releases feed (verified) shows a genuinely confusing picture as of Aug 2026:\n\n| Tag | Released |\n|---|---|\n| v0.38.26 | 2026-08-13 |\n| v0.39.4 | 2026-07-28 |\n| v0.40.0 | 2026-07-27 |\n| v0.38.25 / v0.38.24 | 2026-07-27 |\n| v0.39.3 | 2026-05-05 |\n\n**\"Newest\" is v0.38.26, not v0.40.** The repo README still states *\"Currently supported versions include: v0.38.x.\"* v0.40.0 adds an `mldsa65` post-quantum validator key type. **Pin an exact version and read that version's own changelog**; `go list -m -versions github.com/cometbft/cometbft` is the only trustworthy source. v0.38.x is the correct default: it carries complete ABCI 2.0 and is what Cosmos SDK builds against.\n\nMalachite (Rust) README is explicit: *\"alpha software and under heavy development… has not been externally audited; use at your own risk.\"* Benchmarks: 780 ms finalization at 100 validators with 1 MB blocks, up to 2.5 blocks/s. The team **has joined Circle to build Arc** — treat it as promising, not adoptable.\n\n### Block interval: the survey's biggest stale claim\n\n`FinalizeBlockResponse` now carries **field 6, `next_block_delay`** — *\"Delay between the time when this block is committed and the next height is started\"*, marked non-deterministic, and documented as *\"Previously `timeout_commit` in CometBFT config.\"* **The application, not the config file, sets your block interval.** Advice to \"tune `timeout_commit`\" is the old mechanism.\n\nVerified `DefaultConsensusConfig`: TimeoutPropose 3000 ms (delta 500), TimeoutPrevote 1000 (delta 500), TimeoutPrecommit 1000 (delta 500), TimeoutCommit 1000, CreateEmptyBlocks true, PeerGossipSleepDuration 100 ms. Mempool: Size 5000, MaxTxsBytes 1 GB, CacheSize 10000, MaxTxBytes 4 MB.\n\nVerified `types/params.go` defaults — **not what the survey claimed**: Block `MaxBytes = 22020096 + MaxCommitBytes(...)` (~53 MiB), `MaxGas = -1` (unbounded — a real DoS surface, set it), Evidence `MaxAgeNumBlocks 100000` / `MaxAgeDuration 48h` / `MaxBytes 1MB`, `PubKeyTypes: [\"ed25519\"]`, `ABCIParams.VoteExtensionsEnableHeight: 0` (disabled). On `main` the field is **`ABCIParams`, not `FeatureParams`**, and there is **no `DefaultSynchronyParams`** — so PBTS `PRECISION`/`MSGDELAY` defaults (often quoted as 505 ms / 15 s) are **not on this line**. Version-check before writing genesis.\n\n### The ABCI determinism contract\n\nQuoted verbatim from the spec — this is load-bearing:\n\n| Method | Determinism |\n|---|---|\n| PrepareProposal | *\"MAY be non-deterministic\"* |\n| ProcessProposal | *\"MUST be deterministic\"* |\n| ExtendVote | *\"MAY be non-deterministic\"* |\n| VerifyVoteExtension | *\"MUST be deterministic\"* |\n| FinalizeBlock | must execute deterministically |\n\nOn rejection: *\"the whole precommit message will be deemed invalid and ignored… the consensus algorithm may not be able to finalize a block even if sufficiently many (+2/3) validators send precommit votes.\"* A bug there halts the chain. **Leave vote extensions disabled at genesis** and enable at a scheduled height.\n\nBanned in your app (spec's own list): random numbers, time, floating point, library-version drift, races, JSON/protobuf serialization ambiguity, **hash table iteration**, filesystem and network access.\n\n### Slashing and evidence — the part you must write\n\nThis is chain-specific and cannot be outsourced. Verified from `x/evidence`: the validator *\"is reduced (slashed) by `SlashFractionDoubleSign` … of what their stake was when the infraction occurred, rather than when the evidence was discovered.\"*\n\nThe source computes `distributionHeight := infractionHeight - sdk.ValidatorUpdateDelay` — **no `−1`**, contrary to the survey. Evidence is rejected only when `ageDuration > MaxAgeDuration && ageBlocks > MaxAgeNumBlocks` — **both** must be exceeded. Sequence: `SlashWithInfractionReason` → `Jail` → `JailUntil(DoubleSignJailEndTime)` → `Tombstone`.\n\nCosmos defaults (all confirmed, all *testing* values): SignedBlocksWindow **100**, MinSignedPerWindow **0.5**, DowntimeJailDuration **600 s**, SlashFractionDoubleSign **0.05**, SlashFractionDowntime **0.01**. A 100-block window means a 60-second blip jails you. Ship 10,000+ and **SlashFractionDowntime = 0** for the first year.\n\nStaking model: *\"Shares per Token = validator.TotalShares() / validator.Tokens()\"* — slashing reduces `Tokens` only, repricing every delegation atomically. Defaults: UnbondingTime 3 days (a testing value; use 21), MaxValidators 100, MaxEntries 7. The anti-hopping rule is verbatim: a redelegation is forbidden when the delegator *\"already has another immature redelegation in progress with a destination to a validator (Validator X) and is attempting to create a new redelegation where the source validator is Validator X.\"*\n\n**Hard invariant, enforced by nothing in the software: `checkpoint_interval < evidence_max_age < unbonding_time`.**\n\n### Weak subjectivity\n\nVerified: `SAFETY_DECAY = 10`. The spec table gives **665 epochs (~2.95 days)** at 32,768 validators of 32 ETH, rising to **3,532 epochs** at 262,144 — and then **saturating**; 524,288 and 1,048,576 are also 3,532. It does not grow without bound.\n\nLight client rules: adjacent headers compare `trustedHeader.NextValidatorsHash` to `untrustedHeader.ValidatorsHash` and require `verifyCommitFull` (>2/3); skipping uses `verifyCommitTrusting` requiring *\"more than max(1/3, trustLevel) of the voting power\"*; bisect at `pivotHeight := ceil((trustedHeader.Height + untrustedHeight) / 2)`.\n\n### Economic security\n\nCost of collusion for a cartel = 1/3 of bonded value × slash fraction. At Cosmos's 5% default, **34% of stake burns ~1.7% of total bonded value to halt or fork the chain.** Raise it to 0.20–0.30. On day one your token has no float and no reliable price, so bonded value is *undefined*, not small. **Launch permissioned** with equal voting power and a swappable `ValidatorUpdate` source; flip to open PoS by module swap. Don't ship a bridge into a chain whose security you cannot price.\n\n### Traps\n\nRestoring `priv_validator_state.json` from backup, or running one `priv_validator_key.json` on two machines, is the #1 real-world double-sign cause — operational, not protocol. There is no safe hot standby without a fenced signer. Not persisting the lock to WAL *before* broadcasting the precommit produces silent forks. Slashing current instead of infraction-height stake makes slashing decorative. And `MAX_EFFECTIVE_BALANCE` is 32 ETH in phase0 but **2048 ETH in Electra**, with `MIN_SLASHING_PENALTY_QUOTIENT` moving 128 → 4096 (a *softer* minimum slash) — always read the specific fork's file.",

        "brief": "## Peer-to-peer networking layer\n\nThis is the layer that turns N isolated state machines into one network. It is also where \"works on my laptop, dies at 50 nodes\" lives. The strategic answer for a solo builder is unchanged from the survey — **use libp2p, copy Ethereum's parameterization, and port Bitcoin's address-book and connection-slot design onto it** — but several of the survey's concrete facts are now stale or wrong, and the defaults you inherit from rust-libp2p are actively hostile.\n\n### The three reference designs, current as of Aug 2026\n\n| Stack | State | Copy it for |\n|---|---|---|\n| **libp2p** (rust/go/js) | rust-libp2p umbrella crate is **still 0.56.0, published 2025-06-27** (crates.io `max_stable_version`) — no umbrella release in ~14 months; sub-crates move faster | Everything. Transports × security × muxers, Kademlia, GossipSub, DCUtR, relay |\n| **devp2p** (RLPx + discv4/discv5) | **Current wire protocol is `eth/72` (July 2026)**, not eth/68. `Status` is now `[vsn, networkid, genesis, forkid, earliest, latest, latestHash]` — no total difficulty, plus a served-block range. `NewPooledTransactionHashes` gained a `cells: B_16` field; `GetCells`/`Cells` added for cell-level blob relay. **`snap/2` (EIP-8189, June 2026)** removed `GetTrieNodes`/`TrieNodes` (0x06/0x07 reserved) and added `GetBlockAccessLists`(0x08)/`BlockAccessLists`(0x09), replacing iterative trie healing with BAL application | Ethereum interop only |\n| **Bitcoin** hand-rolled | `protocol.h`: `MESSAGE_TYPE_SIZE=12` (renamed from `COMMAND_SIZE`), `MESSAGE_SIZE_SIZE=4`, `CHECKSUM_SIZE=4`. `MSG_WTX=5` exists; `MSG_WITNESS_FLAG = 1<<30` | A weekend reimplementation; the addrman and connection-type designs |\n\n### Decisions, with recommendations\n\n**Stack — rust-libp2p 0.56, QUIC-first.** Listen on `/ip4/0.0.0.0/udp/P/quic-v1` and `/ip4/0.0.0.0/tcp/P`, dial QUIC first. QUIC uses ALPN `\"libp2p\"` and TLS 1.3 with a self-signed single cert carrying OID **`1.3.6.1.4.1.53594.1.1`**, whose extension value is signed over `\"libp2p-tls-handshake:\" ‖ cert_pubkey`; no SNI, no CA path. TCP path: `/noise` = `Noise_XX_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256` only (IK and XXfallback were removed), identity proven by a `NoiseHandshakePayload` signing `\"noise-libp2p-static-key:\" ‖ noise_static_pubkey`, 2-byte BE framing, 65535 max. **Never offer mplex** — the spec says outright \"mplex is deprecated for applications requiring resiliency and liveness.\" Yamux: `/yamux/1.0.0`, **256 KiB default window**, ACK backlog ≤256 streams. That window is a throughput ceiling: at 80 ms RTT one stream caps near 3 MB/s, so raise it before you debug \"slow sync.\"\n\n**Identity — Ed25519, with one caveat.** Ed25519 serializes under 42 bytes, so per `peer-ids.md` the PeerId uses the *identity* multihash (the PeerId **is** the key). Ed25519 is the only MUST; secp256k1/ECDSA are MAY, with a connectivity warning. **Correction to the survey:** Ethereum's consensus layer does *not* use Ed25519 — the spec mandates \"Libp2p-noise ... with `secp256k1` identities,\" because the discv5 ENR v4 identity scheme is secp256k1 and they reuse one key. If you run discv5, take secp256k1; otherwise Ed25519.\n\n**Discovery — layered.** Hardcoded bootnodes (6–10, ≥4 ASNs) + `/dnsaddr` TXT + Kademlia. libp2p kad: **k=20, α=10**, distance `XOR(sha256(k1), sha256(k2))`, bootstrap on start then **every 10 min**, `QueryTimeout` 10 s. The trap is verbatim in the spec: \"Nodes ... add another node to their routing table **if and only if that node operates in server mode**.\" Call `kad.set_mode(Some(Mode::Server))` after AutoNAT confirms an external address, or your DHT silently never forms. If you want pre-dial fork filtering, run discv5 (256 buckets, k=16, α=3; packets 63–1280 bytes; HKDF info `\"discovery v5 key agreement\" ‖ node-id-A ‖ node-id-B`; id-signature over `\"discovery v5 identity proof\" ‖ challenge-data ‖ ephemeral-pubkey ‖ node-id-B`, where `challenge-data = masking-iv ‖ static-header ‖ authdata`). **Budget check the survey missed: an ENR is capped at 300 bytes** (EIP-778) — you get a fork digest and a couple of bitfields, not \"arbitrary fields.\"\n\n**Gossip — GossipSub v1.2 with Ethereum's numbers.** Spec defaults are D=6, D_low=4, D_high=12, D_lazy=D, heartbeat 1 s, fanout_ttl 60 s, mcache_len 5, mcache_gossip 3, seen_ttl 2 min. Ethereum overrides, verbatim: **D=8, D_low=6, D_high=12, D_lazy=6, heartbeat 0.7 s, fanout_ttl 60 s, mcache_len 6, mcache_gossip 3, seen_ttl = SLOT_DURATION_MS × SLOTS_PER_EPOCH × 2 // 1000**, `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE = 10 MiB`, `max_message_size() = max(max_compressed_len(MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE) + 1024, 1 MiB)`. Message-id = first 20 bytes of `SHA256(MESSAGE_DOMAIN_VALID_SNAPPY(0x01000000) ‖ decompressed)`, else the `0x00000000` domain over raw bytes. Topic format `/eth2/ForkDigestValue/Name/Encoding`; note the fork digest is now `compute_fork_digest(genesis_validators_root, epoch)`.\n\nv1.1 additions the survey skipped: `PruneBackoff` 1 min, `UnsubscribeBackoff` 10 s, `FloodPublish` true, `GossipFactor` 0.25, `D_score` 4–5, and **`D_out` = 2 with the constraint `D_out < D_low` and `D_out ≤ D/2`** — a reserved-outbound-mesh rule that is a real anti-eclipse mechanism. Opportunistic grafting: every 1 min, graft ≥2 peers above the median. Threshold ordering is fixed: `Graylist < Publish ≤ Gossip < 0 ≤ AcceptPX`. Lighthouse's production values check out: −4000 / −8000 / −16000, accept_px 100, opportunistic_graft 5, decay_to_zero 0.01, retain_score 100 epochs, IP colocation threshold 8, behaviour penalty threshold 6, `time_in_mesh_weight = 10.0/cap` with cap = 3600 s, `first_message_deliveries_weight = 40.0/cap`, topic weights beacon_block 0.5, slashings/exits 0.05. One conflict worth knowing: the v1.1 spec recommends `MeshMessageDeliveryWindow` of **1–5 ms**; Lighthouse ships **2 s**. Trust Lighthouse.\n\nv1.2 `/meshsub/1.2.0` adds `ControlIDontWant { repeated bytes messageIDs = 1; }` as ControlMessage field 5, optional on both sides. The spec leaves `max_idontwant_messages` literally undefined (`???`); rust-libp2p already ships `idontwant_message_size_threshold = 1000` bytes and `idontwant_on_publish = false`.\n\n**The rust-libp2p defaults that will bite you.** From `protocols/gossipsub/src/config.rs`: `max_transmit_size = 65536` (your 2 MB block is silently unsendable), `mesh_n_low = 5` (not the spec's 4), `duplicate_cache_time = 60 s`, `heartbeat_interval = 1 s`, and the default message-id is **base58(peer_id) ‖ seqno** — the duplicate-storm bug. Override all five.\n\n**Propagation.** Gossip small objects; for blocks over ~128 KiB use BIP-152 form: 80-byte header ‖ 8-byte LE nonce ‖ CompactSize ‖ 6-byte short ids ‖ prefilled txs. Short id = SipHash-2-4 over the txid (wtxid in v2), k0/k1 = first two LE u64 of **single**-SHA256(header ‖ nonce), truncated by dropping the 2 most-significant bytes. **Correction:** the survey's \"0.5×RTT vs 1.5×RTT\" is only half the story. BIP-152's High Bandwidth section says announce-then-request is still \"the same 1.5*RTT minimum time that nodes take today\"; the 0.5×RTT figure appears in Implementation Notes/Justification and requires the smart policy of pushing `cmpctblock` unsolicited right after header validation. Low bandwidth is 1.5×RTT best, \"at least 2.5*RTT\" worst. **Erlay is confirmed unshipped**: BIP-330 is still **Draft**, only the `sendtxrcncl` negotiation message landed (PR #23443); BIP-330 states no bandwidth percentage at all.\n\n**Sync.** Headers-first + parallel bodies + a compiled-in checkpoint. If your state is flat and range-provable, snap-style works (`GetAccountRange [reqID, rootHash, startingHash, limitHash, responseBytes]` → `AccountRange [reqID, accounts, proof]`), but note snapshot data is only served for the **last 128 blocks**. The cheaper design is Bitcoin's assumeutxo: `loadtxoutset` creates a `chainstate_snapshot` dir with a `base_blockhash` file, serves the tip immediately, and validates history in a second chainstate until it reaches the base block and hashes the UTXO set against `CMainParams::m_assumeutxo_data`.\n\n**NAT.** AutoNAT v2 (`/libp2p/autonat/2/dial-request`, `/dial-back`): server dials **exactly one** address, SHOULD NOT reuse its listening port, and **must** demand 30k–100k bytes in ≤4096-byte `DialDataResponse` chunks whenever the selected address's IP differs from the client's observed IP. Client MUST verify the `fixed64` nonce. Relay v2 status codes include `MALFORMED_MESSAGE=400` / `UNEXPECTED_MESSAGE=401` beyond the 100/20x set; the voucher is a signed envelope with domain `libp2p-relay-rsvp`, codec `0x0302`. DCUtR `/libp2p/dcutr`: CONNECT=100, SYNC=300, dial at RTT/2, QUIC responder sprays random UDP at 10–200 ms intervals, retry twice (3 total), 4 KiB max message.\n\n**Eclipse defense — the survey's headline claim, verified and sharpened.** `addrman.h` gives: `ADDRMAN_NEW_BUCKETS_PER_SOURCE_GROUP=64`, `ADDRMAN_NEW_BUCKETS_PER_ADDRESS=8`, `ADDRMAN_TRIED_BUCKETS_PER_GROUP=8`, bucket size 64, 1024 new / 256 tried buckets, `ADDRMAN_SET_TRIED_COLLISION_SIZE=10`, `ADDRMAN_TEST_WINDOW=40min`, `HORIZON=30d`, `RETRIES=3`, `MAX_FAILURES=10`, `MIN_FAIL=7d`, `REPLACEMENT=4h`. Slots from `net.h`: 8 full-relay, 2 block-relay, 1 feeler, 8 addnode, `DEFAULT_MAX_PEER_CONNECTIONS=200`, `TIMEOUT_INTERVAL=20min`, `FEELER_INTERVAL=2min`, `MAX_PROTOCOL_MESSAGE_LENGTH=4,000,000`. **Two corrections:** there is now a **seventh connection type, `PRIVATE_BROADCAST`** (short-lived Tor/I2P connections for relaying your own transactions), and **Bitcoin Core no longer has a numeric ban score** — the `PeerManager` interface exposes only `UnitTestMisbehaving(NodeId)`; misbehaviour is binary discouragement. Do not build accumulating ban points because Bitcoin \"does\"; it doesn't any more.\n\n**Testing.** turmoil is at **0.7.2 (July 2026)**; the API is `Sim`, `host()`, `client()`, `partition()`/**`repair()`**, `hold()`/`release()`, `elapsed()`, with `turmoil::net` mirroring `tokio::net`.           {
            "label": "GossipSub config: the five defaults that must be overridden",
            "language": "rust",
            "code": "// rust-libp2p 0.56 defaults that will bite you (verified in protocols/gossipsub/src/config.rs):\n//   max_transmit_size = 65536 | mesh_n_low = 5 | duplicate_cache_time = 60s\n//   heartbeat_interval = 1s   | message_id = base58(peer_id) || seqno   <-- duplicate storms\nlet message_id_fn = |m: &gossipsub::Message| {\n    let mut h = Sha256::new();\n    match snap::raw::Decoder::new().decompress_vec(&m.data) {\n        Ok(d)  => { h.update([0x01, 0, 0, 0]); h.update(&d) }      // MESSAGE_DOMAIN_VALID_SNAPPY\n        Err(_) => { h.update([0x00, 0, 0, 0]); h.update(&m.data) } // MESSAGE_DOMAIN_INVALID_SNAPPY\n    }\n    gossipsub::MessageId::from(&h.finalize()[..20])               // truncate: 128-bit is plenty\n};\nlet cfg = gossipsub::ConfigBuilder::default()\n    .message_id_fn(message_id_fn)\n    .mesh_n(8).mesh_n_low(6).mesh_n_high(12).mesh_outbound_min(2) // D_out < D_low && <= D/2\n    .gossip_lazy(6).gossip_factor(0.25)\n    .heartbeat_interval(Duration::from_millis(700))\n    .history_length(6).history_gossip(3).fanout_ttl(Duration::from_secs(60))\n    .duplicate_cache_time(SLOT * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH * 2)\n    .max_transmit_size(max(snappy_max_compressed_len(10 << 20) + 1024, 1 << 20))\n    .validation_mode(gossipsub::ValidationMode::Anonymous) // objects self-authenticate\n    .validate_messages()                                   // => you MUST report every result\n    .flood_publish(true)\n    .idontwant_message_size_threshold(1000)                // v1.2; spec leaves the cap undefined\n    .build()?;"
          },
          {
            "label": "addrman new-bucket placement (source-group keyed, the actual eclipse defense)",
            "language": "rust",
            "code": "// Constants verified in bitcoin/src/addrman.h\nconst NEW_BUCKET_COUNT: u64 = 1024;   const TRIED_BUCKET_COUNT: u64 = 256;\nconst BUCKET_SIZE: u64 = 64;          const NEW_BUCKETS_PER_SOURCE_GROUP: u64 = 64;\nconst NEW_BUCKETS_PER_ADDRESS: u64 = 8; const TRIED_BUCKETS_PER_GROUP: u64 = 8;\n\n// group() = ASN if an asmap is loaded, else IPv4 /16 or IPv6 /32. Using the raw address here\n// instead of its group is the bug that makes you eclipse-able by one machine and a script.\nfn new_bucket(key: &[u8; 32], addr: &NetAddr, source: &NetAddr) -> u64 {\n    let h1 = h64(key, &[group(addr).as_ref(), group(source).as_ref()].concat());\n    let h2 = h64(key, &[group(source).as_ref(),\n                        &(h1 % NEW_BUCKETS_PER_SOURCE_GROUP).to_le_bytes()].concat());\n    h2 % NEW_BUCKET_COUNT   // one /16 can reach at most 64 of 1024 new buckets\n}\nfn tried_bucket(key: &[u8; 32], addr: &NetAddr) -> u64 {\n    let h1 = h64(key, addr.key());                       // full address, not group\n    let h2 = h64(key, &[group(addr).as_ref(),\n                        &(h1 % TRIED_BUCKETS_PER_GROUP).to_le_bytes()].concat());\n    h2 % TRIED_BUCKET_COUNT\n}\nfn position(key: &[u8; 32], is_new: bool, bucket: u64, addr: &NetAddr) -> u64 {\n    h64(key, &[&[if is_new {b'N'} else {b'K'}][..], &bucket.to_le_bytes(), addr.key()].concat())\n        % BUCKET_SIZE\n}"
          },
          {
            "label": "Three-valued validation dispatch (Reject vs Ignore is a consensus-splitting distinction)",
            "language": "rust",
            "code": "// GossipSub v1.1 requires Accept/Reject/Ignore, not a boolean.\n// Reject charges P4, a SQUARED penalty. Ignore charges nothing.\nfn acceptance(err: Option<&BlockError>) -> gossipsub::MessageAcceptance {\n    use gossipsub::MessageAcceptance::*;\n    match err {\n        None => Accept,\n        // Cryptographically or structurally invalid: the peer is at fault.\n        Some(BlockError::BadSignature | BlockError::BadProofOfWork\n           | BlockError::MalformedSsz  | BlockError::TooLarge) => Reject,\n        // Valid-but-we-lack-context: NOT the peer's fault. Rejecting these means you\n        // graylist every peer ahead of you during your own initial sync, then cannot sync.\n        Some(BlockError::UnknownParent | BlockError::FutureSlot\n           | BlockError::AlreadyKnown  | BlockError::NotYetFinalizedRoot) => Ignore,\n        Some(_) => Ignore, // default to Ignore; only penalize what you can prove\n    }\n}\n\n// Validation is asynchronous.         "brief": "## Transaction Lifecycle, Mempool, Fee Markets and MEV\n\n### The pipeline, and where the design freedom actually is\n\nA transaction passes six stations: **wire decode → stateless validation → stateful validation → mempool admission (policy) → block building (ordering) → execution/settlement**. Stations 3–5 hold every real design decision and every DoS vector, because they run on unauthenticated, unpaid-for bytes from anonymous peers.\n\nThe load-bearing split is **stateless vs. stateful**. Stateless failures are *permanent and attributable* — cache the txid as invalid and decrement the peer's score. Stateful failures are *transient* — the same tx may be valid next block, so **never ban a peer for a nonce or balance failure**. Conflating them lets an attacker make honest nodes disconnect each other by relaying soon-to-be-valid transactions.\n\ngo-ethereum's `core/txpool/validation.go` is the reference. `ValidateTransaction` (stateless) runs, in source order: tx-type accepted → size cap → fork gating → init-code size → **per-tx gas cap** (`ErrGasLimitTooHigh`) → negative value → block gas limit → feecap/tipcap bit-length → tip ≤ feecap → **signature recovery** → nonce overflow → value overflow → intrinsic gas → floor data gas → min-tip vs pool floor → blob sidecar → SetCode auths. `ValidateTransactionWithState` then does: sender recovery → nonce-too-low → nonce-gap → balance → replacement/expansion funds → per-account slot limit.\n\n**Correction to the survey:** it advised putting signature recovery *last*. Geth does not — recovery sits at position 14 of 21, ahead of intrinsic gas and the min-tip check. Geth's order is *not* cheapest-first. Do better than geth here: recovery is the only ~100 µs step, so put it last behind a txid-keyed LRU validity cache. Just know you are deviating from the reference, not copying it.\n\n### Mempool: a bounded, self-evicting priority index\n\nNot a queue. One owning map plus the *minimum* set of secondary indexes your block builder actually reads. Every index must stay consistent across insert, replace, evict, expire, block-connect and reorg — the #1 source of node bugs.\n\n| Parameter | Bitcoin Core (v31.1, verified) | go-ethereum legacypool | geth blobpool |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Size cap | `DEFAULT_MAX_MEMPOOL_SIZE_MB` 300 | `GlobalSlots` 4096+1024 | disk-backed (billy) |\n| Per-sender | cluster: 64 tx / 101 kvB | `AccountSlots` 16, `AccountQueue` 64 | `maxTxsPerAccount` 16 |\n| Global future queue | — | `GlobalQueue` 1024 | `maxGapped` 128 |\n| Expiry | `DEFAULT_MEMPOOL_EXPIRY_HOURS` 336 | `Lifetime` 3h | — |\n| Min fee | `DEFAULT_MIN_RELAY_TX_FEE` 100 sat/kvB (0.1 sat/vB) | `PriceLimit` 1 wei | — |\n| Replacement bump | `DEFAULT_INCREMENTAL_RELAY_FEE` 100 sat/kvB | `PriceBump` 10% | **100%** |\n| Max tx size | `MAX_STANDARD_TX_WEIGHT` 400,000 WU | `txMaxSize` 128 KB | `txMaxSize` 1 MB |\n| Persistence | `mempool.dat` on shutdown | `transactions.rlp`, `Rejournal` 1h | disk store |\n\nThe real anti-spam mechanism is **not** the static floor — it is the *dynamic* one. When the byte cap is exceeded, evict lowest-fee-rate first and raise `mempoolminfee` to the last-evicted fee-rate plus the incremental relay fee, so you stop even *validating* the flood. This is node-local and non-consensus: two honest nodes will legitimately disagree about relayability, and your integration tests must not assume otherwise.\n\n**Major correction / resolved gap.** The survey's 404 on `doc/policy/mempool-limits.md` was not a broken link — the file was **deleted and replaced** by `doc/policy/mempool-design.md` and `doc/policy/mempool-terminology.md`. And cluster mempool is no longer forthcoming: **Bitcoin Core v31.0 shipped 2026-04-20 (v31.1 on 2026-07-08)**. Per the v31.0 notes: *\"The mempool no longer enforces ancestor or descendant size/count limits\"*, the **CPFP carve-out has been removed**, clusters are capped at **64 transactions / 101 kvB**, RBF now requires the mempool feerate diagram be **strictly improved**, and `getmempoolcluster` / `getmempoolfeeratediagram` are new RPCs. `DEFAULT_ANCESTOR_LIMIT`/`DEFAULT_DESCENDANT_LIMIT` (25/25) still exist in `policy.h` but are no longer the mempool's governing constraint.\n\nAlso corrected: `packages.md` defines package feerate as total modified fees over *\"the total virtual size of all transactions in the package\"* — not \"of transactions not already in the mempool\" as the survey stated. `MAX_PACKAGE_COUNT` 25, `MAX_PACKAGE_WEIGHT` 404,000 WU, child-with-parents topology, and each tx is *\"always validated individually first\"*. BIP-431 (TRUC) remains **Draft**.\n\n### Replacement: require both a ratio and an absolute floor\n\nPercentage-only bumps break at the bottom of the range (10% of 1 wei is 0 wei with integer math ⇒ unbounded free rebroadcast). Bitcoin's surviving rules are **3** (absolute fee ≥ sum of originals), **4** (the fee *delta* pays the replacement's own bandwidth at the incremental relay feerate), **5** (≤100 conflicting clusters), **6** (feerate diagram strictly improved). BIP-125 rules 1 and 2 are **removed**; full-RBF has been default since v28.0. Require *both* a ≥10% bump on **every** fee dimension **and** `incremental_relay_fee_rate × size` in absolute terms. Use **100%** for data-carrying types, exactly as geth's blobpool does. (Note EIP-4844 itself only *recommends* 1.1×; geth chose 2×. Follow geth.)\n\n### Fee market: use the exponential rule\n\nEIP-1559's linear rule, verified verbatim: `gas_used_delta = parent_gas_used - parent_gas_target`; `base_fee_delta = max(parent_base_fee * gas_used_delta // parent_gas_target // 8, 1)` on the up-move, without the `max(…,1)` on the down-move. `ELASTICITY_MULTIPLIER` 2, `INITIAL_BASE_FEE` 1e9 wei, `BASE_FEE_MAX_CHANGE_DENOMINATOR` 8 ⇒ ±12.5%/block. That asymmetry plus multiplicative-in-levels makes it **path-dependent**: up 12.5% then down 12.5% does not return to start.\n\nEIP-4844's exponential rule fixes this and is what to build: keep one cumulative `excess` counter and compute `base_fee = fake_exponential(MIN_BASE_FEE, excess, UPDATE_FRACTION)`. Constants: `GAS_PER_BLOB` 2^17, target 393,216, max 786,432, `MIN_BASE_FEE_PER_BLOB_GAS` 1, `BLOB_BASE_FEE_UPDATE_FRACTION` 3,338,477. It is path-independent, symmetric in log space, and ~15 lines of integer code.\n\n**EIP-7918 (Final)** is the piece most designs miss. Any secondary dimension spends most of its life pinned at its floor, where the price signal is dead and the resource is effectively free — a real bandwidth cost, unpriced. The fix: when `BLOB_BASE_COST * parent.base_fee_per_gas > GAS_PER_BLOB * get_base_fee_per_blob_gas(parent)` (`BLOB_BASE_COST` = 2^13), excess **grows** by `blob_gas_used * (max - target) // max` instead of decaying. Peg every secondary dimension's floor to a fraction of the primary's price.\n\n**EIP-7999 (Draft, 2025-08-04)** generalizes this: one `BASE_FEE_UPDATE_FRACTION` = 4,245,093,508, per-dimension excess normalized as `delta * GAS_NORMALIZATION_FACTOR // limits[i]` so all dimensions move at equal percentage rates, three dimensions (execution, blob, calldata), and — critically for UX — the user still sets **one scalar** `max_fee`, checked as `sum(vector_mul(base_fees, tx_gas_limits)) <= max_fee`. Fungible budget for the user, separate prices for the node. It is Draft; treat the *shape* as proven and the constants as unvalidated.\n\n**Gap the survey missed entirely: EIP-7623 (Final).** Ethereum already shipped a de-facto second dimension without a second fee. `tx.gasUsed = 21000 + max(4*tokens + exec_gas + creation_cost, 10*tokens)` where `tokens = zero_bytes + 4*nonzero_bytes`. A *floor* price on calldata, motivated by 7.15 MB worst-case blocks against ~100 KB average. If you don't want two dimensions on day one, a floor-cost term is the cheap approximation.\n\n### Gas metering\n\nGas must be a linear upper bound on worst-case real cost on your *slowest supported* node. Ethereum failed repeatedly (`EXTCODESIZE` at 20 gas hiding a disk read → EIP-150; `SLOAD` repriced twice → EIP-1884, EIP-2929's 2600 cold / 100 warm). **EIP-7825 (Final)** caps any single transaction at **16,777,216 gas (2^24)**, enforced at *both* mempool and block-validity level — rationale being *\"approximately half of typical block sizes (30-40 million gas)\"*. (The survey said ~1/4; the spec says ~1/2.) Ship this at genesis; Ethereum took ten years.\n\n### Block building and MEV\n\nTwo invariants, stated best by the Cosmos SDK spec: *\"for a given sender their txs must be selected in nonce order\"* and *\"a transaction with a higher priority is always selected before a transaction with a lower priority except when to do so would violate sender-nonce order.\"* Implement as one global priority structure plus one per-sender nonce structure, iterated as a topological sort.\n\nYour default builder **is** your MEV policy. MEV cannot be eliminated, only reassigned. Arbitrum's Timeboost is the honest fix: sealed-bid **second-price** auction, 60 s rounds closing 15 s early, 0.001 WETH reserve, and a **200 ms artificial delay** on all non-express transactions — and the docs state plainly it redirects capture rather than eliminating it. (Timeboost docs do *not* quantify an express-lane edge in ms; only the 200 ms delay is specified.) Encrypted mempools are **not** a v1 feature: size, timing, IP and fee data all leak; users can be paid to decrypt voluntarily; encrypted fee data means *\"anybody can broadcast malformed encrypted transactions that will be ordered but have no ability to pay fees\"*; and *\"a malicious committee privately decrypting transactions early will generate no public evidence and hence such an attack cannot be detected or slashed.\"* PBS is infrastructure, not a feature — a relay is four services plus Redis plus 100 GB+ Postgres. Ship **FOCIL-style inclusion lists** instead (EIP-7805, **Draft**: `IL_COMMITTEE_SIZE` 16, `MAX_BYTES_PER_INCLUSION_LIST` 8192, ILs t=0–8 s, view freeze t=9 s): highest censorship-resistance per line of code.\n\n### State, dust, replay\n\nEIP-1559 prices **flow**; nothing in it prices **stock**. Charge a refundable rent-exempt deposit per account and storage slot — Ethereum's fixed 25,000 gas (`PER_EMPTY_ACCOUNT_COST`) is a permanent liability sold at a spot price. Dust threshold from a separate `DUST_RELAY_TX_FEE` (3000 sat/kvB ≈ 30× the 100 sat/kvB relay floor). For replay: put chain id **and** a fork byte inside the signed payload from block zero — EIP-155 (`v = {0,1} + CHAIN_ID*2 + 35`, nine RLP elements `(nonce, gasprice, startgas, to, value, data, chainid, 0, 0)`) is the canonical example of what retrofitting costs. Finally, EIP-7702's warning generalizes to any programmable account: once code *\"can be called by anyone at any point in a transaction\"*, one third-party tx invalidates a whole queue, so *\"do not accept more than one pending transaction for any EOA with a non-zero delegation indicator.\"*",

Must beat incumbent on BOTH axes.\n    if let Some(old) = self.pending.get(&sender).and_then(|m| m.get(&tx.nonce)) {\n        let bump = if tx.is_data_carrying() { 200 } else { 110 };   // geth blobpool = 100%\n        // multiply BEFORE divide; 10% of 1 wei rounds to 0 and gives free rebroadcast\n        if tx.max_fee * 100 < old.max_fee * bump { return Err(ReplaceUnderpriced); }\n        if tx.max_tip * 100 < old.max_tip * bump { return Err(ReplaceUnderpriced); }\n        // absolute bandwidth floor -- this is Bitcoin RBF rule 4, and it is what\n        // actually stops the attacker; the percentage alone does not.\n        if tx.total_cost() < old.total_cost() + self.incr_relay_fee * tx.size() as u128 {\n            return Err(ReplaceUnderpriced);\n        }\n        self.pending_cost.entry(sender).and_modify(|c| *c -= old.total_cost());\n    }\n    // 2. THE bug everyone ships: balance must cover the sender's WHOLE queue.\n    // Without this a sender with balance B admits 100 txs each spending B.\n    let pending = *self.pending_cost.get(&sender).unwrap_or(&0);\n    if st.balance(sender) < pending + tx.total_cost() { return Err(InsufficientFunds); }\n    if tx.max_fee < max(st.base_fee, self.dynamic_min_fee) { return Err(Underpriced); }\n    if st.is_delegated(sender) && self.count(sender) >= 1 { return Err(DelegationLimit); }\n    Ok(())\n}"

Only sender HEADS ever enter the heap.\nfn build_block(&self, parent: &Header, deadline: Instant) -> Vec<Tx> {\n    let base = next_base_fee(parent);           // THIS block's base fee, not the parent's\n    let mut heap = BinaryHeap::new();\n    for (sender, q) in &self.pending {\n        if let Some((_, tx)) = q.iter().next() { heap.push(Entry(tx.eff_tip(base), *sender)); }\n    }\n    let (mut out, mut gas, mut data) = (vec![], 0u64, 0u64);\n    while let Some(Entry(_, sender)) = heap.pop() {\n        if Instant::now() > deadline { break; }              // never miss your slot\n        let tx = self.pending[&sender].values().next().unwrap();\n        if gas + tx.gas_limit > GAS_LIMIT || data + tx.data_len > DATA_LIMIT {\n            continue;   // drop this SENDER entirely; skipping a nonce breaks invariant 1\n        }\n        match self.execute(tx) {\n            Ok(used) => { gas += used; data += tx.data_len; out.push(tx.clone());\n                          if let Some(next) = self.next_nonce_tx(sender, tx.nonce + 1) {\n                              heap.push(Entry(next.eff_tip(base), sender)); } }\n            Err(_) => continue,                              // sender dropped, not skipped\n        }\n    }\n    out\n}"

The wave is what makes `finish_validation` sound; a plain counter is a subtle liveness/correctness bug.\n\nEmit an EIP-7928 block access list from day 1 — you already have the read/write set.         "brief": "## Cheaper paths: tokens, rollups and rollup-as-a-service\n\nAlmost nobody who says \"I want my own crypto\" needs an L1. There are five rungs, and the cost gap between the bottom and the top is four orders of magnitude. This brief is verified against primary docs and source files (fetch dates: 29–30 Aug 2026); every number below is either quoted from a source in the list or explicitly flagged as an estimate.\n\n### The five rungs\n\n| Rung | What it is | Time to live | Running cost | What you give up |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1. Token on an existing chain | ERC-20/721/1155, SPL/Token-2022, Cosmos TokenFactory denom | An afternoon | $0/mo | Execution-environment sovereignty. Nothing else. |\n| 2. L3 on Arbitrum One / Base via RaaS | Settles into an L2, pays L2 gas for settlement | Days | Vendor fee + tiny DA | Parent's sequencer + stacked exit windows |\n| 3. Managed L2 (RaaS) on Ethereum | Vendor runs sequencer/batcher/proposer/RPC/explorer/bridge | Days | ~$3k/mo (Conduit: \"$36,000 per year… plus DA\") + 5% sequencer profit | Key custody; Stage 1 is unreachable |\n| 4. Self-hosted OP Stack L2 | You run op-reth, op-node, op-batcher, op-proposer, op-challenger | Weeks | Infra + DA + ~14 ETH bonds + on-call | ~1.5 FTE, forever |\n| 5. Sovereign rollup / own L1 | Posts to a DA layer, no settlement contract | Months | Everything above + security budget | Trust-minimised bridge; escape hatch |\n\n**Recommendation: ship rung 1 today.** Move up only when you can name a specific transaction your users cannot afford or cannot execute on the chain you are already on.\n\n### Rung 1 — the token\n\nEIP-20 is six functions (`totalSupply`, `balanceOf`, `transfer`, `transferFrom`, `approve`, `allowance`), two events (`Transfer`, `Approval`) and three optional metadata calls, with `decimals()` returning `uint8`. The spec itself carries the two integration warnings: callers \"MUST handle `false` from `returns (bool success)`\" and the approve race is mitigated by \"set the allowance first to `0` before setting it to another value for the same spender.\"\n\nDeploy OpenZeppelin's canonical shape — `contract T is ERC20 { constructor(uint256 s) ERC20(\"Name\",\"SYM\") { _mint(msg.sender, s); } }` — plus `ERC20Permit`, and stop. No `Ownable`, no `mint()`, no pause, no proxy. `decimals` is \"only used for display purposes\"; 18 is the default, so 5 whole tokens is `5 * 10**18`.\n\nCost is `gas × gasPrice × ETH price`. An OZ ERC-20+Permit deploy is on the order of 1.0–1.5M gas (**estimate — not re-verified this session**): at 1.2M gas and 5 gwei that is 0.006 ETH; at 40 gwei, 0.048 ETH. On Base/Arbitrum the same deploy is cents. Deploy with `forge create <path>:<Contract> --rpc-url … --private-key … --broadcast --verify --verifier etherscan --verifier-api-key … --constructor-args …`. (Correction to the survey: Foundry's reference lists `--broadcast` as an option, not a documented requirement.)\n\nRun the Trail of Bits integration checklist against yourself before an integrator does. Its actual wording: \"The token is not upgradeable\", \"The owner has limited minting capabilities\", \"The token is not pausable\", \"The owner cannot blacklist the contract\", \"The team behind the token is known and can be held responsible\", \"`Transfer` and `transferFrom` return a boolean\", \"`Decimals` returns a `uint8`\", \"The token mitigates the known ERC20 race condition\", \"The token has only one address\". (Its `SafeMath` item predates Solidity 0.8 checked arithmetic — ignore that one.)\n\n**Solana variant.** `Mint::LEN` is exactly `82` bytes and `Account::LEN` is `165` (verified in the token program's `interface/src/state.rs`). Create the mint with two instructions in one transaction: `SystemProgram.CreateAccount` sized from `getMinimumBalanceForRentExemption(space)`, then `InitializeMint2` (which, unlike `InitializeMint`, \"does not require the rent sysvar account\"). For Token-2022, decide the whole extension set first: \"Most extensions can't be added after an account is initialized\", and \"you can't combine the NonTransferable extension with the TransferFeeConfig extension.\" **Correction:** the survey's TransferHook/ConfidentialTransfer conflict is not stated in the primary docs; what *is* documented is that \"the permanent delegate extension does not work with tokens stored in the confidential balance.\" Also note TransferFees force integrators onto `transfer_checked`.\n\n**Liquidity.** `PoolKey{currency0, currency1, fee, tickSpacing, hooks}` with `uint160(currency0) < uint160(currency1)`; fee in pips (3000 = 0.30%); native ETH is `CurrencyLibrary.ADDRESS_ZERO`. `startingPrice = sqrtPriceX96 = floor(sqrt(token1/token0) * 2^96)`; 1:1 is `79228162514264337593543950336`. Anyone can initialize a pool for your key at any price, so initialize and seed in one bundle: `PositionManager.multicall` with `abi.encodePacked(MINT_POSITION, SETTLE_PAIR)` after Permit2 approvals. Launch with `hooks: IHooks(address(0))`.\n\n### Rungs 2–4 — the rollup\n\n**Framework.** OP Stack for a solo build: the create-l2-rollup tutorial names the exact component set (L1 contracts, op-reth, op-node, op-batcher, op-proposer, op-challenger), prerequisites (go v1.26+, rust, just, Node v20, pnpm, foundry, jq, direnv, Docker v24+) and \"about 2-3 ETH\" of Sepolia funding. Polygon CDK is explicitly *not* self-serve any more — its docs say \"Work with Polygon to design and launch a bespoke chain; CDK is the product, not a self-serve kit.\" ZK Stack is mid-rewrite (ZKsync OS, Airbender prover, Prividium). Arbitrum Orbit is the right pick only for an L3 on Arbitrum One, or for Stylus.\n\n**Licence.** Arbitrum's AEP is 10% of *Protocol Net Revenue*, and the docs define that as \"equivalent to an Arbitrum chain's profit (revenue minus costs)\" — profit, not gross. It is enforced on-chain: a `RewardDistributor` splits accrued fees 90/10, the 10% goes through a `ChildToParentRouter` up to the Arbitrum Foundation multisig `0x1Afa41C006dA1605846271E7bdae942F2787f941`. Chains settling to Arbitrum One or Nova are exempt. **Correction:** the 8%/2% split is only partly documented (the guild fund is stated as 2%), and **nothing in the fetched pages says Timeboost/MEV revenue is included** — the survey asserted more than the source supports.\n\n**Stages.** L2BEAT Stage 0 needs: self-identifies as a rollup, state roots on L1, DA on L1, node software that reconstructs state from L1, a proper proof system, and \"at least 5 external actors that can submit a fraud proof.\" Stage 1: the only way to indefinitely block an L2→L1 message is \"compromising ≥75% of the Security Council\", with a ≥7-day exit window for non-Council upgrades. Stage 2: permissionless proofs, ≥30-day exit, Council restricted to onchain-detected errors.\n\n**Fault proofs cost ETH, not dollars.** ~1 week challenge period; initial bond 0.08 ETH per proposal on OP Mainnet; at hourly proposals across a 7-day window that is \"roughly 14 ETH (including gas costs) to make proposals.\" The Guardian can pause withdrawals, blacklist games, and fall back to a permissioned system.\n\n**Forced inclusion is the security property.** OP Stack: `OptimismPortal` deposit, with a \"12-hour rolling window\" and a 30-minute max time drift for deposits; after the window nodes \"begin generating blocks deterministically, incorporating only the forced-included transactions.\" Arbitrum: `forceInclusion` after 24 hours, or sooner under Censorship Timeout — the window is the lesser of `delayBuffer` (30 min to 48 h) and `delayBlocks` (24 h), with a threshold of 150 L1 blocks (~30 min) on One / 300 (~1 h) on Nova, replenishing ~1 minute per 20 minutes of healthy operation.\n\n### DA: the numbers that changed\n\nMainnet `config.yaml` verifies exactly two BPO entries: epoch 412672 (9 Dec 2025) `MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK: 15`, epoch 419072 (7 Jan 2026) `MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK: 21`, against `MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK_ELECTRA: 9`; Fulu activated at epoch 411392. **Correction:** the file carries no `TARGET_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK`, and EIP-7892's 10/15 and 14/21 are labelled illustrative. **No BPO3 is scheduled in the mainnet config as of this fetch** — the \"path to 48\" is roadmap, not consensus.\n\nConsequence: Conduit's widely-quoted $20.56/MB Ethereum vs $7.31/MB Celestia vs $0.81/MB SuperBlobs was measured Mar–Oct 2024, under a 6/9 blob regime, before max blobs went to 21. Treat it as evidence that **batching size dominates** (Orderly went $5.27 → $0.70/MB) and as stale for absolute pricing.\n\n| DA | Verified mechanics | Cost knowledge |\n|---|---|---|\n| Ethereum blobs | Max 21/block since 7 Jan 2026; keeps Stage-0 DA property | Market-priced; re-measure |\n| Celestia | `gas = 65,000 + Σ shares × shareSize × GasPerBlobByte`, +10,000 on an account's first tx; first sparse share 478 bytes, subsequent 482 | Quantised shares punish many small blobs |\n| EigenDA | Reservations = leaky bucket (`symbolsPerSecond`, buckets 1 min client / 1.5 min disperser / 2 min validator); on-demand = `PaymentVault` with `pricePerSymbol` and `minNumSymbols`, symbols = 32 bytes, **rounded up to the next power of two**, quorums 0 and 1 only | **No published $ price found** |\n| Avail | Listed as a supported alt-DA provider by Optimism and Gelato | **Docs unreachable — see gaps** |\n\nSwitching alt-DA is one flag pair (`--altda.enabled`, `--altda.da-server` on both op-node and op-batcher, plus `--altda.da-service` on the batcher) and an `alt_da` object in rollup.json (`da_commitment_type`, `da_challenge_contract_address`, `da_challenge_window`, `da_resolve_window`) — **correction: nested, not flat.** It costs you the Stage-0 DA criterion, and the Standard Rollup Charter states plainly that alt-DA chains do not qualify as Standard. The docs warn: \"DA servers are maintained by third parties and run at your own risk.\"\n\n### Fees and RaaS economics\n\nAfter Isthmus, `totalFee = operatorFee + gasUsed*(baseFee+priorityFee) + l1Fee`, with the Fjord L1 fee `max(minTransactionSize*1e6, intercept + fastlzCoef*fastlzSize) * (baseFeeScalar*l1BaseFee*16 + blobFeeScalar*l1BlobBaseFee) / 1e12`. `operatorFee = operatorFeeConstant + gasUsed*operatorFeeScalar/1e6` (Isthmus) or `×100` (Jovian) — that is your margin knob; don't distort the base fee.\n\nConduit is the only vendor publishing real numbers: Trial Testnet **$250/month**; Growth/Pro/Enterprise \"contact for pricing\" and **every tier carries +5% sequencer profit**; RPC Pro $50/month for 1B CU then $0.10/1M CU; indexing $250 (testnet) / $500 (mainnet); queries $250/month for 15M then $5.00/1M. Caldera and Gelato publish **no** rollup hosting price (Gelato's $0/$99/$399 tiers with $40/1M CU overage are platform CUs, not a chain). Alchemy is \"deploy for free\" + custom enterprise, 99.99% SLA.\n\n### Traps\n\nCustom gas token v2: 18-decimal tokens only, ETH deposits and withdrawals are rejected, `SystemConfig.isCustomGasToken()` and `L1Block.isCustomGasToken()` must agree, and \"there is currently no migration path from legacy CGT to CGT v2.\" Arbitrum's equivalent forbids rebasing tokens, transfer fees, reverts on 0-value transfers, and transfer callbacks. Never merge the batcher, proposer and admin keys. Never launch without op-challenger. Never announce a token before its canonical pool exists.\n",

        "pitfalls": [
          "Quoting 2024 DA cost comparisons in 2026. The $20.56/MB Ethereum vs $7.31/MB Celestia vs $0.81/MB SuperBlobs figures were measured March–October 2024 under a 6-blob target. Fusaka's BPO1 (Dec 2025, target/max 6/9 → 10/15) and BPO2 (Jan 2026, → 14/21) with a stated path to 48 have changed the blob market's supply curve fundamentally. Re-measure at your own throughput before choosing an alt-DA — and note that Celestia's own volume is heavily concentrated in a single customer, which is its own risk.",
          "Treating alt-DA as a free cost optimisation. Switching on --altda.enabled makes you an optimium: full state can no longer be reconstructed from Ethereum alone, which fails an explicit L2BEAT Stage 0 criterion. You inherit a DataAvailabilityChallenge contract to configure and monitor, a third-party DA server the OP docs describe as run at your own risk, and a feature still marked Beta.",
          "Deploying a custom gas token because it sounds cool. CGT v2 supports only 18-decimal tokens, rejects ETH deposits and withdrawals entirely, requires L1 SystemConfig.isCustomGasToken() and L2 L1Block.isCustomGasToken() to agree exactly or transactions fail, has no migration path from legacy CGT, and forces you to cover ETH-denominated L1 gas and DA costs out of minBaseFee and operatorFee denominated in a volatile asset. A 40% token drawdown means running the chain at a loss until you re-tune.",
          "Running one key for the batcher, proposer and admin roles. They have different funding profiles, different slashing exposure, and different rotation cadences. The proposer key is bonded and at risk; the batcher key is drained continuously; the l1ProxyAdminOwner is the key that can rewrite your chain. Leaving fundDevAccounts = true on a chain you intend to keep is the adjacent version of this mistake.",
          "Never testing the escape hatch. Forced inclusion via OptimismPortal.depositTransaction or Arbitrum's forceInclusion is easy to break while adding an allowlist, a custom gas token, or a modified derivation pipeline — and the breakage is silent until the day your sequencer goes down and users discover their funds are frozen. Test it against a deliberately stopped sequencer, in CI.",
          "Launching without op-challenger. An optimistic chain with a live DisputeGameFactory and nobody watching it is a chain where the first attacker to bond a false output root wins after the ~7-day window. This is not a decentralization nicety; it is the security model.",
          "Under-budgeting fault-proof bonds. Permissionless proposals on OP-Mainnet-like parameters cost ~0.08 ETH per proposal and imply roughly 14 ETH of live capital across a 7-day window at hourly cadence. That capital is locked and at risk, not spent — which is why almost every new chain quietly runs a permissioned proposer and stays Stage 0.",
          "Reading only the RaaS sticker price. Conduit's published tiers all carry '+5% sequencer profit', and the bundled Pro RPC plan autoscales at $0.10 per additional 1M compute units beyond 1B, with indexing at $250/$500 per month and queries at $5.00 per additional 1M. The variable components scale with your success, not your costs. Model them at 10x expected volume before signing.",
          "Missing the Arbitrum AEP revenue share. Chains built on Nitro that settle to a parent chain other than Arbitrum One or Nova owe 10% of net chain revenue — 8% to the DAO, 2% to a developer guild — and it applies to sequencer profits and potentially to Timeboost MEV. This is permanent and it is exactly why the L3-on-Arbitrum-One configuration exists.",
          "Choosing Token-2022 extensions at the wrong moment. Extensions are mostly immutable after mint initialization and the account must be sized for them at creation. NonTransferable and TransferFeeConfig cannot coexist; TransferHook and ConfidentialTransfer do not work together. Getting this wrong means minting a new token and migrating every holder — and every extension you add narrows the set of wallets, DEXs and indexers that will handle your token at all.",
          "Shipping an upgradeable proxy token 'just in case'. The Trail of Bits token integration checklist scores non-upgradeability, no arbitrary mint, no pause and no blacklist as security properties. A proxy makes your token uninvestable to serious counterparties and structurally indistinguishable from a rug, regardless of your intent.",
          "Leaving the ERC-20 approve race condition unaddressed in integrating code. EIP-20 itself flags it: a spender can front-run an allowance change and spend the old plus the new allowance. Also handle a false return from transfer/transferFrom — the standard says callers MUST, and plenty of real tokens return false rather than reverting.",
          "Announcing the token before the canonical pool exists. Anyone can call IPoolManager.initialize for your PoolKey at any sqrtPriceX96 they like. If you leave a gap between the token's first transfer out of the deployer and your own pool creation, someone else sets your opening price and takes the first-block spread.",
          "Adding a Uniswap v4 hook to your first pool. A hook is arbitrary code executing inside the swap path — the newest and least-battle-tested attack surface in the AMM stack. Launch with hooks: IHooks(address(0)) and add a hook later, audited, as a separate pool.",
          "Assuming an L3 gets you L2 treatment. An L3 inherits its parent's sequencer, its parent's liveness, and stacked exit windows — a worst-case withdrawal to Ethereum crosses two challenge periods. Bridges, oracles and DeFi protocols integrate L2s far more readily. If your plan requires other teams to deploy on you, pay the L1 settlement premium.",
          "Calling a sovereign rollup a cheap L2. There is no settlement contract validating it, so there is no trust-minimised bridge, no escape hatch anyone outside your own community honours, and disputes are resolved by social fork exactly as on an L1. It is an L1 that rents DA. Choose it for upgrade sovereignty, never for cost.",
          "Self-hosting with one engineer. The real job list is op-conductor for sequencer failover, op-challenger and op-dispute-mon running continuously, redundant RPC with consistent state, tracking the OP Labs upgrade cadence, hot-key management for four funded L1 addresses, and a written incident runbook. A stalled batcher is not degraded service — it is frozen user funds."

        "brief": "## Node Interfaces, Wallets, Explorers, Indexers and Dev Tooling\n\nThe node is not the product. The interface surface around it is what decides whether anyone can use your chain. This dimension is where solo chain builds die: consensus works, but month six arrives with no explorer, no wallet button, and no way to answer \"show me this address's transactions.\"\n\n### The one decision that dominates everything\n\nDoes your node speak the Ethereum JSON-RPC surface? Match it and you inherit MetaMask, viem/wagmi/ethers/web3.py, Foundry, Hardhat, Blockscout, Ponder, graph-node, Envio, Safe, chainlist.org, WalletConnect's `eip155` namespace, and Ledger's existing Ethereum app. Diverge and you owe four SDKs, a bespoke explorer, a bespoke indexer, and a Ledger device app.\n\nThat last cost is now higher than the survey suggested. Ledger [mandates Rust for all new device apps](https://developers.ledger.com/docs/device-app/getting-started) (C is maintenance-only), and the gate for appearing on the \"My Ledger\" list is a **third-party security audit** by an approved partner (Kudelski IoT, Quarkslab) — not merely passing a CI workflow. Ledger Live support requires a separate commercial agreement on top. Budget 6–12 months and real money, or stay secp256k1/EVM.\n\n**Recommendation: implement the Ethereum JSON-RPC surface exactly**, unless your execution model genuinely cannot express (account, nonce, code, storage, logs, receipts). Cosmos SDK builds should ship gRPC:9090 + REST:1317 + CometBFT RPC:26657 *and* an EVM shim. SVM-semantics builds should ship the Solana surface — Phantom and `@solana/web3.js` are equally locked in.\n\n### What \"the spec\" actually contains in 2026\n\nVerify against [ethereum.github.io/execution-apis](https://ethereum.github.io/execution-apis/), not memory. Two corrections worth internalizing:\n\n- The spec's `debug` namespace is **only** `debug_getRawBlock`, `getRawHeader`, `getRawReceipts`, `getRawTransaction`, `getRawBlockAccessList`, `getBadBlocks`. `debug_traceTransaction` is a **geth extension**, not spec. Implement it anyway — Blockscout needs it.\n- The spec's `net` namespace is **only** `net_version`. `net_listening` and `net_peerCount` are de-facto geth. Implement them anyway.\n- The eth namespace has grown: `eth_config`, `eth_capabilities`, `eth_simulateV1`, `eth_blobBaseFee`, `eth_getBlockAccessList`, `eth_getStorageValues` are now present. Engine reaches `getPayloadV6`/`newPayloadV5`/`getBlobsV4`.\n\n**Minimum set for MetaMask + Foundry + Blockscout + Ponder:** `web3_clientVersion`, `web3_sha3`, `net_version`, `net_listening`, `net_peerCount`, `eth_chainId`, `eth_blockNumber`, `eth_syncing`, `eth_gasPrice`, `eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas`, `eth_feeHistory`, `eth_getBalance`, `eth_getTransactionCount`, `eth_getCode`, `eth_getStorageAt`, `eth_getProof`, `eth_call`, `eth_estimateGas`, `eth_createAccessList`, `eth_sendRawTransaction`, `eth_getBlockByHash/Number`, `eth_getBlockTransactionCountByHash/Number`, `eth_getBlockReceipts`, `eth_getTransactionByHash`, `eth_getTransactionByBlock{Hash,Number}AndIndex`, `eth_getTransactionReceipt`, `eth_getLogs`, the five filter methods, `txpool_status`, `txpool_content`, plus `debug_traceTransaction` with `callTracer`.\n\n**Encoding rules to write as tests before any handler exists.** QUANTITY: `0x`-prefixed hex, no leading zeros, `0x0` for zero. DATA: `0x`-prefixed, even digit count. Unknown block/tx/receipt returns `result: null`, never an error. Block tags `latest|earliest|pending|safe|finalized` plus [EIP-1898](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1898) objects `{blockHash, requireCanonical}` (defaults **false**) and `{blockNumber}` — required on exactly six methods (`eth_getBalance`, `getStorageAt`, `getTransactionCount`, `getCode`, `call`, `getProof`), with `-32001` for block-not-found and `-32000` when `requireCanonical` fails. Revert data must use geth's shape `{code: 3, message: \"execution reverted\", data: \"0x08c379a0…\"}` — that is what viem and ethers decode.\n\n### Ports, auth, and the gateway\n\n| Port | Purpose | Bind | Verified default |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 8545 | JSON-RPC HTTP | 127.0.0.1 | geth `--http.port 8545`, `--http.addr localhost` |\n| 8546 | JSON-RPC WS | 127.0.0.1 | geth `--ws.port 8546` |\n| 8551 | Engine API | 127.0.0.1 | spec: MUST be a port independent of public JSON-RPC |\n| 6060 | Prometheus | 127.0.0.1 | geth `/debug/metrics/prometheus` with `--metrics` |\n| 26657/26660 | CometBFT RPC / metrics | 127.0.0.1 / `:26660` | CometBFT config.toml |\n\n[Engine API auth](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/authentication.md), verified verbatim: hex-encoded **256-bit** secret, stored as `jwt.hex`; MUST support `HS256`; MUST reject `alg: none`; SHOULD only accept `iat` within **±60 seconds**; optional `id`/`clv` claims. HTTP authenticates **per request**, WebSocket **only at handshake**, IPC **not at all**. Run chrony — clock skew past 60s stalls the head with no useful log line.\n\nNever expose the node directly. Put a method-aware proxy in front. Reference caps: batch ≤ 50 (geth's own default is a reckless 1000 with a 25 MB response cap; CometBFT's `max_request_batch_size` is **10**), body ≤ 1 MiB, `eth_getLogs` ≤ 10,000 blocks and ≤ 10,000 results rejected with `-32005` naming the limit, WS ≤ 5 subscriptions/connection and ≤ 900 connections (CometBFT's tested `max_subscriptions_per_client = 5`, `max_open_connections = 900`). Allowlist methods; block `engine_*`, `admin_*`, `personal_*`, `miner_*`. Note geth's `--http.vhosts` defaults to `localhost` — behind a load balancer you get opaque 403s. Reth is stricter: **no namespaces are enabled on HTTP/WS by default**; IPC is enabled with all namespaces at `/tmp/reth.ipc` (`\\\\.\\pipe\\reth.ipc` on Windows).\n\n### Node CLI and home layout\n\nFreeze this in week one; operators will script against it and you can never change it. `$HOME/.<chain>/config/{app.toml, config.toml, genesis.json, node_key.json, priv_validator_key.json (0600), addrbook.json}` and `$HOME/.<chain>/data/{*.db, priv_validator_state.json}`, all overridable by `--home`. Command set, modelled on Cosmos SDK because operators already know it: `init`, `keys add`, `genesis add-genesis-account`, `genesis gentx`, `genesis collect-gentxs`, `genesis validate` (emitting a sha256), `start`, `status`, `show-node-id`, `rollback`, `export`, `snapshots {list,export,restore}`, `unsafe-reset-all`.\n\nSerialize `genesis.json` with sorted keys, LF endings, no trailing whitespace. A non-deterministic serializer produces an app-hash mismatch at height 1 across operators and points the error at consensus, not JSON.\n\nOn SIGTERM: stop accepting connections, drain in-flight requests, fsync the WAL and `priv_validator_state.json`, close the DB, exit 0. Set `TimeoutStopSec=300` in systemd — Pebble/LevelDB need flush time, and the default 90s SIGKILL corrupts databases.\n\n### Explorer and indexer\n\nDeploy [Blockscout via docker-compose](https://docs.blockscout.com/setup/deployment/docker-compose-deployment) in week one. Nine containers (13 with microservices), Postgres **17 on port 7432**, frontend on `:80`. Required env: `ETHEREUM_JSONRPC_VARIANT` (`geth|erigon|nethermind|besu|filecoin|anvil`, default `geth`), `ETHEREUM_JSONRPC_HTTP_URL`, `ETHEREUM_JSONRPC_TRACE_URL`, `ETHEREUM_JSONRPC_WS_URL`, `DATABASE_URL`, **`SECRET_KEY_BASE`** (generate with `mix phx.gen.secret` — the survey omitted this and it is required), `CHAIN_ID`, `COIN` (default `POA`). Linux users pointing at a local node must use `0.0.0.0`, not `127.0.0.1`. No tracer yet? Set `INDEXER_DISABLE_INTERNAL_TRANSACTIONS_FETCHER=true` and document the gap. Verify [EIP-3091](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3091) routes: `/block/<h>`, `/tx/<hash>`, `/address/<addr>`, `/token/<addr>`.\n\nYou need an indexer the week your testnet opens. `eth_getLogs` cannot answer \"all transactions for address X,\" \"top 100 holders,\" or \"TVL over time.\" Start with **Ponder**: `ponder.config.ts` / `ponder.schema.ts` (`onchainTable`) / `src/index.ts` (`ponder.on(\"Contract:Event\", …)` with `context.db.insert().onConflictDoUpdate()`), PGlite in dev, Postgres in prod, GraphQL on `:42069/graphql`. graph-node is the right second step and needs exactly seven methods: `eth_getLogs`, `eth_call` (archive + EIP-1898), `eth_getBlockByNumber`, `eth_getBlockByHash`, `net_version`, batched `eth_getTransactionReceipt`, and optionally `trace_filter`. Its config env var must literally be named `ethereum` regardless of your network name. Envio's HyperSync advantage does not apply to an unindexed chain and requires API tokens; it falls back to RPC like everyone else.\n\n### Registries, wallets, predeploys\n\nClaim your chain ID **before public testnet**, both mainnet and testnet in one PR: `_data/chains/eip155-<id>.json` with `name`, `chain`, `chainId`, `networkId`, `shortName` (globally unique — required), `nativeCurrency`, `rpc[]`, `explorers[{standard:\"EIP3091\"}]`. Icons need an IPFS-resolvable CID, positive integer dimensions, png/jpg/svg, **under 250 KB**. Run `./gradlew run` and `npx prettier --write _data/*/*.json`. **First PR wins the ID permanently**; no reassignment except for deprecated chains.\n\nDo **not** register a SLIP-0044 coin type: \"Coin types will be added only if there is a wallet implementing BIP-0044 for desired coin.\" Reuse **60** (EVM) or **118** (Cosmos — Keplr explicitly recommends 118 for Ledger compatibility).\n\nOnboarding is [EIP-3326](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3326) `wallet_switchEthereumChain` with an [EIP-3085](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3085) `wallet_addEthereumChain` fallback. Only `chainId` is required; the wallet MUST reject `file:`/`http:` schemes, empty `rpcUrls`, negative `decimals`, and any case where `eth_chainId` from your RPC disagrees with the declared ID.             "label": "Method-aware RPC gateway guard — the single piece of code that keeps your only node alive",
            "language": "typescript",
            "code": "const COST = { eth_getBalance:1, eth_chainId:1, eth_call:10, eth_getLogs:50, debug_traceTransaction:200 };\nconst BLOCKED = /^(engine_|admin_|personal_|miner_|txpool_content$)/;\nconst MAX_RANGE = 10_000, MAX_BATCH = 50;\n\nfunction guard(body: any) {                        // body = single req or batch array\n  const reqs = Array.isArray(body) ? body : [body];\n  if (reqs.length > MAX_BATCH)\n    throw rpcErr(-32005, `batch size ${reqs.length} exceeds limit ${MAX_BATCH}`);\n  let weight = 0;\n  for (const r of reqs) {\n    if (BLOCKED.test(r.method) || !(r.method in COST))\n      throw rpcErr(-32601, `method ${r.method} not available on this endpoint`);\n    let w = COST[r.method];\n    if (r.method === \"eth_getLogs\") {\n      const { fromBlock = \"latest\", toBlock = \"latest\" } = r.params?.[0] ?? {};\n      const span = blockSpan(fromBlock, toBlock);   // resolves tags against head\n      if (span > MAX_RANGE)                        // MESSAGE must name the limit so\n        throw rpcErr(-32005,                       // clients can auto-paginate\n          `eth_getLogs range ${span} exceeds limit ${MAX_RANGE} blocks`);\n      w *= Math.max(1, span / 1000);\n    }\n    weight += w;\n  }\n  return weight;                                    // feed into per-IP token bucket\n}\n// Cache (method, params) responses forever when the pinned block <= finalized."
          },

            "label": "Reorg-safe aggregate commit — the correctness bug that stays silent for months",
            "language": "typescript",
            "code": "// Never materialize an aggregate from an unfinalized block.\n// Keep head..finalized in an append-only journal you can replay backwards.\nasync function onBlock(block: Block) {\n  const finalized = await rpc(\"eth_getBlockByNumber\", [\"finalized\", false]);\n\n  // 1. Detect reorg: our stored parent must match the incoming block's parentHash.\n  const stored = await db.blockAt(block.number - 1n);\n  if (stored && stored.hash !== block.parentHash) {\n    const fork = await findCommonAncestor(block);            // walk back by hash\n    for (const j of await db.journalAbove(fork.number))       // newest -> oldest\n      await db.applyInverse(j);                               // undo the delta\n    await db.deleteJournalAbove(fork.number);\n  }\n\n  // 2. Apply this block's deltas AND record their inverses in the journal.\n  const deltas = await handle(block);\n  await db.tx(async (t) => {\n    for (const d of deltas) { await t.apply(d); await t.journal(block.number, invert(d)); }\n    await t.putBlock(block.number, block.hash);\n  });\n\n  // 3. Only now is history below `finalized` safe to compact and to serve as truth.\n  await db.deleteJournalBelow(BigInt(finalized.number));\n}\n// Verify: force-reorg a devnet N blocks deep, assert every aggregate reconverges."
          },

Returns null on success. Carries no metadata by design.\n    await provider.request({ method: \"wallet_switchEthereumChain\",\n                             params: [{ chainId: CHAIN_ID_HEX }] });\n  } catch (e: any) {\n    // 4902 is a MetaMask CONVENTION — EIP-3326 defines no error codes.\n    // Fall back on 4902 or on any \"unrecognized chain\" shape.\n    if (e.code !== 4902 && e.code !== -32603) throw e;\n    await provider.request({ method: \"wallet_addEthereumChain\", params: [{\n      chainId: CHAIN_ID_HEX,                        // only required field per EIP-3085\n      chainName: \"MyChain\",\n      rpcUrls: [\"https://rpc.mychain.xyz\"],         // http:/file: are REJECTED;\n      nativeCurrency: { name: \"Foo\", symbol: \"FOO\", decimals: 18 },\n      blockExplorerUrls: [\"https://explorer.mychain.xyz\"],\n    }]});\n  }\n}\n// Wallet rejects if eth_chainId from rpcUrls[0] != CHAIN_ID_HEX. Test that first.\n// Discover the provider via EIP-6963, never window.ethereum:\nwindow.addEventListener(\"eip6963:announceProvider\",\n  (e: any) => providers.set(e.detail.info.rdns, e.detail)); // never removeEventListener\nwindow.dispatchEvent(new Event(\"eip6963:requestProvider\"));"

        "pitfalls": [
          "Hex encoding violations. QUANTITY values must have no leading zeros — '0x41' not '0x041', and '0x0' for zero — while DATA must have an even number of digits. Nearly every hand-rolled RPC returns '0x00' from eth_getTransactionCount on a fresh account, and ethers/viem throw on it. Write the conformance test before the handler.",
          "Returning an error where the spec says null. Unknown block, unknown transaction, and pending receipt must return {\"result\": null}, not a JSON-RPC error. Wallets interpret an error as 'chain is down' and show a red banner; libraries retry in a tight loop.",
          "Missing EIP-1559 fee methods. Without eth_feeHistory and eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas, MetaMask cannot construct a type-2 transaction and falls back to a legacy gas estimate that will usually be wrong, surfacing as a generic 'gas estimation failed'. Ship both even if your fee market is trivial.",
          "eth_estimateGas that simulates against `latest` instead of pending state. Every transaction a user sends right after another of their own will underestimate and revert. Simulate against the pending block, and apply a buffer.",
          "Unbounded eth_getLogs. The first indexer anyone points at your chain will request the full range in one call. Public endpoints in the wild cap between 50 and 20,000 blocks, or cap matched results regardless of range; pick 10,000 blocks / 10,000 results, reject with -32005, and put the limit in the error message so clients can auto-paginate.",
          "Exposing engine_*, admin_*, personal_*, miner_*, or debug_* on the public port. engine_* on a reachable interface is a full chain compromise; debug_traceCall is an unmetered CPU DoS; personal_* plus an unlocked account is theft. Allowlist, never denylist.",
          "JWT mismatch or clock skew on the engine API. The ±60 second `iat` window means an unsynchronized clock breaks consensus↔execution communication with a generic auth failure and no obvious log line.         "brief": "## Tokenomics, Monetary Policy and Governance\n\nTokenomics is the one subsystem you cannot refactor. Consensus bugs get patched; a genesis allocation is permanent social fact. It reduces to four coupled numbers: how many units exist, who holds them at t=0, how fast new ones appear, and what it costs to attack the chain. Everything below is checked against primary sources; where the survey pass was wrong, I say so.\n\n### 1. Units and decimals\n\n`decimals` is display metadata. EIP-20 defines `decimals()` returning `uint8` as OPTIONAL — \"interfaces and other contracts MUST NOT expect these values to be present\" — while `totalSupply()`/`balanceOf()` return `uint256`. The binding constraint is integer width. `2^64-1 = 18,446,744,073,709,551,615`:\n\n| Decimals | Max tokens in u64 | Convention |\n|---|---|---|\n| 6 | 1.845e13 | Cosmos `uatom` |\n| 8 | 1.845e11 | Bitcoin satoshi (int64) |\n| 9 | 1.845e10 | Solana lamport |\n| 18 | **18.4** | ERC-20 wei — forces u128/u256 everywhere |\n\n**Recommendation.** EVM chain or ERC-20: 18 decimals / `uint256`, no exceptions — `parseEther`, MetaMask and every integration hard-assume it. Non-EVM sovereign chain: **6 decimals, u64 storage, u128 for every intermediate multiply**, denom prefixed `u`. Smallest unit should be ≤ $1e-6 at plausible peak price (6 decimals is fine to ~$1/token, 8 to ~$100, 9 to ~$1,000). The overflow you actually hit is `reward_index * stake`, not storage. Serialise amounts as decimal **strings** in RPC/JSON — JSON numbers are IEEE doubles and lose precision above 2^53.\n\n### 2. Emission\n\nBitcoin's entire monetary policy is `halvings = nHeight / nSubsidyHalvingInterval; if (halvings >= 64) return 0; nSubsidy = 50*COIN; nSubsidy >>= halvings;`. Justify every alternative against those eight lines.\n\n**The survey mischaracterised Cosmos.** SDK *module defaults* are `InflationRateChange 0.13, InflationMax 0.20, InflationMin 0.07, GoalBonded 0.67, BlocksPerYear 6311520, MaxSupply 0`. The **live Cosmos Hub** runs `inflation_rate_change 1.0, inflation_max 0.10, inflation_min 0.07, goal_bonded 0.67, blocks_per_year 4360000`. So \"Cosmos prints at 20% when stake leaves\" is false today — the Hub capped it at 10%. Note the Hub is *currently railed at that cap* (`/cosmos/mint/v1beta1/inflation` returns exactly `0.10`), which is the reflexivity critique demonstrated live rather than argued. Also: `blocks_per_year` encodes block time. 31,557,600/6,311,520 = 5.0s (SDK default); 31,557,600/4,360,000 = 7.24s (Hub). Get this wrong and realised inflation silently misses target.\n\nSolana's published schedule is initial 8%, dis-inflation −15%/yr, long-term 1.5%.
