Predictable (publish the curve to year 50), monotone (no reflexive spiral), never zero (no terminal security cliff). Do **not** use the bonded-ratio controller on a small chain. Market a \"maximum issued supply\" over a bounded horizon; never claim a hard cap you don't have. The SDK exposes `InflationCalculationFn` so you can swap this in without forking x/mint.\n\n### 3. Genesis allocation and vesting\n\nFor a solo/tiny team with no institutional round: founders 15%, ecosystem/grants 25%, airdrops 10% (≥3 waves), on-chain community pool 25%, liquidity/MM 10%, genesis validator + testnet incentives 15%. Founders get **0% at TGE, 12-month cliff, then 36 months of per-block linear streaming** — never monthly tranches, which are 36 calendar dates the market shorts into. Target 25–35% real float at TGE. If you raise, keep total investor allocation under 15%. Build vesting as protocol-level accounts with queryable schedules, not a contract or a promise.\n\n### 4. Fees\n\nImplement EIP-1559 verbatim: `INITIAL_BASE_FEE = 1000000000`, `BASE_FEE_MAX_CHANGE_DENOMINATOR = 8`, `ELASTICITY_MULTIPLIER = 2` (so `parentGasTarget = parentGasLimit / 2`). Copy the branch structure exactly, **including `max(..., 1)` on the upward delta** — dropping it lets the base fee stick at low values under congestion. \"The base fee is always burned\"; the proposer keeps only the priority fee. Burning is credibly neutral and removes the incentive to self-stuff blocks. Fund the treasury from a **tax on the subsidy**, not from fees: `community_tax = 0.10` (Hub uses 0.02, which on a small chain funds roughly one part-time contractor). Make the base-fee destination a governable parameter defaulting to burn.\n\n### 5. Staking, slashing, security budget\n\nReal yield, not nominal APR, is the honest number: `real = (1 + (1-c)·I/s)/(1 + I) - 1`. At I=10%, s=40%, c=5%: nominal 23.75%, real **12.5%**, non-staker **−9.1%**. Most of the headline is redistribution from non-stakers. When fee-yield alone exceeds 3–4%, start tapering I.\n\nShip **Cosmos Hub production slashing values, not SDK defaults**. SDK defaults are `signed_blocks_window 100, min_signed_per_window 0.5, slash_fraction_downtime 0.01` — a validator missing 51 consecutive blocks (~4 min) loses 1% of everything delegated to it, which happens during ordinary rolling upgrades. The design inequality is **`B ≥ 3·V_max/f`**. At 1e9 supply, $0.10, 40% bonded → B = $40M; with f = 0.05 a 1/3 attacker risks only $665k, so that is your safe per-window settlement ceiling. Publish this number and enforce it as a hard per-window cap in any bridge.\n\nThe highest-leverage move is **correlated slashing**, and Ethereum's live formula is the template: `process_slashings` applies, at the midpoint of the withdrawal period, `penalty = (EB // increment) * min(sum(slashings) * PROPORTIONAL_SLASHING_MULTIPLIER, total_balance) // total_balance * increment`, with `PROPORTIONAL_SLASHING_MULTIPLIER_BELLATRIX = 3`. Optimism-style default-pass-unless-vetoed must be custom code or an off-chain social process.\n\nUpgrades enact via `Plan{Name, Time(dep), Height, Info, UpgradedClientState(dep)}` and `UpgradeHandler(ctx, plan, fromVM) (VersionMap, error)`.             "code": "// Registered via mint.NewAppModule(..., InflationCalculationFn) so x/mint is not forked.\n// Params: InitialInflation 0.10, DisinflationRate 0.15, TerminalInflation 0.015.\nfunc DisinflationaryInflation(ctx sdk.Context, m minttypes.Minter, p minttypes.Params, bondedRatio math.LegacyDec) math.LegacyDec {\n    // blocksPerYear MUST equal 31_557_600 / blockTimeSeconds. 5s => 6_311_520.\n    year := ctx.BlockHeight() / int64(p.BlocksPerYear)\n    infl := InitialInflation                       // 0.10\n    decay := math.LegacyOneDec().Sub(DisinflationRate) // 0.85\n    for i := int64(0); i < year; i++ {\n        infl = infl.Mul(decay)                     // integer-year steps: no float pow\n    }\n    if infl.LT(TerminalInflation) {\n        infl = TerminalInflation                   // 1.5% floor, perpetual\n    }\n    return infl\n}\n\n// BeginBlocker, unchanged from x/mint:\n//   annual   := infl.MulInt(k.StakingTokenSupply(ctx))\n//   perBlock := annual.QuoInt64(int64(p.BlocksPerYear)).TruncateInt()\n//   k.MintCoins(perBlock) -> k.AddCollectedFees(feeCollector)\n// distribution then takes community_tax (0.10) before any validator split."

Never iterate delegators in BeginBlock.\nfunc (k Keeper) CalculateRewards(ctx sdk.Context, val ValAddr, del DelAddr) sdk.DecCoins {\n    startInfo := k.GetDelegatorStartingInfo(ctx, val, del)\n    stake     := startInfo.Stake                 // stake at delegation time\n    rewards   := sdk.DecCoins{}\n    previous  := startInfo.PreviousPeriod        // period A\n\n    // Iterate ONLY the slash events recorded between A and now.\n    k.IterateValidatorSlashEventsBetween(ctx, val, startInfo.Height, uint64(ctx.BlockHeight()),\n        func(height uint64, ev SlashEvent) bool {\n            if ev.ValidatorPeriod > previous {\n                rewards = rewards.Add(k.calculateDelegationRewardsBetween(ctx, val, previous, ev.ValidatorPeriod, stake)...)\n                stake = stake.MulTruncate(math.LegacyOneDec().Sub(ev.Fraction)) // stake *= F(P)\n                previous = ev.ValidatorPeriod\n            }\n            return false\n        })\n\n    endingPeriod := k.IncrementValidatorPeriod(ctx, val)   // period B\n    return rewards.Add(k.calculateDelegationRewardsBetween(ctx, val, previous, endingPeriod, stake)...)\n}\n// Bug class: applying F(P) before accruing the segment that preceded the slash.\n// Silent, compounding, and only surfaces after your first real slash.         "brief": "# Security: Attack Surface, Hardening, and Audits\n\n## The organizing rule\n\nTwo invariants generate almost every mitigation below. **(1) Every byte an attacker can put on the wire must have a bounded, deterministic, metered cost. Caveat: this doc predates Electra's balance-weighted churn, so treat the *shape* as the model, not the absolute numbers. Network layer\n\nVerified from `src/addrman.h` / `addrman_impl.h`: `ADDRMAN_NEW_BUCKET_COUNT = 1<<10` (1024), `ADDRMAN_TRIED_BUCKET_COUNT = 1<<8` (256), `ADDRMAN_BUCKET_SIZE = 1<<6` (64), `ADDRMAN_SET_TRIED_COLLISION_SIZE = 10` (test-before-evict), `ADDRMAN_HORIZON = 30 days`, `ADDRMAN_RETRIES = 3`, `ADDRMAN_MAX_FAILURES = 10`, `ADDRMAN_REPLACEMENT = 4 hours`. Mandate: encrypted+authenticated transport with peer identity keys, AS-diversity in outbound selection, sentries across ≥3 ASNs, per-peer block-arrival latency monitoring.\n\n## 3.             "language": "rust",
            "code": "// Verified against BIP-340: SHA256(SHA256(tag) || SHA256(tag) || x).\n// The doubled tag is a 64-byte prefix = exactly one SHA-256 block, so the\n// midstate can be precomputed once per tag.\nfn tagged_hash(tag: &[u8], msg: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {\n    let t = Sha256::digest(tag);\n    let mut h = Sha256::new();\n    h.update(t); h.update(t); h.update(msg);\n    h.finalize().into()\n}\n\n// One tag per (chain, message type, version). Never reuse a tag.\n// Leaf and node MUST differ or Merkle second-preimage attacks are trivial.\nconst TAG_VOTE: &[u8] = b\"mychain/vote/v1\";\nconst TAG_TX:   &[u8] = b\"mychain/tx/v1\";\nconst TAG_LEAF: &[u8] = b\"mychain/merkle-leaf/v1\";\nconst TAG_NODE: &[u8] = b\"mychain/merkle-node/v1\";\n\n// EIP-155 lesson: the chain id goes INSIDE the signed bytes, not just the tag,\n// so a testnet or forked-chain vote can never be replayed on mainnet.\nfn vote_sighash(chain_id: u64, h: u64, r: u32, step: u8, blk: &[u8; 32]) -> [u8; 32] {\n    let mut m = Vec::with_capacity(8 + 8 + 4 + 1 + 32);\n    m.extend_from_slice(&chain_id.to_be_bytes());\n    m.extend_from_slice(&h.to_be_bytes());\n    m.extend_from_slice(&r.to_be_bytes());\n    m.push(step);\n    m.extend_from_slice(blk);\n    tagged_hash(TAG_VOTE, &m)\n}"

Bound it and bounds-check the buffer BEFORE allocating.\n    fn bytes(&mut self, max: u32) -> Result<&'a [u8], Err> {\n        let n = self.u32()? as usize;\n        if n > max as usize { return Err(Err::TooLong); }\n        if self.b.len() - self.pos < n { return Err(Err::Truncated); }\n        let s = &self.b[self.pos..self.pos + n];\n        self.pos += n;\n        Ok(s)\n    }\n\n    fn nested<T>(&mut self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut Self) -> Result<T, Err>) -> Result<T, Err> {\n        if self.depth == MAX_DEPTH { return Err(Err::TooDeep); }\n        self.depth += 1;\n        let r = f(self);\n        self.depth -= 1;\n        r\n    }\n\n    /// Canonicality: trailing bytes are a second encoding of the same object,\n    /// which makes \"the hash of the transaction\" ambiguous. Reject, never normalize.\n    pub fn finish(self) -> Result<(), Err> {\n        if self.pos == self.b.len() { Ok(()) } else { Err(Err::Trailing) }\n    }\n}"

Only this file prevents double-SIGNING. It is the safety-critical part.\n#[derive(PartialEq, PartialOrd)]\nstruct Hrs { height: u64, round: u32, step: u8 }\n\nfn sign_vote(st: &mut State, v: &Vote, hsm: &Hsm) -> Result<Sig, Err> {\n    let want = Hrs { height: v.height, round: v.round, step: v.step };\n    // `<=`, not `<`: re-signing the SAME (h,r,s) with a different block is the\n    // equivocation that gets you slashed.\n    if want <= st.high_water { return Err(Err::WouldDoubleSign); }\n    st.high_water = want;\n\n    // ORDERING IS THE ENTIRE POINT. Durable on disk BEFORE the signature can\n    // leave this process. Pair with a distributed lease and an alert on\n    // any two signatures at the same height.\n    f.try_lock_exclusive().map_err(|_| Err::AnotherSignerRunning)?;\n    State::load(f) // NEVER ship this file in a VM snapshot or backup.\n}"

        "key": "testing-ops-upgrades",
        "title": "Testing, simulation, releases, forks and network operations",
        "confidence": "high",
        "brief": "## Testing, Simulation, Releases, Forks and Network Operations\n\n### The one property everything hangs off\n\nConfidence in a chain reduces to a single design decision: the state transition function (STF) must be a pure, deterministic function of `(pre_state, block, block_context)`, and clocks, sockets, disk, threads and RNG must all be injected dependencies. Every technique below is cheap if you make that seam in week one and expensive-to-impossible if you retrofit it. An impure STF produces divergence between honest nodes running the *identical binary*, which presents as a Byzantine fault and is the most expensive bug class in the project.\n\nWrite the signature first:\n\n```\napply_block(pre: &dyn StateView, block: &Block, ctx: &BlockCtx) -> Result<BlockOutcome, StfError>\n```\n\n`BlockCtx { height, timestamp_ms, proposer, randomness, fork }`. The `stf` crate must not depend on tokio, `std::net`, `std::fs`, `std::time`, `rand`, or floats. Enforce it mechanically, not by code review: a `clippy.toml` with `disallowed-methods = [\"std::time::SystemTime::now\", \"std::time::Instant::now\", \"rand::thread_rng\"]` and `disallowed-types = [\"f32\", \"f64\"]`, plus a CI dependency-graph check. In Go, add an analyser that fails on `for range` over a map and on `time.Now()` outside `_test.go`.\n\n### The pyramid\n\n| Layer | What it catches | Runs |\n|---|---|---|\n| Unit tables on STF | Per-tx logic, every `StfError` variant | Every PR, seconds |\n| Property tests (proptest) | Roundtrip, totality, model equivalence | Every PR |\n| Fuzzing (`cargo fuzz`) | Decoder panics, `apply_tx` panics | Nightly, 4 CPU-h/target |\n| Golden fixtures (fill/consume) | Cross-version and cross-impl semantics | Every PR (direct), nightly (rpc) |\n| **Deterministic simulation (DST)** | Consensus safety/liveness under fault schedules | Every PR (3 seeds) + nightly (10k seeds) |\n| Multi-node Docker e2e | Real TCP, real fsync, real restarts, version mixing | Nightly |\n| Open-loop load + soak | Saturation, tail latency, state growth | Nightly + weekly |\n\n### Decision 1 — build the determinism seam at commit #1 (strong recommendation)\n\nDefine four traits with `Real*` and `Sim*` implementations — `Clock`, `Rng`, `Net`, `Storage` — and make the node a step function `handle(&mut self, ev: Event) -> Vec<Action>` that owns no threads. All socket wiring lives in a thin `node-runtime` shim (<400 lines), the only non-deterministic code you own. Then write a ~600-line simulator: a `BinaryHeap` of `(virtual_time_ns, seq, Event)`, a seeded `ChaCha8Rng`, a link matrix, and an invariant checker that runs after every event. Budget one week. Retrofitting costs 5–20x because `spawn`-and-`await` will be spread through every module.\n\nThis is verified as the highest-leverage investment by the people who did it: TigerBeetle's simulator runs \"24/7 on 1024 cores, fuzzing the latest version\" at \"1000x speed\", subjecting the cluster to \"all kinds of network, storage and process faults\", catching \"both logical errors in the algorithms and coding bugs in the source\".\n\nPrint `DST_SEED=<n>` as the first line of every run; on failure append the seed to `tests/seeds/regressions.txt`, which CI replays on every PR. **Caveat:** seeds are invalidated by any refactor that changes the number or order of RNG draws, so for every bug also hand-write a scenario test encoding the *shape* of the failure (`sim.partition(&[0,1],&[2,3]); sim.run_for_ms(5000); sim.heal();`).\n\n### Decision 2 — hand-roll the cluster simulator; use the libraries narrowly\n\nHand-rolling gives you virtual time you can jump by hours, a partition matrix you can flip mid-run, and invariant hooks at every event boundary. If you are on Rust+tokio and want a shortcut, `turmoil` is now the closest fit and has grown well beyond a network simulator: it ships as `turmoil` plus `turmoil-net` (drop-in for `tokio::net`), `turmoil-fs` (drop-in for `std::fs`/`tokio::fs`) and `turmoil-io-uring`, injecting \"latency, drops, and partitions\" plus \"crashes and torn writes\" under \"manual control or a seeded RNG\". `madsim` takes the crate-swap route (`madsim-tokio`, `madsim-tonic`, patched `quanta`/`getrandom`) and is used by RisingWave; note \"all I/O-related interfaces must be mocked during the simulation\".\n\n`loom` and `shuttle` are **not** cluster simulators — they permute concurrent executions of a single test. Use `loom` only on the ~200 lines of lock-free code you actually write (`RUSTFLAGS=\"--cfg loom\" cargo test --release`), and know its documented gaps: `SeqCst` accesses \"are regarded as `AcqRel`\" (false alarms) and \"load buffering behavior\" is not fully explored, meaning \"there can be a bug in the checked code even if Loom says there is no bug (not sound)\". `shuttle` trades soundness for scale — \"randomized testing, rather than the exhaustive testing that Loom offers\". Antithesis is a supplement, not a substitute: its docs claim \"the Antithesis environment is fully deterministic... every bug we find perfectly reproducible\", with faults like \"network partitions or node kills\", but it gives you no sub-second local replay loop.\n\n### Fault taxonomy — crash faults are the easy half\n\n| Fault | Mechanism |\n|---|---|\n| Crash-stop / recover | `docker kill -s KILL`, restart from disk |\n| Pause | `docker pause` / `unpause` (SIGSTOP semantics) |\n| Symmetric partition | `docker network disconnect` |\n| **Asymmetric partition** | `iptables -A INPUT -s <peer-ip> -j DROP` inside one container |\n| Delay/loss | `tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem delay 200ms 50ms distribution normal loss 3%` |\n| Clock skew | `LD_PRELOAD=libfaketime.so.1 FAKETIME=\"+7s\"` |\n| Disk full | data dir on a fixed-size tmpfs |\n| WAL corruption | stop, truncate last N bytes, restart |\n| Byzantine | compiled-in variant: `BYZ_MODE=equivocate\\|invalid_block\\|silent\\|censor\\|flood` |\n\nThe `invalid_block` mode is not optional. Base's June 2026 mainnet halt was exactly this class: the status feed says \"We have isolated a consensus problem that caused an invalid block to be sequenced\", with block production stopping at block 47806542 and node operators required to restart. Process kills would never have found it.\n\n### Cross-implementation confidence with one implementation\n\nBuild a reference-vs-optimised differential inside one repo: a deliberately naive `reference` STF (BTreeMap state, no caching) and the `production` STF (trie, caches, batching). Every fixture, fuzz input and simulated block runs through both; state roots must match. Back it with a versioned fixture suite in the EEST shape and a fill/consume split.\n\n**Correction to the survey's location, now confirmed:** `ethereum/execution-spec-tests` is archived — \"All code from this repository has been migrated to ethereum/execution-specs\" — and the docs live at `steel.ethereum.foundation/docs/execution-specs/` (`eest.ethereum.org` redirects there). The current fixture formats are `state_test`, `blockchain_test`, `blockchain_test_engine`, `blockchain_test_engine_x`, `transaction_test` and `blockchain_test_sync`; fixtures are published as versioned \"EELS Fixture Releases\", not committed to the client source tree. Consume runs in a direct in-process mode and via Hive simulators. Hive itself is the model for heterogeneous black-box testing: `./hive --sim ethereum/sync --client go-ethereum,besu,nethermind`, clients at `./clients/*/Dockerfile`, simulators at `./simulators/<name>`, controller URL passed via `HIVE_SIMULATOR`, results as JSON in `./workspace/logs`.\n\n### Multi-node integration\n\nCopy CometBFT's e2e design: a TOML manifest plus a `runner` executing named stages — `setup` (generates configuration files), `start` (starts Docker containers), `load` (generates a transaction load), `perturb` (runs any requested perturbations), `wait`, `test`, `stop`, `cleanup` — each individually invocable. Tests run as `E2E_MANIFEST=networks/ci.toml go test -v ./tests/...`. A `generator` emits randomised manifests: `-d networks/generated/`, `-g 8` to split into CI groups, and `-m \"latest:1,local:2\"` for mixed-version testnets. Two features the survey missed and you should copy: a built-in `double-signing` perturbation, and node type `upgrade` with an `upgrade_version` manifest attribute, which makes upgrade rehearsal a first-class manifest option rather than a bespoke script. If you are EVM/Engine-API shaped, Kurtosis is a real alternative (`kurtosis run --enclave my-testnet github.com/ethpandaops/ethereum-package --args-file network_params.yaml`) and gives you Prometheus/Grafana and shadowforks via `network_params.network: \"hoodi-shadowfork\"` with `persistent: true`.\n\n### Honest performance numbers\n\nThroughput is not load ÷ latency; the curve is a hockey stick. Generate load **open-loop** (Poisson arrivals at rate λ, drops recorded, never blocking) — a closed-loop generator self-throttles and measures itself. Publish **SLO-throughput**: max λ at which p99 submit-to-finality stays under target, sustained ≥30 min after warm-up, alongside node count, regions, hardware, tx mix, and starting state size. Never benchmark on localhost, on empty state, or with transfers only. Weekly, run a 24h soak at 80% of SLO-throughput and measure DB bytes/block, compaction stalls, p99 drift first-hour vs last-hour, and **time for a fresh node to sync from genesis** — a chain that becomes unjoinable in six months is dead.\n\n### Upgrades, forks, and running it\n\nModel forks as data: `const FORKS: &[ForkSpec]` with `Activation::ByHeight(u64) | ByTimestamp(u64)`, plus an EIP-6122 ForkID in the handshake. The spec defines `FORK_HASH` as the \"IEEE CRC32 checksum of the genesis hash and fork blocks numbers or timestamps that already passed\" (ascending, duplicates checksummed once, e.g. `CRC32(<genesis-hash> || uint64(1150000) || uint64(1668000000))`), and `FORK_NEXT` as the next fork point or 0. Two rules are load-bearing: \"Forks by timestamp MUST be scheduled at or after the forks by block\", and verification \"needs to filter the incoming forkids first by block then by timestamp\". Outcomes are compatible / `ErrRemoteStale` (tolerate) / `ErrLocalIncompatibleOrStale` (disconnect and alert).\n\nFor the primary mechanism, ship the halt-height binary swap. The Cosmos `Plan` is `{Name string; Height int64; Info string}` (plus deprecated `Time` and `UpgradedClientState`); the handler is `func(ctx, plan, fromVM module.VersionMap) (module.VersionMap, error)`, registered via `Keeper#SetUpgradeHandler` with store changes via `app#SetStoreLoader`. Critically, \"if there's a planned upgrade and the upgrade height is reached, the old binary writes `Plan` to the disk before panicking\" — that ordering is what makes restarts idempotent. **Cosmovisor defaults, corrected:** `DAEMON_ALLOW_DOWNLOAD_BINARIES=false`, `DAEMON_DOWNLOAD_MUST_HAVE_CHECKSUM=false` (you must set it true), `DAEMON_RESTART_AFTER_UPGRADE=true`, `DAEMON_POLL_INTERVAL=300ms`, `UNSAFE_SKIP_BACKUP=false`. Two footguns: upgrade names \"are normalized to lowercase\", and \"if a chain upgrade via governance proposal is executed before the specified height with `--upgrade-height`, the governance proposal will overwrite the `upgrade-info.json`\". Never mix both paths.\n\nIf you go the Substrate route instead, use `VersionedMigration<const FROM: u16, const TO: u16, Inner, Pallet, Weight>` wrapping an `UncheckedOnRuntimeUpgrade` — it compares the on-chain version to `FROM`, runs `Inner`, then sets the version to `TO`. Rehearse against live state with `try-runtime --runtime <wbuild>/my-runtime.wasm on-runtime-upgrade live --uri ws://localhost:9999`, with `pre_upgrade() -> Result<Vec<u8>>` / `post_upgrade(state)` checks. Multi-block migrations are now first class (hence the `--disable-mbm-checks` flag) — use them for any migration over an unbounded collection.\n\n### Monitoring and incidents\n\nEnable `instrumentation.prometheus=true` (default `:26660/metrics`, address via `instrumentation.prometheus_listen_addr`) and alert on: `increase(consensus_height[3m]) == 0`; sustained `consensus_rounds > 0`; `consensus_missing_validators_power / consensus_validators_power > 0.2`; `consensus_byzantine_validators_power > 0` (page); `p2p_peers < 5`; growing `mempool_size`; disk runway <14 days; and voting power on the target binary <2/3 with six hours to the upgrade height (if unmet, **cancel the plan** — cancelling is cheap).\n\nWrite the runbooks before mainnet. Rule one for a halt: do not run any reset command; copy `data/` and the consensus WAL from ≥3 nodes — including one that disagreed — to cold storage first. Default to forward-only recovery (patch, resume from halt height, no state change); reserve export-and-restart for unrecoverable corruption, and rehearse it once on the public testnet so you know the wall-clock cost. Recovery time is dominated by coordination, not by the patch: decide in advance who declares an incident, where the war room is, and what quorum authorises a restart. Note the sharpest lesson from Base: the halt landed the day of a scheduled hardfork (Beryl, 25 June 2026, 20:00 UTC), which is precisely when your fork-activation code path is least exercised and your team is most fatigued.\n",

          {
            "label": "Deterministic cluster simulator core loop — the (time, seq) tie-break and per-event invariant check are the load-bearing parts",
            "language": "rust",
            "code": "// Same seed => byte-identical execution => byte-identical failure.\npub fn run(&mut self, until_ns: u64) -> Result<(), Violation> {\n    while let Some(Reverse((at_ns, _seq, ev))) = self.queue.pop() {\n        if at_ns > until_ns { break; }\n        self.now_ns = at_ns;                       // virtual clock: never sleeps\n        let node = &mut self.nodes[ev.dst.0];\n        for action in node.handle(ev.payload) {    // pure step function\n            match action {\n                Action::Send { to, msg } => {\n                    let (from, dst) = (ev.dst, to);\n                    if self.links.partitioned(from, dst) { continue; }          // asymmetric-capable\n                    if self.rng.gen::<f64>() < self.links.loss(from, dst) { continue; }\n                    let lat = self.links.sample_latency(from, dst, &mut self.rng); // log-normal\n                    self.seq += 1;\n                    self.queue.push(Reverse((self.now_ns + lat, self.seq,\n                        ScheduledEvent { dst, payload: Payload::Msg(msg) })));\n                }\n                Action::SetTimer { at_ns, tag } => {\n                    self.seq += 1;\n                    self.queue.push(Reverse((at_ns, self.seq,\n                        ScheduledEvent { dst: ev.dst, payload: Payload::Timer(tag) })));\n                }\n                Action::Persist(w) => self.disks[ev.dst.0].apply(w, &mut self.rng), // torn writes\n                Action::Halt => self.nodes[ev.dst.0].halted = true,\n            }\n        }\n        self.checker.check(&self.nodes, self.now_ns)?;  // agreement, validity, supply, liveness\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}"
          },

Timestamp forks must come at/after block forks.\nfn fork_id(genesis: [u8; 32], head: u64, time: u64) -> ForkId {\n    let mut crc = Crc32::new();\n    crc.update(&genesis);\n    let mut last = 0u64;\n    for f in FORKS {                       // pre-sorted: all ByHeight, then all ByTimestamp\n        let point = f.point();\n        if !f.passed(head, time) { return ForkId { hash: crc.finalize(), next: point }; }\n        if point != last { crc.update(&point.to_be_bytes()); last = point; }\n    }\n    ForkId { hash: crc.finalize(), next: 0 }\n}\n\nfn validate(local_head: u64, local_time: u64, genesis: [u8;32], peer: ForkId) -> Result<(), Err> {\n    // Walk our own history; if peer's hash matches a PREFIX of it, peer is merely behind us.\n    for (i, checkpoint) in fork_checksums(genesis).enumerate() {\n        if peer.hash != checkpoint { continue; }\n        let point = FORKS.get(i).map(|f| f.point()).unwrap_or(0);\n        // Peer announced a next-fork we have already passed => it is on stale rules.\n        if peer.next != 0 && passed(peer.next, local_head, local_time) && peer.next != point {\n            return Err(Err::RemoteStale);          // tolerate: they will catch up\n        }\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n    Err(Err::LocalIncompatibleOrStale)             // disconnect + loud operator alert\n}"

This is what makes it Poisson.\n        let gap = -(1.0 - rng.gen::<f64>()).ln() / rate_hz;\n        next += Duration::from_secs_f64(gap);\n        tokio::time::sleep_until(next.into()).await;          // sleep to the SCHEDULE, not the reply\n        let acct = &accounts[i % accounts.len()]; i += 1;     // per-account nonces never collide\n        let permit = match inflight.clone().try_acquire_owned() {\n            Ok(p) => p,\n            Err(_) => { dropped += 1; continue; }             // record the drop; never back-pressure\n        };\n        let (tx, rec) = (acct.next_tx(&mut rng), rec.clone());\n        tokio::spawn(async move {\n            let t0 = Instant::now();\n            if let Ok(r) = submit_and_await_finality(tx).await {\n                rec.lock().unwrap().push(Sample { submit: t0, incl: r.incl, fin: r.fin });\n            }\n            drop(permit);\n        });\n    }\n    Report::from(rec, dropped)   // publish p50/p90/p99/p99.9 + drops, never a peak-TPS scalar\n}"

        "pitfalls": [
          "**Map iteration order.** Go's `for range` over a map and Rust's `HashMap` iteration are deliberately randomised. Any code path where iteration order affects state — ordering transactions, ordering validator rewards, ordering events — produces different state roots on different nodes running the *identical binary*. This looks like a byzantine fault and is the hardest bug class to diagnose. Use `BTreeMap`, or extract keys and sort explicitly, in every consensus-visible path, and enforce it with a lint rather than a code review habit.",
          "**Floating point anywhere near consensus.** Reward calculations, inflation rates, commission, slashing fractions and price feeds are the usual offenders. IEEE-754 results can differ across architectures, compiler versions and optimisation levels. Use fixed-point integer arithmetic (e.g. u128 with a 10^18 scaling factor) with explicit rounding direction, and ban float types at the crate level in the STF.",
          "**Wall-clock reads inside the STF.** `time.Now()` inside block execution means two nodes replaying the same block at different moments compute different results. The *only* legitimate time source in the STF is the block timestamp handed in via `BlockCtx`, and it must be validated by consensus (monotonic, within a bounded window of the parent).",
          "**Error strings that reach state.** Hashing a `format!(\"{:?}\", err)` into a receipt or an event makes your consensus depend on Rust's Debug formatting and on your Display impls. Use stable numeric error codes in anything that touches state or the receipts root.",
          "**Encoding drift from a dependency bump.** A serde/protobuf/RLP library update that changes how an edge case (empty vec, None, a large integer) is encoded is a silent hard fork. Pin encoding libraries exactly, and keep a fixture test that encodes a fixed corpus of every wire type and asserts against committed byte strings.",
          "**Retrying flaky CI instead of fixing it.** A test that passes on rerun is telling you about a real ordering-dependent bug in a distributed system. Every `retries: 3` in your CI config is a consensus bug you have chosen to ship.",
          "**Treating a seed as a permanent regression test.** Seeds are invalidated by any refactor that changes the number or order of RNG draws. When DST finds a bug, extract a hand-written deterministic scenario test alongside the seed, or the regression silently stops testing anything.",
          "**Testing only crash faults.** Kill/restart is the easy fault. The two production halts with the best public postmortems were neither: Base June 2026 was an invalid block from stale journal state after a failed transaction, and Cosmos Hub v17.1 was a panic in `GetLastValidators` when a simultaneous unjail and unbond pushed the set above `MaxValidators`.           "**Not randomising chain parameters in tests.** Cosmos Hub's own postmortem action item was to 'randomize all chain parameters' — their bug required `MaxValidators` to be near the actual validator count. Fixed test parameters test one point in a large configuration space. Generate them.",
          "**Asymmetric partitions never tested.** Symmetric partitions (A can't talk to B and vice versa) are easy and rarely interesting. One-way drops — A sees B's messages but B doesn't see A's — break naive failure detectors and are the realistic shape of a firewall misconfiguration or an overloaded link.",
          "**Closed-loop load generation.** K workers each submitting and waiting for a reply self-throttles when the chain slows, so the measured throughput is a property of your generator. Use Poisson arrivals at a fixed rate λ with drops recorded, and sweep λ.",
          "**Publishing peak TPS.** Peak throughput occurs exactly at the saturation point, where latency is unbounded and the system is in unstable equilibrium — any burst causes an explosion of latency and a rapid SLO breach.           "**Benchmarking on an empty state, on localhost, with only simple transfers.** All three inflate results by an order of magnitude. Empty state hides trie depth and read amplification; localhost hides fsync-coupled network latency; a transfer-only mix hides the workload your chain will actually see. Always report state size, geography, hardware and transaction mix alongside the number.",
          "**Never measuring sync-from-genesis.** If a new node takes 30 days to sync, no one can join, and you will discover this only when someone tries. Measure it every week and treat a regression as a P1.",
          "**Editing the genesis file after publishing its hash.** The hash *is* the coordination mechanism.           "**Genesis time in the past, or a gentx signed with the wrong chain-id or a pubkey from a different machine.** These are the three most common genesis failures.           "**Auto-downloading upgrade binaries on mainnet.** Whoever controls the plan's `Info` field controls what every validator executes.         "brief": "## Scalability and Privacy: What a New Chain Should Know\n\n### The framing that survives contact with a profiler\n\nThroughput is not set by consensus cleverness. It is `min(sig-verify rate, random state-read rate, state-root hashing rate, block propagation rate)`. Every technique below attacks exactly one of those four, and most teams attack the wrong one — parallel execution buys nothing when you are I/O-bound; data availability sampling buys nothing when you are execution-bound. Build a measurement harness in week 0 and write the four numbers on a wall.\n\n**Caveat on the numbers:** the specific figures often quoted for these four (≈25k secp256k1 ecrecovers/s/core, 10–50k cold random reads/s on NVMe, BLAKE3 at 1–3 GB/s vs Keccak at 200–500 MB/s) are folklore-grade estimates. I could not verify them against a primary source. Treat them as hypotheses your harness confirms or refutes, not as design inputs.\n\nThe honest ceiling for a competent single-shard chain that gets the state layer right is roughly 200–1,000 TPS of simple transfers and 100–500 TPS with real contract calls. Every six-figure number in this space is a lab benchmark, and the papers say so themselves — see the corrections below.\n\n### Verdicts\n\n| Technique | Verdict | Effort |\n|---|---|---|\n| Flat state + separate commitment tree | **v1, non-negotiable** | 2–3 pw |\n| Binary (arity-2) tree, EIP-7864 shape | **v1** | 2–3 pw |\n| Refundable storage deposit | **v1** | 3–5 d |\n| Access-list *field* in tx envelope | **v1** (wire format) | 1 pw |\n| Header layout supporting deferred exec | **v1** (layout only) | 0 |\n| Zcash-style key hierarchy + stealth addresses | **v1, mandatory** | ~1 pw |\n| Leader proposes batch *hashes*, not bytes | **v1** | ~1 pw |\n| Separate fee market for non-executable data | **v1** | 1 pw |\n| Access-list scheduler | v2 | 2–4 pw |\n| Deferred execution (Monad model) | v2 | 2–4 pw |\n| Stateless verifier node class (opt-in) | v2 | 4–6 pw |\n| Orchard-shaped shielded pool | v2/v3 | 4–9 months |\n| Block-STM | v2 at earliest | 6–10 pw |\n| Full Narwhal/Bullshark DAG mempool | v2 | 4–8 pw |\n| State sharding, DAS, Verkle, payment channels, ring signatures, FHE, mixers | **never** | — |\n\n### The state layer is the whole game\n\nStoring state *inside* the trie turns one logical read into ~8–9 physical reads on a hexary MPT. Fixing this is worth more than sharding, DAGs and parallel execution combined, and it is very expensive to undo post-mainnet because it changes your DB schema *and* your sync protocol. Store values in a flat KV table keyed by a 32-byte state key; maintain the commitment tree as a separate structure updated in one batched bottom-up pass at end of block.\n\nFor the commitment tree, copy **EIP-7864** — but note what I verified: it is **Draft**, not final, and *the hash function is explicitly undecided*. The spec says the reference implementation \"uses BLAKE3 to reduce friction for EL clients experimenting with this EIP, but the final decision remains TBD,\" with Keccak and Poseidon2 as candidates. This is your decision to make now: pick Poseidon2 if you may ever SNARK your state transition, BLAKE3 if not. You cannot change it later.\n\nThe verified layout: key = `storage_type(1 byte) || tree_position(30 bytes) || sub_index(1 byte)`. The **stem is the 31-byte prefix**, not 30 — a detail that matters because it is the stem that gets hashed. Constants: `HEADER_SUBTREE=0`, `CODE_SUBTREE=1`, `STORAGE_SUBTREE=255`, `BASIC_DATA_LEAF_KEY=0`, `CODE_HASH_LEAF_KEY=1`, `HEADER_STORAGE_OFFSET=20`, `CODE_OFFSET=4`, `CODE_CHUNKS_IN_HEADER=16`, `STORAGE_CHUNKS_IN_HEADER=4`, `STEM_SUBTREE_WIDTH=256`, `MAIN_STORAGE_OFFSET=256^31`. Merkelization is verbatim: `internal = H(left||right)`, `stem = H(stem||0x00||H(left||right))`, `leaf = H(value)`, `empty = [0x00]*32`, with the collapse rule `H([0x00]*64) = [0x00]*32`. The EIP's own justification: \"Binary tries have been chosen primarily because they reduce the witness size\" — ~768 bytes vs 2,880 hexary at 2^24 elements.\n\n**Verkle is dead for new construction.** Ethereum pivoted to binary trees; IPA is not post-quantum; proving got fast enough to make hash-based trees viable.\n\n**Bound state growth with a refundable storage deposit**, not expiry. I confirmed **EIP-7736 (state expiry) is Stagnant** — `EPOCH_LENGTH=15,778,800s` (~6 months), `NUM_ACTIVE_EPOCHS=2`, `RESURRECT_TX_TYPE` still literally \"TBD\". Resurrection semantics break the \"storage is permanent\" assumption every contract makes. The deposit is 3–5 days of work: assert `balance >= bytes_used * COST_PER_BYTE` post-transaction, revert otherwise.\n\n### Parallelism: correcting the survey\n\nThe first-pass claim that Block-STM \"degrades to worse than sequential under contention\" is **wrong**, and the paper contradicts it. Verified from the Block-STM paper: 110k tps (Diem) / 170k tps (Aptos) at 32 threads, 20x/17x over sequential — and on *contended* workloads it still achieves **50k tps (Diem) and 80k tps (Aptos)**. It degrades to roughly half, not below baseline. The honest case against Block-STM for a small team is not throughput: it is that determinism is *emergent* from the MVMemory/wave protocol rather than structural, which is 6–10 pw plus a long tail of nondeterminism bugs.\n\nAccess lists (Sealevel model) win for a tiny team because the schedule is a pure function of the declared sets, so replay is bit-identical no matter how threads interleave. Verified Solana budget frame: **1,400,000 CU max per transaction, 200,000 CU default per instruction, 3,000 CU for builtins**. Ship the *field* in v1 (unchangeable later), the scheduler in v2. On under-declaration: abort and charge. Never silently widen.\n\n### What to skip, with the receipts\n\n**Sharding** destroys synchronous composability permanently — a product decision, not an engineering one. 9–18 months with a team. Never.\n\n**DAS**: I verified the PeerDAS parameters (EIP-7594 is **Final**): `NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS=128`, `NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS=128`, `SAMPLES_PER_SLOT=8`, `CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT=4`, plus two the survey missed — `VALIDATOR_CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT=8` and `BALANCE_PER_ADDITIONAL_CUSTODY_GROUP=32 ETH`. Reconstruction needs ≥50% of columns. All of it is worthless below thousands of independent samplers. Borrow erasure coding for *propagation*; skip sampling.\n\n**Blobs**: EIP-4844 verified — `FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB=4096`, `GAS_PER_BLOB=2^17`, `TARGET/MAX_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK=393,216/786,432`, `BLOB_BASE_FEE_UPDATE_FRACTION=3,338,477`, point-evaluation precompile at `0x0A` for 50,000 gas. The transferable idea is not KZG: it is *a separate fee market for a separate economic good*. Steal that in v1 with plain hashes. Note EIP-7892 (BPO forks) is **Final/Informational** and its example values (target 10/max 15, then 14/max 21) are explicitly illustrative — do not cite them as shipped Ethereum parameters.\n\n**Consensus**: Narwhal's numbers verified exactly — 130,000 tx/s at <2s for Narwhal-HotStuff vs **1,800 tx/s for bare HotStuff**, 600k with more workers, Tusk 160k at ~3s. The 70x came from separating dissemination from ordering, and you capture most of it in ~1 pw by proposing batch digests. Avalanche defaults verified: **k=20, α=14, β=20**, with safety explicitly \"probabilistic... up to a safety threshold\" — only viable above ~100 well-distributed validators.\n\n**Light clients**: Altair verified — `MIN_SYNC_COMMITTEE_PARTICIPANTS=1` (the spec enforces no real threshold; *your client must*), `FINALIZED_ROOT_GINDEX=105`, `CURRENT_SYNC_COMMITTEE_GINDEX=54`, `NEXT_SYNC_COMMITTEE_GINDEX=55`. Ship header chain + Merkle proofs in v1.\n\n### Privacy: one decision you cannot retrofit\n\nDesign the **key hierarchy** in v1 even with zero privacy features. ZIP-32 verified, and it is richer than commonly summarized: the spending key is `(ask, nsk, ovk, dk)`; the full viewing key is `(ak, nk, ovk, dk)`; `ivk` derives from the FVK. There are **four capability levels, not three** — the *outgoing* viewing key (ovk) is separate from the incoming one, which is exactly what lets you disclose sends without disclosing spends. Diversified (stealth) addresses come from `dk` via FF1-AES256; in Orchard *all* diversifiers are valid, in Sapling only ~50%. Reserve address-format version bytes now.\n\nIf you build a pool, copy **Orchard** (ZIP-224 verified): note `(addr, v, ρ, φ, rcm)`, with **ρ set to the nullifier of the note spent in the same Action** so the note is self-contained and needs no tree position; `nf = [F_nk(ρ) + φ mod p]·𝒢 + cm` with F instantiated as Poseidon; Sinsemilla for the commitment tree; one Halo 2 proof over Pallas/Vesta with **no SRS**. Reject ring signatures: Monero's own roadmap lists FCMP++ under \"Coming Soon\" — **it has not activated** — because fixed decoy sets are statistically attackable.\n\n**Toolchain**, all version-verified: Noir **v1.0.0-beta.26** (still beta — a real risk for something holding funds), halo2 (`halo2_proofs` + `halo2_gadgets`, Apache/MIT, Rust ≥1.60, rayon-parallel), SP1 **V6 \"Hypercube\"** (LogUp GKR, Zerocheck, Jagged PCS), RISC Zero **3.0**. Hand-written circuits beat zkVMs by 10–100x for a small fixed per-transaction circuit; zkVMs win for one-off proofs of complex computation. Bulletproofs verified: `2·log₂(n)+9` elements, no trusted setup, and \"the marginal time to verify an aggregation of 16 range proofs is about the same as the time to verify 16 ECDSA signatures.\"\n\n**Never build**: FHE (Zama's constraints are severe and verified — `euint256` supports no arithmetic *and no ordered comparisons*; `eaddress` is eq/ne/select only; `div`/`rem` require a **plaintext** RHS or they panic), TEE-as-sole-confidentiality, or a mixer. On mixers the legal record is now settled enough to cite: OFAC sanctioned Tornado Cash 2022-08-08; the Fifth Circuit held on 2024-11-26 that immutable contracts are not sanctionable \"property\"; Treasury delisted on 2025-03-21; Roman Storm was nonetheless convicted in July 2025 on **one of three counts** (unlicensed money transmitting), and Alexey Pertsev was convicted in the Netherlands on 2024-05-14 (5y4m). Delisting the addresses did not clear the developers.\n\n### Traps\n\n1. Flat state and the tree silently diverging — add a debug invariant that rebuilds the root from the flat table, run it in CI on every test block.\n2. Confidential amounts without range proofs — curve arithmetic wraps, and a \"negative\" output mints coins.\n3. Changing the note format post-launch fragments the anonymity set (Sprout→Sapling→Orchard did this twice).\n4. Nullifier set as a list rather than a sorted KV structure.\n5.             "language": "python",
            "code": "# key = storage_type(1B) || tree_position(30B) || sub_index(1B);  stem = first 31 bytes\nHEADER_SUBTREE, CODE_SUBTREE, STORAGE_SUBTREE = 0, 1, 255\nBASIC_DATA_LEAF_KEY, CODE_HASH_LEAF_KEY       = 0, 1\nHEADER_STORAGE_OFFSET, CODE_OFFSET            = 20, 4\nCODE_CHUNKS_IN_HEADER, STORAGE_CHUNKS_IN_HEADER = 16, 4\nMAIN_STORAGE_OFFSET = 256 ** 31\n\ndef tree_key(storage_type, tree_position, sub_index):      # -> 32 bytes\n    return bytes([storage_type]) + tree_position + bytes([sub_index])\n\nZERO32 = b\"\\x00\" * 32\ndef H(x):   # spec says BLAKE3 today, Keccak/Poseidon2 candidates, decision TBD.\n    return ZERO32 if x == b\"\\x00\" * 64 else hash_fn(x)   # collapse rule is load-bearing\n\ndef merkelize(n):\n    if n is EMPTY:          return ZERO32                       # empty_node_hash\n    if n.kind == \"leaf\":    return H(n.value)                   # 32-byte value\n    if n.kind == \"internal\":return H(merkelize(n.left) + merkelize(n.right))\n    if n.kind == \"stem\":    # n.stem is the 31-byte key prefix, NOT 30\n        return H(n.stem + b\"\\x00\" + H(merkelize(n.left) + merkelize(n.right)))\n\n# whole account header in ONE leaf at sub_index 0 -> one branch touched, not four\ndef basic_data(version, code_size, nonce, balance):   # 1+4+3+8+16 = 32 bytes exactly\n    return (bytes([version]) + b\"\\x00\" * 4 + code_size.to_bytes(3, \"big\")\n            + nonce.to_bytes(8, \"big\") + balance.to_bytes(16, \"big\"))"

            "code": "// The schedule is a PURE FUNCTION of the declared sets, so a replaying node cannot\n// diverge however its threads interleave. That property -- not speed -- is why a tiny\n// team ships this instead of Block-STM.\nstruct Batch { txs: Vec<usize>, reads: HashSet<Key>, writes: HashSet<Key> }\n\nfn schedule(txs: &[Tx], lanes: usize) -> Vec<Batch> {\n    let mut batches: Vec<Batch> = Vec::new();\n    'next: for (i, tx) in txs.iter().enumerate() {\n        for b in batches.iter_mut() {                 // scan oldest-first: preserves order\n            let ok = tx.writes.is_disjoint(&b.reads)\n                  && tx.writes.is_disjoint(&b.writes)\n                  && tx.reads.is_disjoint(&b.writes);\n            if ok && b.txs.len() < lanes {\n                b.txs.push(i);\n                b.reads.extend(tx.reads.iter().cloned());\n                b.writes.extend(tx.writes.iter().cloned());\n                continue 'next;\n            }\n            if !ok { break; }   // conflicts: may not be reordered past this batch\n        }\n        batches.push(Batch { txs: vec![i], reads: tx.reads.clone(),\n                             writes: tx.writes.clone() });\n    }\n    batches\n}\n// Under-declaration => abort and charge full gas. NEVER silently widen the set:\n// that reintroduces precisely the nondeterminism access lists exist to remove."

ACROSS all actions: a binding signature over sum(cv_net) proves\n//    inputs - outputs - fee == 0. Leading-zero counting gives you 2× jumps in difficulty and nothing in between, which makes smooth retargeting impossible. Use Bitcoin's nBits compact encoding and clamp each retarget to 4× in either direction so a hashrate spike or collapse cannot strand your chain.",

Minting is costless, so nothing-at-stake means a rational validator builds on every fork and forks never resolve; and long-range attacks let holders of old, now-worthless keys rewrite history from genesis. Real PoS needs slashing plus weak-subjectivity checkpoints. Read it for orientation, then overwrite the model immediately with the CometBFT/Tendermint spec.",

It specifies Ethereum through Shanghai (block 17,034,870, April 2023) and its README explicitly says it lacks Cancun and directs readers to the Python execution-layer spec. Building against it in 2026 means missing blobs and several forks of changes.",

Writing it is the point; running it in production is a catastrophe — constant-time behaviour, nonce generation (RFC 6979), and side-channel resistance are all specialist work. A chain becomes production-ready through years of adversarial testing, audits, and incident response — Bitcoin Core is at release 31.1 and reth reached v1.0 only after a Sigma Prime audit. Treat that phrase in a tutorial title as a negative reliability signal.",

        "key": "legal-compliance",
        "title": "Legal, regulatory and tax reality of launching a cryptocurrency",
        "confidence": "medium",
        "brief": "> **This is informative research, not legal advice.** I am not a lawyer or a chartered accountant, and no professional relationship exists. Section numbers, rates and dates below are a starting point for a conversation with Indian tax counsel and a CA — and, if you touch other markets, local counsel there. Items I verified against primary text are marked ✓; items I could not reach this session are flagged.\n\n## The model that actually predicts your exposure\n\nYour legal risk is a function of three switches, not of your consensus algorithm.\n\n| Switch | Flips when | What it turns on |\n|---|---|---|\n| **1. A transferable unit of value exists** | genesis block with a real token | India's VDA definition (s.2(47A)); MiCA Title II; recipient-side tax |\n| **2. You take consideration for it** | sale, pre-sale, SAFT, \"allocation\" for USDT | Howey prong 1; the PMLA notified limb on an *issuer's offer and sale*; s.194S TDS falling on your buyer; a FEMA problem with no clean route |\n| **3. You accept and transmit others' value** | custody, bridge, hosted relayer, fee-on-flow | 31 CFR 1010.100(ff)(5) money transmitter ✓; 18 U.S.C. §1960 ✓; FATF R.16 Travel Rule; state MTLs / BitLicense |\n\nSwitch 1 is cheap. **Switch 2 is expensive and entirely optional. Switch 3 is the criminal-exposure one.**\n\n**Recommendation: leave 2 and 3 off.** Ship a mainnet gas token distributed only as validator/block rewards plus a genuinely free claim. Fund development with equity or a SAFE into a company — never a token sale. That single decision keeps you outside MiCA's white-paper duty, Howey's first prong, and the PMLA limb that would otherwise force FIU-IND registration, all at once.\n\n## India\n\n### Tax — verified verbatim from the statute ✓\n\nSection 115BBH, Income-tax Act 1961 (inserted by Finance Act 2022, effective AY 2023-24):\n\n- **(1)(a)** tax on income from transfer of a VDA **\"at the rate of thirty per cent\"**\n- **(2)(a)** **\"no deduction in respect of any expenditure (other than cost of acquisition, if any) or allowance or set off of any loss shall be allowed\"**\n- **(2)(b)** VDA loss **\"shall not be set off against income computed under any provision of this Act\"** and **\"shall not be allowed to be carried forward to succeeding assessment years\"**\n- **(3)** applies whether the VDA is a capital asset or not\n\nTwo consequences bite builders specifically. **No netting, even within crypto**: +₹10L on token A and −₹10L on token B in the same year means tax on ₹10L at 30% + 4% cess despite zero economic gain. **Mined/self-created coins carry effectively nil cost of acquisition**, so ~30% applies to essentially the whole disposal — and gas, servers, audits and legal fees are all explicitly non-deductible. Your contemporaneous receipt log is the *only* lever you have, and it can only be built as it happens (sketch 1).\n\n| Provision | Rule | Numbers |\n|---|---|---|\n| s.115BBH | Flat tax on VDA transfer | 30% + 4% cess + surcharge; no set-off; no carry-forward |\n| s.194S | 1% TDS deducted by the **buyer** | ₹50,000/yr (specified person) or ₹10,000/yr; 20% if seller has no PAN; Form 26QE / 26Q |\n| s.56(2)(x) | Free receipt = Income from Other Sources | slab rates where aggregate FMV > ₹50,000/yr; valued per Rule 11UA |\n| Schedule VDA / Schedule FA | ITR disclosure | Schedule FA omissions carry Black Money Act penalties independent of the tax |\n\nThe s.194S mechanic is a decisive practical argument against any retail sale into India: **the buyer is the deductor**, and you cannot lawfully perform their obligation for them.\n\n### AML — a precision correction to the survey ✓\n\nI read PMLA s.2(1)(sa) directly. Its own clauses cover casinos, Inspectors-General of Registration, real-estate agents, dealers in precious metals/stones/high-value goods, safekeeping of cash and liquid securities, and clause (vi): *\"such other activities as the Central Government may, by notification, so designate.\"* **The VDA activities are not in the statute text** — they arrive through a notification under clause (vi) (S.O. 1072(E), March 2023). That matters because a notification can be amended far faster than an Act.\n\nFIU-IND publishes \"Registration of Virtual Digital Asset Service Providers in FIU-IND as Reporting Entity\" (notice dated 04-07-2023) ✓, with registration through **FINGate (fingate.gov.in)** ✓. The notified limb that catches token launchers is *participation in and provision of financial services related to an issuer's offer and sale of a VDA* — which is exactly switch 2. Registration is not a badge: it assumes continuing obligations (full-time India-based Principal Officer, board-level Designated Director, audited financials, independent infosec audit) that a solo team structurally cannot staff. **Get a written opinion on scope; do not register pre-emptively.**\n\n### Structure — the most expensive available mistake\n\nPOEM (s.6(3)) plus the FEMA Overseas Investment Rules 2022 mean \"just open a Cayman foundation\" while you live and code in India creates two live exposures at once: the offshore entity can be assessed as an Indian tax resident (~40% + surcharge on worldwide income, defeating the structure), and the incorporation is itself an overseas investment requiring AD-bank routing. **Both must be cleared before incorporating, not after.** This is the single highest-value question to take to counsel.\n\n**Gap flag:** the Income-tax Act 2025 renumbering (194S→393, 285BAA→509, penalty at 446) could not be verified — incometaxindia.gov.in returns 403 to automated fetches. I *did* verify that the original Income-tax Bill 2025 was **withdrawn on 8 August 2025** ✓ and replaced by the No. 2 Bill, which the survey omitted. Confirm live section numbers with your CA before citing them anywhere.\n\n## European Union — MiCA ✓\n\nArticle 4(2) exempts an offer of a crypto-asset (other than an ART/EMT) from the white-paper duty where it is **offered for free**, or **automatically created as a reward for maintaining the distributed ledger / validating transactions**, or is a limited-network utility token for goods/services that already exist, or is offered to **fewer than 150 persons per Member State**, or solely to qualified investors, or where total consideration is **≤ €1,000,000 over 12 months**.\n\n**Article 4(3) is the trap**: the exemption ceases once \"the offeror, or another person acting on the offeror's behalf, communicates the offeror's intention of seeking admission to trading or the exempted crypto-assets are admitted to trading.\" One \"listing soon\" tweet from one team member retroactively exposes an offer you believed exempt. Write this into a comms policy.\n\nA free block-reward token sits squarely inside 4(2)(a) by construction. Still write the document in **Article 6** format (issuer, project, rights and obligations, underlying technology, risks — \"fair, clear and not misleading\"): it costs nothing and every serious exchange asks for exactly that. Article 143(3) transitional cover for CASPs ran to **1 July 2026**, with a Member State option to shorten ✓ — there is no grandfathering left. Article 61 reverse solicitation (\"own exclusive initiative\") is a transaction-by-transaction carve-out, not a business model.\n\n*Note:* the fetch summariser inverted MiCA's Article 149 phasing twice. Correct position: Titles III and IV (ARTs/EMTs) from **30 June 2024**; the remainder, including CASP authorisation, from **30 December 2024**.\n\n## United States ✓\n\n**Are you a money transmitter?** 31 CFR 1010.100(ff)(5)(i)(A) verbatim: *\"money transmission services means the acceptance of currency, funds, or other value that substitutes for currency from one person and the transmission of… to another location or person by any means.\"* The decisive exemption at (ff)(5)(ii)(A): a person who *\"provides the delivery, communication, or network access services used by a money transmitter to support money transmission services.\"* Publishing node and non-custodial wallet software sits inside that exemption. A hosted relayer, a bridge you can pause and drain, or a fee taken out of a flow you route does not.\n\n**Why the line is criminal, not civil.** 18 U.S.C. §1960 ✓: knowingly conducting an unlicensed money transmitting business — **5 years**. Critically, §1960(b)(1)(A) applies *\"whether or not the defendant knew that the operation was required to be licensed.\"* Ignorance of the licensing requirement is not a defence. That is the statute behind the Tornado Cash prosecution.\n\n**Securities.** Howey still governs. The SEC's **\"Regulation Crypto Assets\" is a proposed rule only** ✓ — Federal Register 21 August 2026 (doc 2026-17183; Release Nos. 33-11434 / 34-106150; File S7-2026-27; RIN 3235-AN38), **comments close 20 October 2026**, 146 FR pages. It would add 17 CFR Part 228 with Rule 200 (startup exemption, **$5 million over a four-year period**), Rules 300–307 (fundraising exemption, **$75 million per 12-month period**, Reg A-style with ongoing reporting), **Rule 400** — an investment-contract safe harbour under which an asset *\"would be deemed… not to be subject to an investment contract\"* — and new Forms 1-CRYPTO, 1-KC, 1-SC, 1-UC, **Form TR** (17 CFR 239.600–605) and Form NOR. **You cannot rely on any of it today.**\n\n**Legislation.** The CLARITY Act (H.R. 3633) was received in the Senate on 18 September 2025 and **is not law** ✓; it would define \"digital commodity\", \"mature blockchain system\" (\"not controlled by any person or group of persons under common control\") and \"investment contract asset\". The **GENIUS Act IS law** ✓ — Public Law 119-27, S.1582, approved **18 July 2025**: ≥1:1 reserves in cash/short Treasuries, and a flat ban on paying *\"any form of interest or yield… solely in connection with the holding, use, or retention\"* of a payment stablecoin. Its prohibition on offering non-compliant stablecoins takes effect **three years after enactment — 18 July 2028** ✓. A stablecoin is a licensed-institution project, not a solo build.\n\n## Build order\n\n**Phase 0 (empty directory).** Apache-2.0 (express patent grant + retaliation clause, unlike MIT), SPDX headers, NOTICE, DISCLAIMER.md. Commit a written answer to: *\"will consideration ever be taken for this token?\"* Take no money for tokens — ever.\n\n**Phase 1 (testnet).** Faucet page states test tokens have no monetary value, are not offered for sale, and may be reset — this is what keeps them outside s.2(47A)'s \"representation of having inherent value\". Ship geoblocking with the *first* deployed page (sketch 3). Publish ToS + Privacy Policy (DPDP Act 2023 applies — a faucet logging IPs and wallet addresses processes personal data). Start the committed address ledger.\n\n**Phase 2 (mainnet).** Pure gas/fee token, consumed on use, no governance function, no founder treasury allocation; supply schedule encoded in consensus so no key you hold can change it. Get two written opinions *before* genesis: from a CA on receipt-vs-transfer taxation of block rewards, and from a lawyer on PMLA s.2(1)(sa) scope. Build the receipt log into the node (sketch 1). Claim-on-demand, no deadline, signature-only (sketch 2).\n\n**Phase 3 (market price exists).** Advance-tax instalments — budget cash for tax on gross. Schedule VDA *and* Schedule FA. Assemble the listing pack: classification opinions per jurisdiction, KYB + UBO chart, third-party audit, vesting/unlock schedule with circulating-supply attestation, proof no key can mint, MiCA-format white paper.\n\n## Traps\n\n- **The \"utility token\" label protects nothing.** Howey looks at the transaction and the promises; MiCA 4(2)(b) exempts only access to a good or service that *already exists*.\n- **Announcing a listing** kills your MiCA 4(2) exemption retroactively (Art. 4(3)).\n- **Drifting across the operator line.** A gas-sponsoring relayer is arguably accepting and transmitting value; add a fee and the argument gets much harder.\n- **Assuming OFAC doesn't reach an Indian dev.** It reaches through US persons, USD, and US infrastructure — your AWS region, GitHub, npm, Cloudflare.\n- **Airdropping to Indian users without warning them**, and without giving them a claim-event CSV: under 115BBH(2)(a) the s.56(2)(x) amount is the *only* cost base they will ever have.\n- **DAO branding with no wrapper.** An unincorporated group pursuing a common purpose looks like a general partnership — unlimited joint and several liability, plausibly including passive voters.\n- **Citing dead section numbers** post-1 April 2026 (see gap flag above).\n- **GST**: paying a foreign auditor or infra provider is import of services, ~18% IGST under reverse charge, even with no token sale.\n\n## Must go to a qualified professional\n\nPOEM/FEMA clearance before any offshore incorporation; the PMLA s.2(1)(sa) scope opinion; the receipt-vs-transfer position on block rewards (in writing, before mainnet); GST on VDA supply and reverse charge; and per-jurisdiction token classification opinions before any listing.",

            "label": "Node-side receipt ledger — the only cost basis s.115BBH(2)(a) will ever let you deduct",
            "language": "go",
            "code": "// Every credit to an address we control is BOTH a potential s.56(2)(x) receipt\n// AND the only \"cost of acquisition\" deductible on later disposal. s.115BBH(2)(a)\n// disallows gas, servers, audit and legal fees. Build this before genesis.\ntype Receipt struct {\n\tHeight    uint64    `json:\"height\"`\n\tTime      time.Time `json:\"time\"`          // UTC, RFC3339\n\tTxID      string    `json:\"txid\"`\n\tAddress   string    `json:\"address\"`\n\tUnits     *big.Int  `json:\"units\"`         // base units — never float64\n\tKind      string    `json:\"kind\"`          // block_reward|fee|claim|transfer_in\n\tINRPerTok string    `json:\"inr_per_token\"` // decimal string, not float\n\tPriceSrc  string    `json:\"price_source\"`  // ONE named source, used consistently\n}\n\nfunc (l *Ledger) Record(r Receipt) error {\n\t// Refuse silently-untaxable receipts: a row without a valuation is a row\n\t// that gives you zero cost base and 30% on gross at disposal.\n\tif r.INRPerTok == \"\" || r.PriceSrc == \"\" {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"receipt %s at height %d: missing INR valuation\", r.TxID, r.Height)\n\t}\n\tline, err := json.Marshal(r)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\tif _, err := l.f.Write(append(line, '\\n')); err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\treturn l.f.Sync() // append-only + fsync: this file is tax evidence\n}"

          {
            "label": "Free-claim gate that preserves MiCA Art. 4(2)(a) and fails Howey prong 1 by construction",
            "language": "solidity",
            "code": "// Non-payable by design. Accepting ANY consideration converts a gratuitous\n// distribution into an issuer's \"offer and sale\" (PMLA s.2(1)(sa) notified limb)\n// and destroys the MiCA Art. 4(2)(a) \"offered for free\" exemption.\ncontract FreeClaim {\n    bytes32 public immutable root;\n    IERC20  public immutable token;\n    mapping(address => bool) public claimed;\n\n    // Timestamp is the recipient's s.56(2)(x) receipt date — they choose it,\n    // not us. NO deadline: a deadline forces their tax event onto our schedule.\n    event Claimed(address indexed who, uint256 amount, uint256 at);\n\n    error AlreadyClaimed();\n    error BadProof();\n\n    // No msg.value (non-payable), no fee, no referral, no KYC, no email,\n    // no personal data. Gate is proof-of-address-control and nothing more.\n    function claim(uint256 amount, bytes32[] calldata proof) external {\n        if (claimed[msg.sender]) revert AlreadyClaimed();\n        bytes32 leaf = keccak256(bytes.concat(keccak256(abi.encode(msg.sender, amount))));\n        if (!MerkleProof.verifyCalldata(proof, root, leaf)) revert BadProof();\n        claimed[msg.sender] = true;\n        emit Claimed(msg.sender, amount, block.timestamp);\n        SafeERC20.safeTransfer(token, msg.sender, amount);\n    }\n}"

Sanctions are strict\n// liability; the log is your only evidence you ever tried. ~20 lines, day one.\nconst BLOCKED_COUNTRIES = new Set([\"CU\", \"IR\", \"KP\", \"SY\"]);\nconst BLOCKED_UA_REGIONS = new Set([\"43\", \"14\", \"09\"]); // Crimea, Donetsk, Luhansk\n\nexport default {\n  async fetch(req, env, ctx) {\n    const cf = req.cf ?? {};\n    const country = cf.country ?? \"XX\";\n    const region = cf.regionCode ?? \"\";\n    const deny =\n      BLOCKED_COUNTRIES.has(country) ||\n      (country === \"UA\" && BLOCKED_UA_REGIONS.has(region));\n\n    // Log ALLOW and DENY both: \"we screened everyone\" is the defensible claim.\n    ctx.waitUntil(env.BLOCKLOG.writeDataPoint({\n      blobs: [country, region, new URL(req.url).pathname, deny ? \"deny\" : \"allow\"],\n      indexes: [country],\n    }));\n\n    if (deny) {\n      return new Response(\"Not available in your jurisdiction.\", {\n        status: 451, // Unavailable For Legal Reasons — say it out loud\n        headers: { \"cache-control\": \"no-store\" },\n      });\n    }\n    return fetch(req);\n  },\n};"

        "brief": "## From devnet to mainnet: launch, community and running cost\n\n### The honest prior, corrected\n\nI re-fetched DefiLlama's chain API (`https://api.llama.fi/v2/chains`) on 2026-08-30. It now tracks **716 chains**: **198 below $1M TVL, 89 below $100k, and 104 sitting at exactly zero or null**. Ethereum holds ~$48.9B, roughly **42% of all measured TVL** — the survey's \"~87%\" figure is wrong and I am correcting it. The shape of the conclusion survives the correction: about one chain in seven that exists has meaningful economic activity, and roughly one in seven is measurably dead.\n\nChains rarely die loudly. The common failure is a chain that runs for three years at a few hundred dollars a month with four validators and no users. That is worse than stopping, because it consumes the years you would have spent on the next thing. Write kill criteria at T-24 weeks and read them at T+26.\n\n### Decision 1: do not launch an L1 (recommendation)\n\nUnless your differentiator *is* consensus or execution, ship an OP Stack L2 or a Cosmos SDK appchain instead. The OP Stack tutorial (docs.optimism.io) pins **Go ^1.26, Node ^20, pnpm ^8, Foundry ^0.2.0, Docker ^24**, runs **op-reth + op-node + op-batcher + op-proposer + op-challenger**, is driven by `make init` / `make setup` / `make up` around `op-deployer`, and needs **~2-3 ETH on Sepolia** to stand up a testnet. That path deletes validator recruitment, the genesis ceremony, and bridge design from your critical path. The L1 path adds four full-time problems (validator set, security budget, bespoke bridge, 24/7 consensus on-call) on top of the thing you actually wanted to build.\n\n### Decision 2: licence — Apache-2.0 for the node, never BUSL\n\nVerified from source: **Cosmos SDK is Apache-2.0** (repo `LICENSE`). **Uniswap v3-core's BUSL-1.1 header** names Licensor Uniswap Labs, Additional Use Grant `v3-core-license-grants.uniswap.eth`, Change Date \"the earlier of 2023-04-01 or a date specified at v3-core-license-date.uniswap.eth\", Change License **GPL-2.0-or-later** — so v3-core is *already* GPL today. **Uniswap v2-core is GPL-3.0**, not permissive; the survey implied otherwise. Correct that before you plan a DEX fork: both Uniswap generations are copyleft, so your fork must ship source.\n\nSPDX's BUSL-1.1 text caps the Change Date at \"the fourth anniversary of the first publicly available distribution of a specific version\" and requires the Change License be \"GPL Version 2.0 or any later version, or a license that is compatible with\" it. BUSL on node software is a category error: the moat expires in four years, and meanwhile no exchange, RPC provider or institutional validator wants a licence question in their infra review.\n\n### Decision 3: genesis ceremony, verified command-for-command\n\nFrom the Cosmos SDK `x/genutil` README: the flow is `simd genesis add-genesis-account` → `simd genesis gentx [key_name] [amount] --chain-id [chain-id]` → `simd genesis collect-gentxs` → `simd genesis validate-genesis`. The gentx amount must be **at least `1000000000stake`** or the command errors. Run a public gentx ceremony with a 5-day window, then publish `genesis.json` **with its SHA-256** and require every operator to echo their own `sha256sum` in the operator channel. Set `genesis_time` at least 48 hours out.\n\nThe unrecoverable trap: never publish a second hash. Accepting one late gentx and re-running `collect-gentxs` puts two hashes in circulation and forks you at height 1. Once the hash is out, the window is closed — launch without that validator.\n\n### Decision 4: joinability (the silent killer), verified keys\n\nI read CometBFT's config template directly (`config/toml.go`). The `[statesync]` keys are exactly: `enable`, `rpc_servers`, `trust_height`, `trust_hash`, `trust_period`, `discovery_time`, `temp_dir`, `chunk_request_timeout`, `chunk_fetchers`. `[p2p]` carries `seeds`, `persistent_peers`, `seed_mode`. On the app side (`confix` v0.50 app.toml), `[state-sync]` has `snapshot-interval = 0` (0 disables) and `snapshot-keep-recent = 2`; pruning defaults are `pruning = \"default\"`, `min-retain-blocks = 0`. **The default disables snapshots** — you must set `snapshot-interval` explicitly or your chain serves no state-sync at all.\n\nThis failure is invisible. The chain keeps producing blocks, your dashboards stay green, and every prospective validator quietly gives up during genesis replay. `trust_height`/`trust_hash` go stale with no alert. Test a cold-machine join from your own published instructions **weekly**.\n\n### Real monthly cost, from list prices fetched 2026-08-30\n\n| Item | SKU (verified price) | $/mo |\n|---|---|---|\n| 2× seed node | DigitalOcean 4GB/2vCPU @ $24 | 48 |\n| 2× public RPC full node | OVH RISE-S @ $77 (8c/16t, 64GB DDR5 ECC, 2×512GB NVMe) | 154 |\n| 1× archive node | OVH RISE-1 @ $64 (6c/12t, up to 4×3.84TB NVMe) | 64 |\n| Explorer + Postgres | OVH RISE-S @ $77 | 77 |\n| Indexer | OVH RISE-1 @ $64 | 64 |\n| Faucet | DigitalOcean 1GB/1vCPU @ $6 | 6 |\n| Snapshot storage, 500GB | DO @ $0.06/GB-mo | 30 |\n| Monitoring | Grafana Cloud free (10k series, 50GB logs, 50GB traces, 14d, 3 users) | 0 |\n| CDN + docs + domain | Cloudflare free + domain | ~5 |\n| Off-site backup | — | ~15 |\n| **Lean floor** | | **≈ $465** |\n\nRedundant two-region tier (4× RPC, 2× archive, 4 seeds, managed explorer DB, 2TB snapshots, Grafana Cloud Pro at $19 base + $6.50/1k series over 10k, paging): **≈ $1,300-1,600/mo**. One-time: OVH charges a setup fee equal to one month on RISE-S ($77 each); RISE-1 is free installation.\n\n**The RPC trap is not negotiable.** QuickNode's tiers ($49 Build / $249 Accelerate / $499 Scale / $999 Business / $1,499-$2,999 Business+) and Alchemy's PAYG ($0.45/1M CU for the first 300M, then $0.40/1M CU; 30M CU free) both say \"all *supported* chains\". Your brand-new chain is not one. Public RPC for a new chain is self-hosted infrastructure you own; getting carried is enterprise BD, not a signup.\n\n**Explorer DB is bigger than your node.** Blockscout's own sizing (measured 2024-12-23) is **21,000 GiB for Ethereum mainnet, 21,000 GiB for Gnosis, 5,200 GiB for Sepolia, 555 GiB for Ethereum Classic** — and note *Sepolia*, a testnet, needs 5.2TB. Blockscout recommends **16 core / 32 thread, 128GB RAM**; on AWS, `m5a.xlarge` app + `db.t3.large` Postgres 14+ with 500GB gp3. Their docs warn `db_storage` \"can only be adjusted 1 time in a 24 hour period on AWS\" — a launch-week underestimate locks you out for a day.\n\n### Validator hardware is an economic parameter\n\n| Reference | Storage | RAM | CPU | Bandwidth |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| EIP-7870 full node | 4TB NVMe | 32GB | 4c/8t (~1000 ST / 3000 MT PassMark) | 50↓/15↑ Mbps |\n| EIP-7870 attester | 4TB NVMe | 64GB | 8c/16t (~3500 ST / 25000 MT) | 50↓/25↑ Mbps |\n| EIP-7870 local builder | 4TB NVMe | 64GB | 8c/16t | 100↓/50↑ Mbps |\n| Reth (Ethereum) | 1.2TB full / 2.8TB archive, TLC NVMe | 8GB full, 16GB+ archive | high clock > core count | 24Mbps+ |\n| Reth (Base) | 2TB full / 4.1TB archive | **128GB+** | 6 cores+ | 24Mbps+ |\n| Solana (Agave) | 3 separate NVMe: 1TB accounts, 1TB ledger, 500GB snapshots | 256GB validator / 512GB RPC w/ indexes | 2.8GHz+, SHA ext, AVX2, AMD Gen3 / Intel Ice Lake+ | 2 Gbit/s symmetric staked, 10 Gbit/s recommended |\n\nSolana additionally charges validators **up to 1.1 SOL/day** in vote transactions. That is a hard rent only a well-capitalised operator carries. Pick which end of this table you want *before* you pick your block time, because block time is the multiplier that decides it.\n\n### Ecosystem gates: what each integration actually costs you\n\n| Integration | What it actually requires | Lead time |\n|---|---|---|\n| EIP-155 chainId | PR to `ethereum-lists/chains`, file `_data/chains/eip155-<id>.json`, unique `name`+`shortName`, icon <250kb on IPFS, validate `./gradlew run`, `npx prettier --write` | **Claim at T-24.** \"The first pull request gets the chainID assigned\"; replacement PRs \"will be closed\" |\n| Safe | Deploy singletons via Safe Singleton Factory, then `pnpm update-registry --version v1.5.0 --chainId <ID> --deploymentType canonical`, `pnpm lint:fix`, `pnpm test` | \"Merged PRs are batched into a **monthly** npm release\" (not two-weekly — survey corrected) |\n| Pyth (pull oracle) | Deploy receiver contract; \"contact the team if your chain isn't in the upgrade list\". 19 upgraded + 65 legacy EVM mainnets | Days-weeks |\n| Chainlink (push) | Docs route you to \"contact us to talk to an expert\" — a commercial negotiation plus a subsidy for node operators | Months |\n| LayerZero V2 | EndpointV2, SendUln302, ReceiveUln302, LZ Executor; EIDs are 30xxx mainnet / 40xxx testnet, unrelated to chainId; configure DVNs explicitly | Months |\n| Native USDC | Circle's **Bridged USDC Standard \"must be incorporated prior to deploying a bridged USDC token contract as it cannot be retroactively applied.\"** Upgrade to native is discretionary — \"Circle is obligated to upgrade bridged USDC to native USDC? No\" | Deploy correctly on day one or lose the option permanently |\n\n**Never write your own bridge.** rekt.news' leaderboard (fetched) still puts four bridges in the top seven: Ronin $624M, Poly Network $611M, BNB Bridge $586M, Wormhole $326M. Wormhole itself runs a 19-member Guardian set with a 13-of-19 supermajority and cites 29 third-party audits — that is the resourcing level of the *hacked* systems.\n\n### Org side and security posture\n\nShip `SECURITY.md` before the repo goes public.             "label": "Genesis ceremony: validate every gentx, collect, then publish the hash that operators verify",
            "language": "bash",
            "code": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\nset -euo pipefail\nCHAIN_ID=\"mychain-1\"; MIN_STAKE=1000000000   # x/genutil: gentx must be >= 1000000000stake\nGENESIS=\"$HOME/.simapp/config/genesis.json\"\n\n# 1. Reject bad gentxs BEFORE they enter the merge set.\nfor f in gentx/*.json; do\n  amt=$(jq -r '.body.messages[0].value.amount' \"$f\")\n  den=$(jq -r '.body.messages[0].value.denom'  \"$f\")\n  moniker=$(jq -r '.body.messages[0].description.moniker' \"$f\")\n  [[ \"$den\" == \"stake\" ]]        || { echo \"REJECT $f: denom $den\"; exit 1; }\n  (( amt >= MIN_STAKE ))         || { echo \"REJECT $f: $amt < $MIN_STAKE\"; exit 1; }\n  grep -qx \"$moniker\" monikers.txt && { echo \"REJECT $f: dup moniker\"; exit 1; }\n  echo \"$moniker\" >> monikers.txt\ndone\n\n# 2. Merge and validate. collect-gentxs reads ~/.simapp/config/gentx/.\ncp gentx/*.json \"$HOME/.simapp/config/gentx/\"\nsimd genesis collect-gentxs\nsimd genesis validate-genesis \"$GENESIS\"\n\n# 3. Freeze genesis_time >= 48h out, then publish ONE hash. Never publish a second.\njq --arg t \"$(date -u -d '+48 hours' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.000000000Z)\" \\\n   '.genesis_time = $t | .chain_id = \"'\"$CHAIN_ID\"'\"' \"$GENESIS\" > genesis.final.json\nsha256sum genesis.final.json | tee GENESIS_SHA256\necho 'Operators: run sha256sum genesis.json and post output in #operators before starting.'"
          },

            "label": "The two config blocks that decide whether anyone can ever join your chain",
            "language": "toml",
            "code": "# ---- config.toml (CometBFT) — keys verified against cometbft/config/toml.go ----\n[p2p]\n# Seeds crawl and disconnect; persistent_peers stay connected. Use BOTH,\n# and place seeds in >=2 providers on >=2 continents or the chain becomes\n# unjoinable while still producing blocks (green dashboards, zero new nodes).\nseeds = \"id1@seed-eu.example:26656,id2@seed-us.example:26656\"\npersistent_peers = \"id3@rpc-eu.example:26656,id4@rpc-us.example:26656\"\nseed_mode = false                 # true ONLY on the dedicated seed hosts\n\n[statesync]\nenable = true\nrpc_servers = \"https://rpc-eu.example:443,https://rpc-us.example:443\"  # needs >=2\ntrust_height = 1250000            # regenerate weekly via cron — these go\ntrust_hash   = \"A1B2...\"          # stale silently and no alert will fire\ntrust_period = \"168h0m0s\"         # < unbonding period\nchunk_fetchers = \"4\"\n\n# ---- app.toml (Cosmos SDK) — defaults from confix v0.50-app.toml ----\n[state-sync]\n# DEFAULT IS 0 = DISABLED. If you leave this, your RPC nodes serve NO snapshots\n# and every joiner must replay from genesis forever. This is the #1 silent death.\nsnapshot-interval = 1000          # blocks between ABCI state snapshots\nsnapshot-keep-recent = 2          # SDK default\n\npruning = \"custom\"                # default \"default\"; archive node uses \"nothing\"\npruning-keep-recent = \"100\"\npruning-interval = \"10\""
